entityDescription:
Expertise with a past and a future.

The company Bertrandt was founded in 1974 as a one-man engineering office in Baden-Württemberg. Innovative services and expert competence in the mobile world made Bertrandt a guarantee for customer-specific solutions. Today, the Group is one of the world’s leading engineering companies. Our customers value us because we combine customer focus, partnership and responsibility with extensive experience in the leading and internationally relevant technology sectors.

The optimum solution for every customer.
Our strength is our close proximity to our customers. Precise knowledge of our customers’ requirements, intensive cooperation and our presence at more than 50 locations worldwide ensure that we honour our promise to provide services with maximum customer benefit. This is also based on our many years of expertise in processes and interfaces and a high level of innovative capability. We are driven by our commitment to constantly think one step ahead, to open up new research and development potentials and to further develop and apply the very latest technologies.

Services along the entire product development process.
An important precondition for developing customer-specific solutions is to have comprehensive know-how. Our range of services is equally extensive. From the initial idea through to a production-ready product, we offer innovative development services as well as adjacent services in quality and project management or logistics solutions. Our employees are fully committed to what Bertrandt stands for: a high level of motivation, outstanding dedication, know-how and loyalty

Sustainable company success. Also in the future.
Solidity is a key component of our business model. Our financial stability makes us a reliable partner for our customers. And it also increases our attractiveness as an employer, with a workforce that has grown to around 13,000 employees in the meantime. As one of the top employers, we are also one of the preferred addresses for applicants. Providing careers for competent engineers who are prepared to give their best.

Elliptika offers several microwave components development based on conventional technologies such as planar technologies (PCB, Alumina), volumic technologies (mechanical machining) or innovative technologies such as additive technologies. We realize the components by 3D printing (filters or antennas) and then we metallized it in a selective or total way. This last service allows us to significantly reduce the weight, the cost and the manufacturing time.
Elliptika relies on microwave know-how in the 300 MHz to 100 GHz frequency bands. We use the most powerful syntheses and modeling software on the market (ADS, Momentum, HFSS and Ansys Designer) to develop the solution that meets the best compromise between electrical performance, size, weight and cost.

entityDescription: BIOEMTECH is a fast-growing Greek SME, which aims to bridge the gap between ex vivo studies and in vivo molecular imaging, by providing cost-effective solutions in terms of instrumentation and services. The company designs and develops low cost molecular imaging systems and provides molecular imaging services. In its short life BIOEMTECH participates in 6 Horizon 2020 projects including (RISE, NMBP, ITN and recently FET). Starting from three founders, BIOEMTECH is now a multidisciplinary team of 15 young scientists with strong background in biomedical engineering, medical physics, radiochemistry, nanomedicine and small animal handling. By interacting with multidisciplinary consortia, BIOEMTECH developed its imaging platform, which allows production and characterization of biomolecules and nanoparticles, functionalization and radiolabelling with radioisotopes, ex vivo biodistribution and in vivo imaging with its microSPECT, microPET and microCT, while it keeps extending its imaging portfolio.

entityName: Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities
entityDescription: Positioned at the top of the research rankings, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities is the largest of the eight state academies in Germany and one of the oldest. It specialises in innovative long-term research, networks scholars across disciplines and national boundaries, engages with politics and civil society, supports young scientists and provides a first-rate forum for dialogue between the scientific community and the general public. The Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities conducts innovative basic research in the humanities and natural sciences through more than 60 different projects. Since it is not tied to any university, it can focus its efforts on long-term research endeavours. This includes work on scholarly dictionaries, important editions and series of exact measurements – all with the aim of preserving our cultural heritage and laying the foundations for further research. Many of the academy’s projects involve international collaboration. New ad-hoc working groups with a much shorter-term research horizon focus on highly topical social and political issues. With the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre and the Walther-Meißner-Institute for Low Temperature Research, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities oversees two further institutes of international renown at the Garching research campus. Meanwhile, the Bavarian Research Institute for Digital Transformation (BIDT) explores the impact of digitalisation on society.

entityDescription:
Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC) is a research center that began its activities in March 2000. The mission of DIPC is to perform and catalyze cutting-edge research in physics and related disciplines, as well as to convey scientific culture to society. DIPC was conceived and designed based on the idea that an advanced society needs advanced scientific research. 

DIPC is unique in its institutional structure. The Center was founded with close ties to the University of the Basque Country UPV/EHU, yet independent from it. DIPC is a Foundation in which both public institutions (Basque Government, Gipuzkoa Provincial Council, San Sebastian City Council, and UPV/EHU) and private companies (currently Kutxa, CAF, Telefónica, and EDP Naturgas Energia) participate and contribute to its funding. 

DIPC is also unique in its way of operating. DIPC is an agile center that runs under a flexible autonomy of government and management. DIPC makes its researchers and their research activity its top priority. DIPC’s recent history proves how the initiative has hit the mark and become a success model.

entityDescription:
ERINHA-ASIBL (European Research Infrastructure on Highly Pathogenic Agents) is a pan-European Research Infrastructure dedicated to the study of High-consequence pathogens of Risk Group 4 (RG4). As a distributed Research infrastructure, it brings together leading European Bio-Safety Level 4 (BSL4) facilities and national research institutes with longstanding experience of research in this field. Such a coordinated approach is vital in a context marked by frequent globalization of infectious diseases with high risk for public health, society and economy.
The over-arching goal of ERINHA’s Infrastructure research concept is to provide capacities to conduct projects which are broad in scope, ambition and require a range of capabilities inside and outside BSL4 facility that no single facility can provide on its own.
The access to the ERINHA is organized through its Central Coordinating Unit, hosted in Paris (101, rue Tolbiac, 75013 Paris, FRANCE).

entityDescription:
How it started
Pikkart was founded in Modena in 2014 by Lorenzo Canali, owner of Progetti di Impresa (Enterprise Projects), among the Italian leaders in software solutions for the Public Health and Welfare Sector and Public Administrations. Lorenzo Canali brought in a group of genius researchers from the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia and created Pikkart with Davide Baltieri and Giovanni Zuffolini as his Partners, with the goal of becoming one of the best companies in the field of Augmented Reality and Artificial Intelligence.

 
Our technology: 2019 - future
Today Pikkart’s research and development efforts go towards Augmented Intelligence (a technology that incorporates the amazing strenght and versatility of Artificial Intelligence and Augmented Reality), and Deep Learning and Computer Vision solutions.

Among these shines Pikkart-AR Discover, Pikkart’s most recent evolution of augmented reality itself, with an addition of visual recognition. To simplify, it’s a software that from just a few pictures can recognize objects and places, and allows to link to them augmented reality content such as info sheets, pictures, videos and 3D models. It’s a solution that has already been successfully applied to the museums sector, in Industry 4.0 and MMR.

Our technology: 2014-2018
Two years after being founded Pikkart became one of the few companies in the world and the first in Italy to have developed from scratches its own proprietary Augmented Reality Ecosystem, which started with Pikkart-AR SDK, an augmented reality software development kit, followed by Pikkart-AR Logo, a software that allows to link up to a billion different pieces of content to as many copies of the same image.

It’s the kind of innovative technology that lead Pikkart to, in just a few years, gaining space and awards both in and outside of Italy (like for example the prestigious Seal of Excellence, gained in the scope of Horizon 2020’s SME Instrument) and creating solutions for a number of national and international organizations, companies, and sports clubs, such as: Ferretti Group, Generali Insurance, IBM, Marposs, Lega Basket Serie A, Pfizer Vaccines, Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna, etc.

entityDescription:
The Enterprise&Climate Foundation (FEC) is a non-profit organization that works for leadership and business commitment in the fight against climate change. Join us in achieving a low carbon global economy

Climate change is a risk to our society and economy, but also an opportunity for innovation, leadership, and business for companies.

Companies are key in this fight and assume more important commitments every day.

From the FEC we help companies to plan and invest in a low carbon economy, promoting mitigation strategies and strengthening their capacity to adapt to the effects of climate change.

The FEC represents companies of all sizes and sectors, leaders and leaders for integrating into their DNA policies that promote climate action.

Our mission is to offer support to all companies so that they have the information and the right tools to face the commitments and challenges that climate change implies.

We are specialized in emissions calculations, capacity development and strategic roadmaps for enterprises in order to implement and execute low carbon best practices inside companies to allow them to reduce dramatically their emissions.

20% of the IBEX 35 companies are members of the FEC. Additionally, there are another 60 partner companies of the foundation.

Our values are transparency, responsibility, and innovation in sustainability practices

entityDescription:
It is in the DNA of MURMURATION to respect the environment, and all of its activities cater to this issue. Indeed, it is MURMURATION's objective to place the environmental dimension at the core of every decision. In order to do so, we have developed a methodology that combines data from Earth observation satellites, such as the Copernicus satellites, with in-situ data and socio-economic statistics, to assess the state of an ecosystem anywhere in the world. Using this capability, we provide information to a wide range of users, including policy makers, decision-makers, and the general public.

An important aspect of our work is to link environmental observations to anthropogenic activities. We have been able to develop several use cases in different domains based on these data. We can mention for example:
● To support the Green Deal initiative and environmental policies with up-to-date scientific data
● Providing public authorities with a decision-making dashboard presenting historical analyses and forecasts of climate change impacts on their territory.
● Climate change mitigation actions through improved management of terrestrial ecosystems..
● Scientific evidence to support climate change mitigation and adaptation actions.
For the development of our services, we use technologies such as remote sensing, data processing, data calibration, and data fusion, image processing algorithms, classification algorithms, and machine learning

It supports local government with finance services for local enterprises and real estate activities, with an overall asset amount of about 1 Billion Euro.

entityDescription:
The University of Craiova is a Romanian public institution of higher education, founded in 1947, functioning ever since, gaining experience and importance every year. Counting around 2,000 staff members and 25,000 students, it is one of the biggest higher education institutions in Romania. 
The university offers a wide field of Bachelor and Master Programs in sciences, polytechnic engineering, agriculture, humanities, social studies, economics, law, theology and arts (33 specializations and 66 diplomas). The University of Craiova organises Ph.D. Programs in over 70 fields. The institution undertakes major responsibilities in scientific research and in widening active and adequate participation to the social life. The scientific events, the promotion of science, culture and education alongside the cultural events organised by the university make it attractive to different age groups. In this respect, ones of its main priorities are related to research on climate changes and to youngster education in environmental protection. Its main contribution is related to: (i) participation in large-scale EU research projects, within FP7 or Horizon 2020, (ii) publication of a large number of monographs and scientific papers in well known national and international journals, (iii) initiation and organisation of numerous scientific events involving the national and international communities of practice. 
The participation of the University of Craiova in the proposed WASTE Project could combine the expertises of various groups of researchers and educators, focusing on the identification of success measures of environmental protection, of employability enhancing factors, of active citizenship, of establishing virtual communities of practice/social connectivity etc.

entityDescription:
Warwickshire Wildlife Trust aims to protect and enhance wildlife, natural habitats and geology throughout Warwickshire, Coventry and Solihull, and to encourage a greater awareness, appreciation and participation in all aspects of nature conservation and the environment.

We are the leading local conservation charity with over 23,000 members dedicated to supporting our vital work for nature conservation across the county. 

Warwickshire Wildlife Trust is working to create a Living Landscape by:
Managing Nature Reserves - with 65 nature reserves spanning 800 hectares across Warwickshire, a large portion of our role is the management of these havens for wildlife and people. Find out more about nature reserves in Warwickshire.

Engaging our communities to enjoy and care for wildlife - We work on projects at the heart of communities to help build positive relationships between people and their natural spaces.

Encouraging and supporting volunteers - we are indebted to the 500 plus volunteers who help us in every aspect of our work from conservation through to administration. This is why we are committed to being as supportive and inclusive to each dedicated individual.

Educating people about nature - We provide educational activities to thousands of children every year as well as guided walks, talks and events for people of all ages.

Campaigning on behalf of the environment - We are there to give a strong local voice in helping to protect threatened places and rare species.

entityDescription: Corallia is an incubator, youth entrepreneurship accelerator, and multi-Cluster facilitator established in 2005 as a Unit of the Athena Research Centre and has played a key role in the development of the Greek startup ecosystem. Corallia is one of the main pillars of the Greek innovation ecosystem and a think-tank that underpins national development plans in Greece. Our team comprises of people possessing a passion and a vision for supporting Greece’s "sciences, innovation, entrepreneurship and culture to flourish" as well as more specific goals to promote a "Joy of Creation" culture and the development of services and products "Innovation Made in Greece”. To achieve our vision, we have developed a wide range of activities focusing on: enhancing and disseminating innovation of all forms in the private and public sector, shaping cutting-edge technology sectors and integrated value chains with a competitive advantage, stimulating links be-tween industry, universities, research centers, public administration and citizens, boosting exports and competitiveness with a specialized extroversion program, creating and maintaining highly skilled jobs and reversing the brain drain, providing information, inspiration and training, particularly on entrepreneurship and high tech, investing in the human capital available to the country and fostering relations with the diaspora and creating integrated support structures for new aspiring entrepreneurs and dynamic businesses with incubator services and business acceleration. Corallia has supported up to date more than 300 innovative enterprises, of all sizes, to grow in Greece and internationally, of which more than 100 new start-ups. More than 10.000 people and organisations have directly benefited from our activities, including would-be-entrepreneurs, startups, SMEs, large corporations, pupils and students, while the indirect beneficiaries exceed 100.000 civilians and organisations.

entityDescription:
attocube is a leading pioneer for nanotechnology solutions in industry and research. The company develops, produces and distributes components and systems for nanoscale applications such as precision motion, cryogenic microscopy, and nanoscale analytics. All products are manufactured in the NanoFactory, the company’s headquarters in Haar, close to Munich. An international team of 150 physicists, engineers, software developers, and product designers work in close collaboration from conception through to delivery. attocube has sales offices in the US and a broad network of worldwide distributors, covering more than 40 countries and 4,000 customers.

The company was founded in 2001 as a spin-off from the CeNS (Center for NanoScience) at Munich’s Ludwig-Maximilian University. Prof. Dr. Khaled Karraï and his PhD student Dirk Haft - two visionaries with exceptional entrepreneurial spirit and courage - developed a nanopositioning device that could function under extreme conditions such as cryogenic temperatures, ultra-high vacuum and magnetic fields.

This idea won them the Munich Business Plan Competition which was the springboard for the future of attocube. What began as a “two-man show” with a large portion of creative playfulness, passion and the input from some experienced advisors continued to grow. The company has since gone on to win further prestigious awards, sustainably broaden its portfolio, and hire additional employees.

Today, attocube is a global player in the field of nanoscale applications, delivering its products not only to world-renowned research institutes, but also serving customers in future industries such as semiconductor and quantum technologies. One thing, however, has remained unchanged until this day: The team has retained its attocube DNA. From the light and transparency of the NanoFactory’s architecture to the bold, passionate and sometimes even unconventional way that attocube employees inhabit their work. To put it simply: the attocube spirit remains.

entityDescription:
Bonseyes Community Association (BCA) is a non-profit AI-focused association based in Switzerland. BCA was created and inspired by the H2020 Bonseyes AI Marketplace project to ensure that artificial intelligence benefits all of society through open, distributed, and decentralised platforms and technology.

BCA’s mission is to ensure that artificial intelligence (in all forms from narrow to general) which will ultimately create highly autonomous systems benefits all of society – not just a select few. We will attempt to directly build open technology platforms supporting distributed artificial intelligence marketplaces empowering innovators, data scientists, and developers to build and trade value creating, safe, and beneficial AI aligned with societal goals. We will also consider our mission fulfilled if our work aids others to achieve this outcome. To that end, the association pursues the following non- commercial goals:

- Increasing knowledge and understanding of the distributed artificial intelligence systems development across government, universities, industry, and startups.
- Development of an open platform technology and infrastructure for a distributed artificial intelligence marketplace.
- Promoting research into decentralised and distributed artificial intelligence.

entityDescription:
S.A.B. Aerospace Srl is a private and independent SME operating in the Space Business since 2004. The company core business is focused in the development of mechanical systems, sub-systems and mechanisms related to Launchers, Satellites and Payloads.

SAB has been and is currently involved in several projects related to launchers through contracts awarded by ELV, ESA and ARIANESPACE for the development of items such as Adapters, Systems for Payload Multiple launch, Separation Systems and Test apparatus for shock testing. SAB is currently responsible (on behalf of Arianespace) for the Shock testing services executed with the VESTA (VEga Shock Test Apparatus) tool on the payloads to be embarked on the VEGA launcher. Moreover SAB has participated to launch campaigns and is familiar with rules implemented by ESA in the launch space port in French Guyana.

Satellite activities performed by SAB Aerospace are linked to the partnership established in 2010 with OHB System AG and they range from Platform Mechanical Design Development to Mechanical Integration of Satellites including as well MGSE Design and Manufacturing.

SAB Aerospace is performing activities for the development of Optical Payloads and Equipments sub-system in terms of Thermo-mechanical Design, Structures manufacturing, Integration and Environmental Testing.

The above mentioned activities are supported by research program developed in cooperation with a network of research centers for the study of technologies such as Laser Welding Technology, Separation System Technologies, Thermal Control Systems, Advanced Ceramics and Light Alloys.

The company headquarter is in Benevento, an area considered one of the Italian poles concerning aeronautical and aerospace business. In the headquarter S.A.B. Aerospace concentrates all the activities related to Manufacturing, Assembly/Integration and Testing. All the engineering and R/D activities are based in the Ancona office, while a third office is in Milan for Business Development and Marketing. The SAB internal facilities comprises: 
- An Integration facility built inside a 100000 class clean room facility and equipped with a 1ton lifting crane for the handling of the different parts and assembled systems. 
- The Vibration test facility is composed by a 49KN electrodynamics shaker mounted in the clean room described above. 
- A four axes milling machines used to manufacture space components made up of Aluminum, Invar and Peek.

In addition SAB can rely on a manufacturer network for manufacturing of complex mechanical structures.

entityDescription: The IOTA Foundation is a not-for-profit organization established in 2017 and headquartered in Berlin, Germany. The Foundation's mission is to drive the development and standardization of new distributed ledger technologies (DLTs) that enable permissionless innovation ecosystems. The IOTA Foundation works to realize this potential by actively building a collaborative ecosystem of developers, start-ups, private enterprises, and government, civil society and academic institutions with the vision to enable responsible and citizen-centric technology innovation. The IOTA Foundation takes a society-first approach to cutting-edge technological innovation. We employ a collaborative philosophy focused on end-user empowerment and social good rather than towards profit. Concretely, we engage in engineering, research and community organizing efforts around the IOTA Tangle – a new generation of DLT specifically designed to be the open and free trust layer for the Internet-of-Things (IoT). Our aim is to make available to the public a universally utilizable distributed ledger protocol that is stable, scalable, fast and free for all to use. The core functionalities of this DLT protocol include secure data transfer, fee-less micropayments, tamper-proof record-keeping, user-controlled data privacy, distributed computing, and real-time data monitoring and reporting processes. The foundation employees over 100 people across the globe in research, technology development and different adoption verticals. It actively fosters a community of developers, funded over 14 open source projects and engages with academia through the IOTA research council.

Company description: agriBORA is an agri-fintech company with a mission to de-risk smallholder agriculture through a balance of technology and human touch. entityDescription:
The University of Sussex (http://www.sussex.ac.uk) is a leading research-intensive university established in 1961. Over 75% of research activity at Sussex is categorised as world leading or internationally excellent in terms of originality, significance and rigour. 

Sussex has an excellent international reputation and is ranked in the top 50 UK universities (The Guardian University League Tables 2020 and The Complete University Guide 2020), and in the top 150 (146th) in the world (Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2020). In 2020 the QS World Rankings by Subject rated Sussex number one in the world for Development Studies and rated high for research output.
The University has a dynamic and thriving research culture with strengths across the sciences, arts, social sciences and medicine with a focus on interdisciplinary research. It currently has around 17,000 students and 4,000 staff from all over the world including over 1,000 teaching and research staff. It has had three Nobel Prize winners, 14 Fellows of the Royal Society, 12 Fellows of the British Academy and a winner of the prestigious Crafoord Prize on its faculty.
In the financial year 2018/2019 the total income was 323 million and the value of the University’s total portfolio of external project research income was 38 million, ranging from commercial funders to charities and public sector organisations (including governmental departments).
The University of Sussex has experience in dealing with all European Research and Innovation programme matters. It has successfully secured 87 H2020 grants to date: 7 FET, 32 ERC, 21 Societal Challenges, 1 Research Infrastructures, 1 Widening Participation and 25 Marie Skłodowska-Curie projects (5 ITNs, 3 RISE projects, and 17 fellowships). Sussex participates in three FET Flagships: the Human Brain Project, the Humane AI and the Quantum Flagship initiatives.

entityDescription:
My studio specializes in visual communication consultancy for companies and in this we assist the customer at 360 °: logo design, corporate identity, catalogs, brochures, layouts, packaging and web design.
I’ve been working as a Graphic Designer for over 20 years, aiming to face every single project by asking: who is the message to be communicated aimed at and how can I reach the end user in the simplest and most immediate way.
In fact, the phrase that represents me is: " For all companies who want to keep up with the pace of the world, but attract the gaze of those watching". To achieve this in a society full of visual inputs, it is necessary to strike immediately to be recognized with a few well-directed messages.
Creativity is being able to attract attention through the visual message and make people stop, even just for a moment. It’s being remembered!
 
The media we can use nowadays are infinite, but for me "Paper", with its thousand different nuances and appeal to the senses, is still the most effective way: touch, with the use of various embossings, thicknesses or materials; sight, with the various printing technologies; hearing, the sound of the pages turning; and smell, the smell of the ink.
In a world where everyone is racing to go faster it’s important to understand how things are being observed and the importance of providing a clear communication and a strong
visual impact. Here is the winning approach, adopted over the years for the most diverse clients, who have enabled me to maintain an open mind and that creative freshness needed to guarantee solutions that are never obvious or predictable.
Because working every day in different sectors means having one single specialization, that of quality.

Most of the training we deliver are customised in-house group courses, which are tailored to incorporate desired document types, learning objectives and real-life examples. This customisation really brings the content to life and delivers the greatest impact. We also uniquely analyse the writing of each delegate in advance and present the feedback sensitively during the group training. It allows delegates to see how the techniques directly relate to them and provides them with specific takeaways to immediately improve their business writing. 

Our course customisation is partnered with expert, practical delivery. Our trainers all come from long, successful backgrounds in professional communications and we match the trainer's expertise to your organisation. entityDescription:
We are a studio focused on the research and design of services and products. We collaborate with organizations to make their ideas tangible and translate them into unique projects.
Graphic Facilitation (or scribing) visually documents concepts and highlights connections and patterns that emerge during a conversation. This happens in real time through the active listening of all the contributions of participants and their organization, and translated into clear, immediate, memorable and shareable representations. 
Communicatin. We use graphic design as a tool to better explain messages and concepts. We create products and solutions to communicate with efficiency and impact, marrying the beauty of the design with the coherence of the illustrations, infographics, logos, brand identities, icons and visualizations to support your communication campaigns. 
Illustration. We reveal what is hidden and simplify complexity. Both with drawings and digital tools, our goal is to create effective illustrations and elaborate metaphors, in order to explain complex concepts and help people remember them. 
Video and Animation. We translate stories, processes and strategies into creative videos that help convey a powerful message. Video scribing, animation, events’ reportage and products merging footage with digital: whatever the end result, we will take care of it from the beginning to the end, organizing every technical and creative detail. 
Publishing. We create unique editorial publications: reports, books and clear documents for the transmission of information and at the same time pleasing to the eye and to the touch. We pay attention to readability, aesthetics and we design the product according to the type of recipients. 
Digital Publishing. We design digital tools that leave space for the creativity, play, interactivity, and emotions, to bring attention to contents through a unique and completely new experience for the user. 
Interaction. A fundamental part of the success of an event, space or communication campaign is how much they can stimulate interest and engagement. We research and experiment in this field every day, combining tangible and virtual objects, contents and users.
Environment. We design private environments and shared public spaces, combining aesthetics, utility and effectiveness in communication. Environments that improve the interaction among users, telling stories on large and small surfaces: from exhibition stands and company offices to museums, co-working spaces and commercial activities. 
Artifacts. We create one-of-a-kind objects, designing brand identity and communication tools by taking care of the whole process: from the design to the production and the final quality control. We help you leave a tangible memory of your message. 
Training. We organize trainings courses to improve techniques and practices of the visualization and to develop listening capacities and comprehension of collaborative dynamics, with the objective of learning to find values and solutions in every field, for the person and organizations.

entityDescription: Gabriel Scientific OÜ is an owner of globally patented PneumaPure™ Filter Technology and SleepAngel trademark in order to design, manufacture and sell PneumaPure™ filter enabeled bedding products. SleepAngel bedding products with patented PneumaPure Filter Technology are the only products that can simultaneously provide comfort alongside a 100% barrier against pathogens. (Really) flexible and affordable workspace – whether that’s an office, workshop or laboratory
Access to funding that fills the gap between what an entrepreneur can raise themselves through family and friends and what a Venture Capital firm might fund
Support from highly qualified mentors, coaches and other entrepreneurs through part-funded business support programmes

entityName: Sieć Badawcza ŁUKASIEWICZ - Instytut Spawalnictwa; ŁUKASIEWICZ Research Network - Institute of Welding
entityDescription:
Established in 1945, Instytut Spawalnictwa (since 1st April 2019 Sieć Badawcza Łukasiewicz - Instytut Spawalnictwa) is a leading and key welding research and development organisation in Poland. In its long-standing activity Instytut Spawalnictwa has been solving problems in welding technology, coordinated numerous R&D projects and strengthened close links with the Polish industry and foreign centres. It's scope of activities covers issues concerning processes of joining structural materials with the use of advanced technologies of welding, brazing, thermal cutting and allied technologies. Instytut Spawalnictwa is the only organisation of its type in Poland and functions as:

- ANB - Authorised National Body - in European Federation for Welding, Joining and Cutting (EWF) and International Institute of Welding - authorised for qualification of welding personnel,
- ANBCC - Authorised National Body for Company Certification in EWF and IIW - authorised for certification of enterprises according to the PN-EN ISO 3834 standard,
- Accredited in Polish Centre for Accreditation (PCA) organisation for certification of welding processes, Factory Production Control, welding and NDT personnel and quality management systems,
- Notified Body in the European Union in the scope of 2014/68/EU Directive and Regulation (EU) no. 305/2011 of the European Parliament and of the council 

Mission - development and transfer of knowledge in the field of joining advanced structural materials in order to ensure innovation and competitiveness of producers of welded structures

entityDescription:
Open Climate Fix is a new non-profit research and development lab, totally focused on reducing greenhouse gas emissions as rapidly as possible. Every part of the organisation is designed to maximise climate impact, such as our open and collaborative approach, our rapid prototyping, and our attention on finding scalable & practical solutions.

By using an open-source approach, we can draw upon a much larger pool of knowledge and skills than any individual company, so combining existing islands of knowledge and accelerating progress. Our approach will be to search for ML (Machine Learning) problems where, if we solve a well-defined ML task, then there's likely to be a large climate impact.
Then, for each of these challenges, we'll:

1. Collate & release data, and write software tools to make it super-easy for people to consume this data.
2. Run a collaborative 'global research project' where everyone from 16-year-olds to PhD students to corporate research labs can help solve the ML tasks.
3. Help to put good solutions into production, once the community has developed them, so we can be reducing emissions ASAP.

entityDescription:
CAMEA, spol. s r. o., (CAMEA) is engaged in the development and production of modern image and signal processing systems for industrial use, road monitoring and other applications.
CAMEA is active in the following areas:
• research into methods and algorithms of image processing and computer vision,
• research in the field of computer graphics and human-computer interaction,
• research of image sensors and signal processing with acceleration by technical means,
• design of tools and subsystems for image processing and signal processing,
• design of turnkey systems and solutions using research results,
• manufacture and sale of image sensors and image processing equipment.

CAMEA was founded in 1995 by a group of professionals working in the field of image processing, computer graphics and signal processing at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Brno University of Technology (Czech Republic). It has undergone major developments since 1995 and is currently focusing on two basic areas:
• industrial camera systems;
• intelligent transport systems.

In addition to systems and custom solutions, CAMEA's activities include research and development, production and sale of video and signal processing components such as camcorders, digitizing boards for PCs, stand-alone microprocessor boards for control and stand-alone boards with signal processors for control purposes and image and signal processing. The company is also engaged in creating programming tools and subsystems for working with images and signal processing in real time.
Following state-of-art trends and in-house research and development, it is today a leading manufacturer of highly innovative solutions for these two areas.

CAMEA products are at the top of image processing technology in the Czech Republic. It has pioneered the measurement of segment speed and high-speed vehicle weighing. Exports abroad have also increased significantly in the last approximately 7 years. In foreign markets, we are talking about acting on B2B markets. CAMEA intends to build a global network of business partners representing its technology solutions in the regions. This format has already proven itself in the Russian Federation and the East African region.

entityDescription:
Holistic Innovation, S.L.U. (HI2), is a Spanish SME, specialized on services associated to the innovation management for the research and technology development with specific focus on spectrum management affairs, while bearing a holistic and strategic vision for the businesses associated to the research, technology development and innovation in the fields of audiovisual, networked media, future internet, satellite communications, earth observation, mobile communications, eHealth and maritime communications. HI´s staff, headed by Dr. Julián Seseña:
•	Has a particular experience in the field of spectrum management, standardization and policy development.
•	Provides services and associated commitment to reach objectives and flexibility to adapt to the evolving business and technology world, through setting close team with our customers.
•	Counts with spectrum mnagement professionals and researchers who offer many years’ experience on research in the fields of networked media, satellite communications, specific challenges associated to SMEs and eHealth, as well as strategic, regulatory and policy initiatives.
The well experienced staff of the company has participated in many European, National and International Cooperation Projects, as well as on activities of DVB, ETSI, ITU, Networld2020, NEM, ISI, GVF, CENELEC, ECC and is fully aware on the current trends on standardization, regulation, policy and ICT network infrastructure. 
 
HI´s staff is involved usually at the CETP meetings and is deeply aware of the activities of the ECC, CEPT WG FM, PT FM 44, PT FM50, PT FM45, WG SE, PT SE19, PT SE40, etc., monitoring also the international trends in Spectrum management, including activities of the European Radio Spectrum Committee, European Radio Spectrum Policy Group and the preparatory activities towards World Radiocommunications Conferences at European and ITU levels.
 
HI´s staff regularly participates in the activities of national preparatory groups for CEPT and WRC
Specific and relevant studies performed by the company in assotiation to the ESA AO9636 are:
•	Study on future demands and national policy for satellite communications for Mexican Government (Secretaria de Transportes y Comunicaciones).
•	Study for spectrum management organization for the Government of Equatorial Guinea on behalf of the International Telecommunications Union.
•	Study on spectrum management techniques and advisory work for the Spanish Administration through general contracts with the public Entity ISDEFE.
•	Study on monitoring and reporting on 5G evolution for the Spanish Observatory 5G.
•	Sharing studies of the use of FSS in the context of Unmanned Vechicles (UAS)
•	Preparatory studies for WRC 2015 representing European Space Agency.
•	Sharing studies for the use of mobile services in a Licensed Shared Access mechanism applicable in the case of Spain for the 2 GHz band in cooperation with the French company RED Technologies
•	Sharing studies for the use of FSS versus Wireless Access Systems/RLAN in the 5.9 GHz band
•	Sharing studies for the use of FSS systems versus Intelligent Transport Systems in the 6 GHz band.

entityName: STICHTING NEDERLANDSE WETENSCHAPPELIJK ONDERZOEK INSTITUTEN / CWI. CENTRUM WISKUNDE & INFORMATICA
entityDescription:
Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) is the national research institute for mathematics and computer science in the Netherlands. Founded in 1946, CWI is part of the Institutes Organisation of NWO, NWO-I since January 1st, 2018. 
While located at Amsterdam Science Park, our institute has strong international links, and we enjoy a global reputation for our innovative research.
At CWI, our strength is discovering and developing new ideas that benefit society and the economy, as well as other scientific areas. Our research is rooted in practical, real-life questions and explores essential aspects of modern life, including transport and communication networks, internet security, medical imaging and smart energy systems. 
Our innovations form an integral part of numerous software products, programming languages and international standards. CWI is at the heart of European research in mathematics and computer science. We take part in many international programmes, including EU Horizon2020 and EIT Digital. 
With close ties to industry and the wider academic world, both at home and abroad, we maintain a sharp focus on the bigger picture and real-world issues. The institute was the birthplace of the European internet in 1988. We registered one of the first country domains in the world, .nl, in 1986. We built the first Dutch computer in 1952 and kick-started the development of the popular programming language Python in the 1990s. So far, CWI has founded 26 spin-off companies.

entityName: Spacebridge Inc. (formerly known as Advantech Wireless Inc.)
entityDescription:
Founded in 1985, SpaceBridge Inc. is an established supplier and global market leader in broadband satellite communications systems technology. Previously known as Advantech Wireless Inc., the company is now doing business as SpaceBridge Inc.
Headquartered in Montreal, Canada, SpaceBridge Inc. is well positioned to meet the demands of today’s global market, with two affiliate R&D offshore innovation centers. Sales, and support offices, as well as remote offices in: Brazil, Colombia, United Kingdom, the Middle East, Indonesia, China, and Russia. SpaceBridge is an ISO9001 registered vendor.
The company develops and provides satellite network equipment and services, including VSAT HUBs and Terminals for Point-to-Point, Point-to-Multi-Point, and Mesh topologies, as well as SCPC and broadcast modems for GEO and NGSO satellite constellations.
SpaceBridge Inc. also provides Cloud-Based autonomous managed services for its customers, helping them to eliminate initial large Capex investments and save on network management Opex, while speeding time-to-market.
SpaceBridge Inc.’s diverse portfolio includes the ASAT™ product line, which serves different verticals with various technologies and applications. Key areas of focus are: Cellular Backhaul for 2G/3G/4G and 5G, Industrial Internet of Things-IIoT, Commercial and Military Satcoms-On-The-Move, High-Speed Broadband, Multicast IPTV, Voice-over-IP, Videoconferencing, L2/L3 VPN, Virtual Network Operator, and HD/UHD TV Broadcasting.
SpaceBridge Inc. first introduced its ASAT™ WaveSwitch™ technology to the market in 2015. This innovative, award-winning technology enables dynamic return link selection and switching to the most-appropriate waveform, whether MF-TDMA, ASCPC or SCPC, thereby optimizing satellite resource usage for satellite networks and operators.
As new NGSO/LEO/MEO satellite constellations revolutionize the satellite market, SpaceBridge Inc. is working in close partnership with New-Space players to advance the satellite communications landscape by developing VSAT technology to exploit next-gen leaps in capacity, and deliver 4G, 5G backhauling, IIoT and many other applications for our customers.
SpaceBridge Inc. continues to enhance its innovative architecture to not only meet today’s satellite challenges in managing ground and space satellite resources, but also to provide superior solutions that address the New-Space satellite challenges of tomorrow.

entityDescription:
Company profile NEDAERO

NEDAERO, based in The Netherlands at two locations, Zevenaar and Alphen aan den Rijn specializes in the manufacturing, repair (MRO) and distribution of components and systems for civil and military aircraft and helicopters. We service a broad range of platforms, our focus platforms are ATR and Dash8, AS350/Écureuil, F-16, NH90 and PUMA helicopters.

At the Zevenaar facility, NEDAERO manufactures new parts (for Airbus and Lockheed Martin). In fully equipped workshops with high-tech production - and test-equipment NEDAERO ensures that all components are being delivered in accordance with the highest standards and expectations within the Aerospace Industry. 
With over 40 years of manufacturing and MRO experience, NEDAERO has the expertise to provide its customers with proactive advice and technical support helping to ensure the most cost effective support solutions are provided to its civil and military customers worldwide. 
From the Alphen aan den Rijn facility, NEDAERO delivers helicopter and aircraft parts directly from distribution stock. Our products range from transceivers to life vests, from actuators to headsets and from oil & greases to a wide range of filters. We hold an exchange pool for ATR and AS350 Écureuil parts. In addition to this logistic support we also offer broad expertise to military governmental organizations and private military MRO companies. 
For further details on products and capabilities please go to our website www.nedaero.com

entityDescription:
Intelligent Software Solutions Global Limited (ISS Global Ltd) are comprised of a team of industry veterans with decades of real-world experience. This subject matter expertise combined with world class software development allow us to deliver products and solutions that drive a commitment we share with our customers – making the world a safer place. Our team stands stand at the forefront of cybersecurity. Comprehensive, converged offering of technologies and tools expose system and network vulnerabilities, anticipating and neutralizing threats wherever they lie – land, sea, air, cyberspace, or outer space. From large-scale cybersecurity programs to immediate deployment and rapid assistance, our proven security methods reflect our customer-first approach, innovative mindset, and effective execution style. We’re on the cutting edge of cybersecurity innovation, working with machine learning and artificial intelligence–based technologies to help mitigate the cyber threat. Clients trust us to protect their critical assets through services such as integrated electronic security systems, integrated enterprise physical security systems, and threat vulnerability assessments and mitigation.

Our space and operations support programs boost service component leads in space. We provide systems engineering, advisory, and technical services for space satellite systems that encompass defence satellite communications systems (DSCS), global positioning systems (GPS), space based infrared systems (SBIRS), third generation infrared sensors (3GIRS), and the Defence Meteorological Support Program (DMSP). Our experts led the advisory services team responsible for the Commercially Hosted IR Payload (CHIRP) launch. Our key Space capabilities include: specifications and standards development, training, tools development, mission assurance, mission support, test and evaluation, modernization, critical technology and industrial base assessment, physical security, and program protection. Our expertise and services are critical to space launch operations cybersecurity and the underlying disciplines of information systems security and communications security implementation for space systems.

entityName: +ATLANTIC - Association for an Atlantic Collaborative Laboratory
entityDescription:
The Atlantic plays a key role in the strategy to face major societal challenges: Climate Change, Environmental Sustainability, and Energy and Food availability. Major circulation changes during the last thousands of years had large impact on global climate and led to reorganizations of the planet’s ecosystems; the enhanced warming of regions of the north Atlantic will also have major consequences for the marine ecosystems asking for better monitoring and follow-up. Pressures arising from human activities related with coastal urban expansion, fisheries and deep-sea mining need to be quantified and mitigated. Marine renewal energy systems will expand quickly to ensure long term decarbonisation and their operation needs to be supported with minimum harm to the natural systems. The ocean is and will remain critical for the future food supply of humanity. 
This Collaborative Laboratory (CoLAB) for the Atlantic (+Atlantic), which was formally approved by the Portuguese Science and Technology Foundation (FCT) on January 30th 2018, created on May 2018 and initiated its activity on April 14th 2019, targets the challenges put forward by the Atlantic Interactions initiative materialized in the Atlantic International Research Center (AIR Center) through a 5 year plan. The +Atlantic CoLAB will constitute an important node of the AIR Center as well as of the recently created Portuguese Space Agency (Portugal Space).
+Atlantic is a non-profit private association comprising, at the moment of writing, 13 Portuguese members (7 enterprises, 2 universities and 4 non-profit associations of scientific nature or public utility) of different areas of the country and different backgrounds. The latter range from robotics (submarine and aerial), climate modelling and renewable energies to satellites and remote sensing services.
The CoLAB for the Atlantic aims at advancing knowledge on the interactions between the Ocean, Atmosphere, Climate and Energy in the Atlantic, with an integrated approach from deep sea to space. The idea is to develop a better understanding of the Atlantic system, to prepare for the sustainable use of its resources and to create a framework to unleash its potential for Society, promoting blue growth and highly qualified employment. 
The dynamics of these interactions are extremely complex and no single organisation is prepared to tackle them appropriately. Hence, demanding an overarching approach that cannot be achieved without a broad engagement of different stakeholders, able to address the breadth of issues being dealt by the CoLAB. The CoLAB will build on advanced research in Space, Ocean and Energy technologies, as well as in Data Science, to foster the production of new knowledge about the ocean and its interactions as well as the development and deployment of new infrastructures and platforms that will provide new sources of data for the Atlantic, leading to new research strategies. 
The CoLAB will build on the expertise of its founders that, together with a new highly qualified team of researchers and the integrated operation of existing and new infrastructures, will address the major challenges lying ahead for the future of the Atlantic system. Overall, the CoLAB will be advancing knowledge and providing value added services to enhance the sustainable exploration and exploitation of this global resource. 
All CoLAB activities fall within one or more of its 5 scientific priorities:
•	Axis 1: Sustainability of marine resources
•	Axis 2: Atlantic observation and monitoring
•	Axis 3: Impact of climate change on the Atlantic
•	Axis 4: Future technologies for the Oceans
•	Axis 5: Data science and Big Data
All CoLAB activities aim to contribute directly to value creation, be it through the production of new knowledge which can support market research and development strategies or through oriented actions focused on the creation of a portfolio of products and services that can be exploited with the CoLAB members.

Commendium is a 3D data acquisition and processing company specialising in the
capture and processing of 3D data from remote, difficult, and potentially hazardous
environments such as caves, mines, mountains, forests, deserts, underwater and
industrially hazardous locations. We have been mapping underground locations all over
the world including karstic caves and basaltic lava tubes all over the world for many
years and within the speleological world, now have a reputation for high quality work.
Our work can be for scientific, engineering, entertainment or conservational goals. We
have used a wide range of technology to assist us including, LiDAR (both airborne and
terrestrial), photogrammetrics as well as traditional theodolite and tape and compass
work. Most recently we mapped Tham Luang Cave, the cave in Thailand where 12 boys

create 3D graphics to illustrate the cave and how the rescue was conducted.

entityDescription:
Kathy founded Carrak Consulting Ltd to provide a range of geo-environmental services to land and mineral developers seeking to adopt SMART solutions to the responsible management of natural resources and wastes.
Kathy is a mining geologist and chartered environmentalist with sixteen year’s consultancy experience on natural resource projects in the UK and overseas. Carrak Consulting Ltd provides environmental management and sustainable development tools for proposed and operational mines. In the UK the company specialises in mining legacy issues, specifically the assessment of land affected by mineral development and wastes. Kathy is well acquainted with baseline conditions and specific issues at many former mine sites in environmentally sensitive locations across Cornwall.
In 2018 Carrak Consulting Ltd was part of a multi-disciplinary team, including the British Geological Survey, Satellite Applications Catapult and Camborne School of Mines (University of Exeter), involved in a project using earth observation data to identify mineral signatures, vegetation characteristics and land cover types in Cornwall. 
Carrak Consulting Ltd is experienced in ESIA project management, preparing technical due diligence reports and advising on environmentally and socially responsible practices throughout all stages of a project lifecycle. She is conversant with international standards, including those of Equator Principle Financial Institutions and has experience of working in the EU, Russia, Central Asia and the Caucasus. 
Carrak Consulting Ltd employs specialist Associates and works with members of the Cornwall Mining Alliance to provide bespoke consultancy packages. The company has a wide range of industry and public sector contacts and provides services including:
•	Environmental monitoring; management plans & systems
•	Permitting support & compliance monitoring
•	Environmental & social capacity building
•	Environmental impact, risk & liability assessments
•	Due diligence & technical reporting
•	Environmental audits, fatal flaw analysis & action planning
•	Research and project management

entityDescription:
Over the years, Barrnon has developed an enviable reputation for great engineering ideas that are brilliantly executed and then applied in some of the world’s most challenging environments.
We started with exceptionally durable scallop fishing gear – which we still sell to happy fishermen all over the UK. We then took our knowledge of the rigours of trawling and transferred it to some huge problems in the nuclear decommissioning industry.Through our subsidiary company, Kapwell Technologies, we’re now applying insight from the nuclear industry to tackle a considerable challenge for the Oil & Gas sector. We are now at the centre of some of the world’s most demanding industries, delivering innovative engineering solutions that get the job done. 
Barrnon is a boutique engineering services provider based in the quiet Cumbrian town of Appleby. Led by Managing Director, Andy Barr, we don’t just create imaginative engineering solutions to the most complex problems, we also manufacture them on site.
We are exceptionally competent when working with metal, using state-of-the-art manufacturing techniques to bring our innovative 3D CAD designs to life in our extensive workshop.Our unique combination of skills has given us the opportunity to partner with some of the biggest names in engineering around the world – and to take our branded products into specialist markets including nuclear decommissioning in Japan, the USA and the UK.

entityDescription:
Icebreaker One focuses on bridging the gaps between finance, policy and climate — unlocking a data marketplace that will help better inform large-scale financial decisions to minimise their carbon and environmental impact. 

Our ability to join up and use existing and emerging data to address our environmental crises is stifled. The inhibitor to innovation is not technology— it is culture. Asset owners, funders and insurers are complex value chains today: not working with data at-scale due to high transaction costs. 

We have an ocean of available capital. Lack of good data-flow is leading to misallocation of resources, missed opportunities and catastrophic risks on our global balance sheets. Broad digital transformation is reaching maturity across industries—now is the time to build in new uses for the data. If we solve this for climate change, we will unlock solutions for other areas.

Building multi-disciplinary partnerships, based on decades of experience with open standards, data governance, mass collaboration, and public-private partnerships, Icebreaker One will unlock the exchange of decision-critical data to enable a multi-trillion dollar shift in investment.

Company AXIS TECH was founded in 2010 as a Czech company focused on production of precise machining. Through strong investments we achieved very good production technologies supported with know-how from aerospace and space industry. Currently we have 45 employees and we are in SME range.

We are qualified according to ISO 9001:2015. In our ISO certification are implemented aerospace requirements including FAI procedure.

Our core business is production of precise milled parts up to one meter made mainly from titanium and aluminium alloys, stainless steels, plastic materials and hardened materials as well.

For surface treatments, NDT and production of bigger parts are used qualified subsuppliers in Czech republic or in EU countries.
We can offer not only deliveries of parts but also assembly including final adjustment.

Actually we have 1 800 m2 of production area size with ten 5-axis CNC-Machines HERMLE and one 3-axis CNC-Machine ZPS. For turning and grinding are installed conventional machines.

For deburring we have two areas, first one is for deburring according to standard conditions, second one is for precise deburring and cleaning of parts under the microscope.

Inspection room is fully air-conditioned with three CMM machines, the largest one is up to two meters.

Since founding is our company as qualified supplier of structural parts for Airbus, Boeing and Embraer aircrafts.

For space industry we deliver mainly precise parts for telecommunication and meteorological satellites and MGSE as well.
Production of spacer for satellite separation device (customer S.A.B. Aerospace).

entityDescription:

Our technology, OtaskiES' INtuitIV is a patent-pending AI-based street lighting/lamp solution that uses motion (from motion sensors and telemetry) and devices-edge/Lora/WIFI (communication technology agnostic) to implement light dimming regimes on the grid; while learning and developing tailored algorithm using localized data. Thus, saving 40 – 50% of the energy required to power street light (excluding LED savings) and works with non-LED systems.

entityName: UNIV FIRENZE - Dipartimento di Scienze Biomediche Sperimentali e Cliniche (DSBS)
entityDescription:
The Department of Experimental and Clinical Biomedical Sciences "Mario Serio," consists of faculty and researchers pertaining to 15 scientific disciplinary fields of clinical and preclinical areas who carry out teaching activities within the School of Human Health Sciences, the School of Mathematical Physical and Natural Sciences, the School of Engineering, the School of Psychology and the School of Agriculture. Specialization Schools of Health Area and Level I and II Master's degrees are incardinated.
The Department, which is divided into four sections with the task of coordinating, rationalizing and optimizing the use of resources located in different areas, is organized into 42 Research Units that include, in addition to tenured staff, fixed-term researchers, research fellows, PhD students, postgraduates, students and other scholars working under agreements.
Activities in research range from Biochemistry, Molecular Biology and Pathology as basic sciences, embracing more purely clinical disciplines such as Gynecology and Obstetrics, Endocrinology, Diagnostic Imaging and Radiation Therapy and Nephrology. A unifying point among these disciplines as a binding element between areas of scientific excellence is Gender Medicine, a modern view of medicine geared toward capturing gender differences with respect to health and disease processes. It is the administrative home of the Doctoral Program in Biomedical Sciences, and in collaboration with Pisa and Siena, participates in two Pegaso doctoral programs
The Department has the following goals:
1 To create transversality between basic and clinical disciplines, using outstanding research and exploiting the excellence present in both fields of endeavor,
2 Create synergies between different research groups
3 Promote the recruitment of new researchers, in all areas of research, with a view to renewing and enhancing the design capacity of research units,
4 The Department has been selected among the 2018 Excellent Departments (MIUR call). The selected topic is Gender Medicine. The project aims to strengthen SSDs characterized by a gender footprint, create a "facility" to support both intra- and inter-departmental research, stimulate an exchange of translational and clinical expertise, and create a research funding fund.
5 Support the research of young researchers with a view to achieving standards of excellence.
6 Maintain the high quality of teaching delivered by the Department's faculty members by enhancing the relationship between research and teaching and supporting with adequate staffing points all teaching delivered by faculty members
7 Support the teaching activities carried out within the teaching laboratories and improve the teaching facilities and laboratories dedicated to students

entityDescription:
SYLEX, a mid-size company founded in 1995, is a world-class original design manufacturer of high quality optical interconnect solutions. 
Our superb engineering and design capabilities, strong quality control systems, and substantial manufacturing capacity allows us to deliver both high-volume and custom-tailored solutions extremely rapidly as clients or the market require. 
For telecom and datacom markets SYLEX specializes in designing and manufacturing MTP harnesses, PRIZM LightTurn assemblies and high density DURALINO fanout trunks for enterprise, carrier, and specialty applications.
SYLEX offers tailor made automated monitoring system solutions based on modernized FBG technology. These systems, which have been repeatedly verified by many projects around the world, are used to monitor the structural health and geotechnical safety of infrastructure projects. Our sensors utilize the principle of Fiber Bragg Gratings manufactured by either Draw Tower Technology (DTG) or Femto-Second writing technology (FS), thus providing the systems with unique advantages compared to the conventional electrical solutions (or even compared to standard FBG based monitoring systems).
SYLEX sensing solutions are suitable for strain, temperature, displacement, pressure, load, vibration and deformation measurements within the Mining industry, Civil Engineering, Geo-technical markets or any other SHM and monitoring purposes. 
We are ready to design, develop and manufacture any application tailored sensors offering to our partners a high quality engineering and manufacturing environment along with our modern design approach.

entityDescription:
LAER S.p.A. works in the Aeronautical field since 1989, born as family run Company today is a private Company with 207 employees on two sites. Laer is able to manage fully vertically integrated work packages, from design to manufacturing of complex assembled structures and UNI EN ISO 9100:2009 - 9001:2008 and NADCAP qualified. The organization has maintained the direct vertical relationship between Top Management and R&D department thus guaranteeing quick feedback flexibility and in production reaction time. 
Two production sites are located in Campania, Southern Italy Region. Headquarter, Technical, Administrative and Staff Offices are located in Airola, where Machining and Metal sheet, Thermal and Special Processes and Assembly are performed according to Quality standard requirements.
Acerra plant (on 2.000 Sq.m covered area) is dedicated to Composite materials production by the conventional Autoclave methods and by innovative Liquid Resin Infusion technique. All items, fabricated and inspected in each site, join in Airola for final assembly on different Program Workshops, which take up about 60% of total cover area that is 15.400 square meters.
Laer has a prominent position in Aerospace Industry of Campania Region, supplying items and large assemblies in both metal and composite material, fabricated and inspected according to relevant standards. Main products are: fuselage sections, such as central, fore and aft - movable surfaces, such as aileron, spoiler and flaps – machined parts for primary structures such as Horizontal and Vertical Stabilizers. Laer is LEONARDO TIER1 on ATR, Airbus, Boeing B767 e B787, C27J, Bombardier C-Series, Aermacchi M346 programs and direct supplier for FACC on SSJ100 program and for Piaggio Aerospace on MPA e P180 programs. Each year LAER engineering manages about 15.000 Part Number, counting about 1000 tools designed and fabricated. During last three years period, Turnover overcame 20 Million following a growing trend assessed in 2016. 
LAER aims to ensure continuous improvement of its own know—how and to acquire innovative industrial capacity in the context of national and international growth, in order to improve competitiveness on the international market. In last three years period LAER had the opportunity to develop several projects, funded on Public Entities (MiSE, MIUR, Armareo, Regione Campania, European Commission) in collaboration with Research Centres and Private Company. As production Private Company operating in Aerospace, the research thematic area is aimed to develop innovative manufacturing processes applied to both fabrication and assembly stage. R&D team, specialized in aeronautical fabrication processes and coordinated by a Philosophy Doctor in Smart Systems for Automation of Production, is supported by different skills, coming from Process Engineering, Production, Quality Control and all impacted departments.

entityDescription: Polariton Technologies Ltd.'s objective is to deliver the world's fastest and smallest modulators, overcoming the current limitations in telecommunications and sensing applications. In particular, we address the transport bottleneck due to faster evolution in electronic signal generation than in fiber optical transport capability. Modulators that are key components in today’s communication infrastructure perform the conversion from an electrical signal to an optical signal. Today’s electro-optic modulators cannot deliver the speed required for future high-speed telecommunications; they are too large in footprint and hence expensive in fabrication, and energy inefficient. Through recent advances in our endeavor, we could demonstrate plasmonic modulators that are 10 times faster and 100 times smaller than current devices. Further, our devices are extremely energy efficient, thus reducing the carbon footprint for future telecommunication systems. Coming out of ETH Zurich, Switzerland, Polariton Technologies Ltd. is a newly incorporated start-up.

entityDescription:
Business Development for geospatial Services and Solutions

Urbetho e.K., registered in Alling, Germany, was founded in 2019 by Dr. Ursula Benz. It provides business development consultancy for Geo-IT companies who want to scale up their business and integrate their services into business solutions of other verticals like agronomics, IoT, logistics, telecom, utilities and others.

Geo-IT companies get support by Urbetho and its partner network to evolve their business from one-off projects to reusable solutions and finally to repeatable geoservices with a high degree of automation and well packaged for a scalable sales approach. 

The rapidly growing number of public funded and private market- and Geo-IT platforms are a great opportunity for many of those geoservices. Urbetho explores for its customers how and which platforms can be of best help for the certain services to simplify and speed up the intended go-to-market strategy and to reach business scalability fast and at low risk. 

For example, market platforms, as e.g. ArcGIS Marketplace, cloudeo, NoR and eoMall can serve as worldwide marketing and sales channels and take away a lot of the technical and financial administration processes and overhead. They allow their platform members to fully focus onto the development of the solutions and services to accommodate their customers’ needs. The IaaS, DaaS and SaaS offerings of Geo-IT platforms, e.g. AWS, Google, GBDX from Maxar and the DIAS – funded by ESA to support especially the European business – save with their fast access to a multitude of data and re-usable software tools production cost and time and provide scalability and reliability for the service delivery.

However, to unlock this potential technical, commercial and sometimes also legal challenges have to be overcome. Together with its partners Urbetho helps its customers to address these topics and to pave their path to a scalable business and – if applicable – to accelerate a successful onboarding of such services onto the best fitting marketplaces and Geo-IT platforms.

Company description: Business Development for geospatial Services and Solutions

Urbetho e.K., registered in Alling, Germany, was founded in 2019 by Dr. Ursula Benz. It provides business development consultancy for Geo-IT companies who want to scale up their business and integrate their services into business solutions of other verticals like agronomics, IoT, logistics, telecom, utilities and others.

Geo-IT companies get support by Urbetho and its partner network to evolve their business from one-off projects to reusable solutions and finally to repeatable geoservices with a high degree of automation and well packaged for a scalable sales approach. 

The rapidly growing number of public funded and private market- and Geo-IT platforms are a great opportunity for many of those geoservices. Urbetho explores for its customers how and which platforms can be of best help for the certain services to simplify and speed up the intended go-to-market strategy and to reach business scalability fast and at low risk. 

For example, market platforms, as e.g. ArcGIS Marketplace, cloudeo, NoR and eoMall can serve as worldwide marketing and sales channels and take away a lot of the technical and financial administration processes and overhead. They allow their platform members to fully focus onto the development of the solutions and services to accommodate their customers’ needs. The IaaS, DaaS and SaaS offerings of Geo-IT platforms, e.g. AWS, Google, GBDX from Maxar and the DIAS – funded by ESA to support especially the European business – save with their fast access to a multitude of data and re-usable software tools production cost and time and provide scalability and reliability for the service delivery.

However, to unlock this potential technical, commercial and sometimes also legal challenges have to be overcome. Together with its partners Urbetho helps its customers to address these topics and to pave their path to a scalable business and – if applicable – to accelerate a successful onboarding of such services onto the best fitting marketplaces and Geo-IT platforms.

entityDescription:
Telecom ParisTech is one of France's leading graduate engineering schools and is considered the school in the field of Communication and Information Technologies. Its disciplines include all the sciences and techniques that fall within the term "Information and Communications": Computer Science Networks, Communications, Electronics, Signal and Image Processing, as well as the study of economic and social aspects associated with modern technology.

 The school was founded more than a hundred years ago and is classed among the Grandes Ecoles d'Ingénieurs. Because of its high scientific standard and the extremely competitive admission procedures, ENST can be compared to the highest level engineering schools and universities that one would find abroad.
As an institution of higher education, the school is publicly funded, with close links with a number of partner institutions: it is part of a federation of schools in telecommunications, called the Institut Mines-Télécom and a member of ParisTech, a multi-campus networks of nine graduate engineering schools, all located in the Paris area. 

The Telecom ParisTech laboratories are part of Institut Mines Telecom-Recherche, research unit also gathering laboratories from the ENST-Bretagne, the INT and from the subsidiaries (Eurécom, ENIC, ¿).

Telecom ParisTech today has a faculty of about 150 full-time staff (full professors, associate and assistant professors), over 200 part-time lecturers and a student body of about 1000 students (including 750 in the three year diploma program, 100 in one of the master's level programs, and 200 Ph.D. students. 

Telecom ParisTech's four departments carry out research and teaching activities in the school's central areas of expertise :
¿	Department of Communications and Electronics (COMELEC)
¿	Department of Computer Science and Networks (INFRES)
¿	Department of Signal and Image Processing (TSI)
¿	Department of Economics and Social Sciences (EGSH) 

Telecom ParisTech's scientific policy is in phase with the rapid evolution of the sector of Information Technologies and the central role played by networks and information systems today. Research builds upon the major disciplines of digital communications, electronics, computer science and engineering, networks, digital signal and image processing and the economics of information systems, with applications in many systems, such as :
¿	high speed optical networks 
¿	local loops 
¿	satellites 
¿	mobile communications 
¿	multimedia and hypermedia 
¿	internet and the web and many of their areas of application (distance learning, health, environment, etc.) 

Over the last few decades, Telecom ParisTech has gained a recognized position internationally in its technical domains. In addition to working on the development in the basic sciences, research at Telecom ParisTech also aims at broadening its field of study, moving in particular towards system integration, innovative services on the internet and in other media, and the analysis of users communication practices and their social impact. Telecom ParisTech thus covers all aspects of Information Technologies. 
Telecom ParisTech is committed to maintaining an optimal balance between scientific research, whose themes remain fairly stable, and applied research, which changes more rapidly.
