entityDescription:
Fotosintetica & Microbiologica S.r.l. (F&M) is a Spin-off company of the University of Florence founded in 2004 to exploit the know-how on microalgae physiology and mass cultivation developed since 1980 by a research group coordinated by Prof. Mario Tredici. F&M technologies are backed up by more than 30 years of studies in algae cultivation and characterization. Our laboratories and outdoor experimental facilities are located within the Polo Scientifico e Tecnologico dell’ Università di Firenze in Sesto Firentino (Firenze).
F&M provides consultancy on microalgae cultivation for production of biofuels, biofertilisers, functional feeds and foods, biomass for aquaculture, polyunsatured fatty acids, pigments, natural drugs and cosmetics. 
With our staff we are able to provide technical and scientific assistance services relating to: isolation, selection and characterization of algal strains, modification and optimization of algal production process, development and process/product innovation, contract manufacturing and training. F&M supplies turnkey algal cultivation systems, following all the phases: design, construction, start-up and maintenance. The need to produce at ever lower costs has led the company to develop "scalable", reliable and cost-effective cultivation systems such as the Green Wall Panel (GWP®) panel photobioreactors (ITFI20030047 and ITFI20090167 patents) and column photobioreactors F&M-AC. Our reactors are used in Italy and abroad for research (Kalmar University, Sweden; Wageningen University, Holland; Bergen University, Norway; KAUST, Saudi Arabia; VEOLIA, France) and production (Necton SA, Portugal; Archimede Ricerche Srl , Italy, Agricultural Society Serenissima, Italy).Because of its know-how, proprietary photobioreactor technologies, and its collection of over 1300 microalgal and cyanobacterial strains, F&M is the ideal partner for starting applied research and commercial activity on microalgae.
F&M was partner of several UE research project: BIOFAT, FUEL4ME, SPLASH, NOMORFILM and has participated in the Italian project “MAMBO: MicroAlghe Materia Prima perBioOlio” funded by Italian biodiesel producers.

entityDescription:
CESEFOR (www.cesefor.com) is a private non-profit Foundation founded in January 2003. It is a Service provider for the promotion of forestry and forest-based industries, originally within the Region of Castile and León (one of the 17 Autonomous Regions in Spain) but today with a national and international remit. The Foundation contributes to the regional development, competitiveness and sustainability of the forestry industries that use regional forest resources. Cesefor signed in 2014 an agreement with the Regional Managing Authority for the development of a series of services and products related to the forestry sector (among these: conservation actions). The agreement covers a wide group of forestry fields. In order to do this, Cesefor brings together a range of services: capacity building, consultancy, training and R&D projects. 
Cesefor, as Forestry and Wood Technology Centre, has an extensive experience in the development of R&D&I projects, mainly focused on the enhancement of NWFP and the development of new wood products.
Another interesting and active working line for the project is focused on IT developments for the forestry sector: web and software development, GIS analysis and applications, mobile devices solutions for geographical projects, and high-tech solutions for forestry products evaluation, such as the Lidar application for forestry inventories.
CESEFOR is also present in several European Networks and highly experienced in communication and dissemination: graphic design, web page development and management, social media, event planning and organization, newsletters and media work. CESEFOR publishes “IndForma”: a leading e-newsletter of the Spanish forest sector. CESEFOR is an official member of the European Forest Institute; hosts the Secretariat of the Mediterranean Model Forest Network since 2008; it is member of the IUFRO Network and part of the Steering Committee of the ERIAFF Network and of the FAO SilvaMed’s CPMF.

Barrier Networks is a Scottish Cyber Security Company that specialises in protecting organisations from modern day cyber threats.
We partner with leading cyber security vendors and work in a trusted partner capacity to help our customers identify and resolve the cyber risks that threaten their business operations. As a ‘Trusted Partner’ of Police Scotland and the Scottish Business Resilience Centre we assist organisations with improving their cyber security and can accredit them with the National Cyber Security Centre’s Cyber Essentials and Cyber Essentials Plus certification. We work closely with Public Sector and Central Government and are a Scottish Government listed supplier for Digital Technology Services Dynamic Procurement System for Cyber Security, a UK Government G-Cloud Supplier and a UK Government Digital Outcomes Specialist supplier for Cyber Security.
Our Client base covers most industry verticals, but Finance and the sectors which rely on Industrial and Automated Control Systems are specialist delivery areas for us.

INNO'Energy is a recent and dynamic company specializing in the following areas:
 • Research and Development (R & D) in satellite and physical oceanography, meteorology and climate : expertise, analysis and evaluation of data (in situ, satellite, models), numerical oceanic and meteorological modeling;
 • Marine and Onshore Renewable Energies: wind, solar, currents energy, wave energy, sea thermal energy.

INNO'Energy provides scientific expertise and engineering services in satellite data, in situ measurement and ocean and meteorological numerical models aimed at:
 • improving their quality,
 • increasing the knowledge of the modes of climate variability (regional and global oceanic and atmospheric circulation),
 • characterizing and qualifying the resource potential of renewable energies (marine and onshore) as well as assessing their predictability in the climate change context.

INNO'Energy also develops custom decision support software solutions tailored to the needs of:
 • analysis and assessments of satellite data and numerical models, 
 • climate variability studies, 
 • renewable energy (offshore and onshore) resource potential assessments,
 • wind and solar production forecast,

entityDescription:
Montimage is a French SME located in the central 13th district of Paris. It is a research oriented company that proposes its know-how and tools for monitoring and testing network traffic and services. The tools are dedicated to help developers and operators improve the quality and reliability of their services.
Montimage relies on innovation to deliver competitive tools and know-how that provide end-to-end monitoring solutions integrating functional, QoS and security analysis of network communications and business activity. For this Montimage has developed an integrated modular set of tools that makes it possible to perform traffic inspection and activity monitoring based on formal models and machine learning used to identify the expected behaviour and anomalies. The tool framework is called MMT (Montimage Monitoring Tool) and can be deployed as a stand-alone tool for operators, a library that can be integrated in specialised frameworks or applications, or as a cloud service. These tools are applied to different domains (including: Telecommunications, eHealth and Industry 4.0...) and environments (IoT, SCADA, Critical Infrastructures, Cyber Physical Systems, 4G/5G...). 
The core business of Montimage is developing tools for monitoring and testing networks, applications and services; in particular, for the analysis of functional, performance and security aspects; and, for improving context awareness and end-user trust. Montimage's flagship tool (MMT) allows the capture of telecommunication packets, as well as any structured messages, for performing traffic analysis, estimating quality of user experience (QoE), analysing security and detecting/mitigating security attacks. It uses deep packet inspection (DPI), statistics and machine learning techniques to classify traffic and analyse its behaviour.
Montimage has participated in the development of the ground system data processing and visulaisation for the Plank space mission, in the development of cybersecurity solutions for Thales and the French department of Defense, and is very active in European collaborative research projects in the domain of future mobile networks, cyber physical systems, critical infrastructures, Iot networks, advanced testing and monitoring techniques, etc.

entityName: State Nature Conservancy of Slovak Republic
entityDescription: The State Nature Conservancy of the Slovak Republic (SNC) is a government/public institution operating on the basis of the state/government budget contribution and own income, however, it is not primarily a profit making institution. It was established by the Ministry of the Environment of the Slovak Republic. SNC SR is an expert institution focused on actions for nature and landscape conservation and administration of Slovak caves accessible to visitors in accordance with the provisions of the Act. No. 543/2002 C.L. on Nature and Landscape Conservation as amended by later regulations. Its actions are also governed by the Act No. 15/2005 C.L. on the Conservation of Wild Animals and Plants through Regulating Trade therein. Scope of activities of the SNC SR covers the following: area protection, species (both animals and plants) protection, protection of minerals and fossils, protection of woody vegetation on not-forest land, environmental education, training and promotion, monitoring a relevant information systems. Specific activities relevant to aforementioned fields of actions include: development of draft strategies, concepts, programmes and formulating/designing nature conservation measure, methodologies, development of background documents for law making activities, formulating of technical standpoints and background documents for decision-making activities, development of projects for new designations or amendments of protected areas, research and monitoring of protected areas and species, management of publicly accessible caves, information centres, educational trails and sites, international co-operation in the field of nature/biodiversity conservation, publishing. SNC SR coordinates technical implementation of NATURA 2000 network in Slovakia. It is a designated scientific authority for the purpose of CITES and coordinates actions in Slovak biosphere reserves designated under the UNESCO-MAB Programme. SNC SR has a long term experiences with implementing the projects, including international ones. All projects at which SNC SR have participated or has been participating/implementing are focused on nature and biodiversity conservation, particularly on area and species protection, through implementing management measures in protected areas, as well as on education, training and communication in this area. SNC SR implemented several projects funded through various financial schemes/programmes.

entityDescription:
AGC Glass Europe SA (www.agc-glass.eu) produces, processes and distributes flat glass for the construction (external glazing and interior decorative glass), the automotive (original & replacement glass) and the solar sectors. Its Technovation Centre in Gosselies, Belgium is hosting the research, engineering and IP activities of AGC Glass Europe. It employs around 300 people among which 200 researchers (mostly Engineers and PhD's), all driven by operational excellence and innovation. Based on its three missions of technological innovation, technical assistance and scientific advice, the R&D Centre is developing the high-tech glass products of tomorrow while taking human wellbeing and protection of the environment into account. 
Its main activities are:
Developing Innovations:It drives research and development for new glass, chemical, and high-tech materials, turning ideas into market-ready products and improving manufacturing processes.
Customer Co-creation:It serves as a collaborative space where AGC works directly with customers and partners to design and develop custom solutions.
Showcasing Technology:It functions as an interactive showroom to demonstrate AGC's latest technologies and inspire new applications in architecture and automotive industries.

The Technovation Centre's connectivity activities aim to make glass an active, intelligent component in cars and buildings.
- For Automotive:They focus on integrating antennas into glass for seamless 5G and Wi-Fi, ensuring perfect compatibility with sensors for autonomous driving (ADAS), and developing advanced Head-Up Displays (HUDs) that project information onto the windshield.

- For Architectural:They develop glass that improves indoor 5G signal reception in modern buildings. They also create smart glass that connects to building management systems (IoT) and turn glass surfaces into interactive media displays.

entityName: Stichting International Soil Reference and Information Center
entityDescription:
ISRIC - World Soil Information is an independent, science-based foundation. The institute was founded in 1966 following a recommendation of the International Soil Science Society (ISSS) and a resolution of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). ISRIC has a mission to serve the international community with information about the world’s soil resources to help addressing major global issues. 
 
ISRIC produces and serves quality-assured soil information together with our partners at global, regional and national levels. ISRIC stimulates the use of this information to address global challenges such as improved food security, land degradation and climate change mitigation through capacity building, awareness raising and direct cooperation with users and clients. 
 
ISRIC has been elected in 2017 to host the soil data facility for the Global Soil Partnership (GSP). For 25 years ISRIC is a consortium member of the World Overview of Conservation Approaches and Technologies (WOCAT). ISRIC is a member of Global Open Data on Agriculture and Nutrition (GODAN) and co-chairs the GODAN Working Group on Soils focusing on interoperability of soil databases for better policy & investment decisions and risk mitigation. 
 
ISRIC operates in four priority areas:
Setting standards and providing reference for soil information (‘’the Foundation”)  
Brokering of soil information (“Raison d’être”)  
Education, capacity building and advocacy (“Competent user community”)  
Innovative data and information products for development (“Boosting impact”)

entityName: INSTITUTO DE GEOGRAFIA E ORDENAMENTO DO TERRITORIO - UNIVERSIDADE DE LISBOA
entityDescription:
The Institute of Geography and Spatial Planning (IGOT) – University of Lisbon was created in 2009 and aims at promoting geography and planning higher education, advanced training and research. The Centre of Geographical Studies (CEG) is the research unit of IGOT. Established in 1943, CEG is the main Portuguese institution conducting research in the field of Geography. The research environment at CEG –IGOT benefits from belonging to the Universidade de Lisboa, which is the largest and one of the most prestigious universities in Portugal. CEG is organised in three Thematic Lines, which coordinate the activities of 7 Research Groups. Currently, around 200 researchers, of which 78 PhD graduates, work at CEG. CEG work is global in scope and addresses cutting-edge subjects of contemporary Human and Physical Geography and Planning inquiries, aiming at contributing to theoretical, methodological and empirical knowledge on the field. CEG owns and publishes continuously since 1965 the prestigious journal Finisterra. CEG is involved in several collaborative research partnerships and networking activities, both at international and national scales.
Due to the high quality of research environment and facilities, such as a specialized library and a vast Map Collection, CEG hosts numerous visiting Scholars and Researchers as well as graduate students from around the world, including from some of the most prestigious research centres in the field.

entityDescription: Fraunhofer LBF in Darmstadt is one of the most traditional institutes of the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft. Over 75 years ago, the former “Laboratory for Structural Durability LBF” shaped a completely new area of research that even back then was already economically significant and, up to today, has lost none of its topicality and pertinence. Particularly in the last decade, the institute developed its competence center both in breadth and depth on the basis of experimental structural durability with a great deal of innovation force and high degree of dynamics. Additional market segments beyond the traditional vehicle and mechanical engineering branches of industry were opened up.The Fraunhofer LBF teams offer services along the entire valueadded chain starting with the material and its processing up to the finished component, the complex system, its qualification with regard to safety and reliability, and performance from product design to verification. Particularly in the area of plastics, the institute provides support at an early stage of the value added chain with polymer synthesis and in-depth material characterization. Comprehensive material and energy-efficient solutions are developed in the areas of vibration technology, lightweight construction, reliability and polymer technology – tailored to the individual needs of each customer. Fraunhofer LBF reaches a number of different markets with its characteristic, wide-reaching competence and service portfolio, particularly in rail transport technology, ship building, aviation, mechanical and plant engineering, energy technology, building industry, medical technology and the chemical industry.

Every placement involves customisation. In practice, this means you avoid getting sixteen CVs on your desk and your IT staff do not have IT vacancies thrown in their lap. entityName: ARPA Puglia - AGENZIA REGIONALE PER LA PREVENZIONE E LA PROTEZIONE AMBIENTALE PUGLIA
entityDescription:
The Regional Agency for the Environmental Prevention and Protection (ARPA Puglia) is the official monitoring authority for Apulia Region in environment management. It is responsible for the monitoring of surface water bodies (Water Framework Directive),
marine waters (Marine Strategy Framework Directive) and bathing waters (Bathing Water Directive) in the Region. ARPA is the regional reference centre for the environmental control of the coastal marine ecosystem, with good international linkages with Countries of the Adriatic coasts. It participated into several research programs on marine pollution and ecology and institutional programs to support the ecosystem and biodiversity safeguard, besides developing plans and projects for the improvement, environmental protection and integrated management of the marine costal area. ARPA is also involved in educational programs contributing to dissemination of knowledge of marine environment and campaigns for increase of public awareness.
ARPA Puglia is involved in control activities on chemical, biological and physical risk factors which could affect all environmental matrices also with the aim at preventing harmful effects for human beings and for the sustainable territorial management. The staff of the Agency actually consists of more than 380 employees (scientific, technical and administrative). The Agency includes the Direction (located in Bari) and six local Departments called DAPs (Bari, Barletta-Andria-Trani, Brindisi, Foggia, Lecce and Taranto).

entityDescription: Statsat AS was established in 2013 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Space Norway AS. The company is established to provide services to government agencies within expanded self-government. This means that the state, through the Ministry of Trade and Industry (NFD), which owns Space Norway AS, through its ownership and control of the company and through the statutes for the two companies, has a continuous control in Statsat AS. The NFD shall, among other things, approve the tasks Statsat takes for state entities. The statutes specify that "the company can only provide services to persons other than such government entities or its shareholders to a very limited extent". Services to non-governmental entities are limited to a certain proportion of turnover, in order for Statsat not to act as a commercial company. As of 2017, this share has been set at 20% in accordance with Norwegian and European rules for companies with extended self-registration.

entityDescription: MITIGA Solutions is a spin-off of the Barcelona Supercomputing Center, a world renowned institution with over two decades of experience in developing and implementing models in the fields of geophysics, volcanology and atmospheric science under one roof. The Center houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe. We bring this expertise together with computational resources to help make the world safer and more resilient against natural hazards. We bridge the gap between scientific research and operational impact, helping our clients manage their risks and make their decision-making more accurate, reliable and timely. We believe science can make the world safer and more resilient against natural hazards. We harness supercomputers and data science/analytics to build whole-cycle solutions for the aviation industry, insurance, and humanitarian sectors, amongst others. We leverage world-class scientists and tech experts to make decision-making more accurate, reliable and timely.AVIATION:MITIGA FLYaware is a decision-making tool that helps aviation stakeholders reduce the impact of volcanic ash, mineral dust, sea salt and other atmospheric hazards. We combine global high-res weather data; flight plan configuration/routes; and engine dose to aerosol contaminants with ICE, our Impact Calculator Engine tool, to inform safer and more efficient air traffic and asset management. MITIGA FLYaware benefits the following aviation stakeholders:- Airlines: improved flight operations, maintenance, asset utilization, and disruption management- Airports: optimized air and ground traffic management- Lessors: asset utilization and optimization- Engine manufacturers: predictive maintenance and asset optimization INSURANCE:In 2018, insured losses from the California Wildfires alone topped $12B. MITIGA E2E Fire System is our disruptive technology that helps manage wildfire risks. It outperforms traditional cat modeling, with greater competitive advantage to its users: insurance/reinsurance, energy companies and governments. It provides critical information in three phases: (i) prevention (live and historical risk indexes); (ii) reaction (fire spread in real time); and (iii) diagnosis (AI and big data, including a social disaster management component).E2E Fire System offers:- High-res Early Warning System that facilitates preventive measures and reduces the impact of a catastrophic event - contrary to current probabilistic assessments that take a long-term view of the wildfire risk in a specified region, based on static catalogues of events..- High-Performance Computing (HPC) that runs hundreds of thousands of simulations a week (up to 30-meter spatial res) to assess the spread probability of wildfires with respect to projected high-res fuel conditions and weather forecasts. It helps determine investment decisions around forest cleaning and land management. HUMANITARIAN:Traditional aid is rarely sufficient to cover humanitarian needs worldwide. So we transfer our industry tech solutions to benefit the humanitarian sector. Seikey Srl, based in Caronno Pertusella (Varese, ITALY), is a company focused on technology solutions through the use of UAVs (Unmanned Aerial Vehicles) or drones, for aerial photography with high accuracy sensors.
Our services, provided in different fields of application, include monitoring and data processing with dedicated software, data management and secure storage, data analysis support, reporting, ENAC (Italian Civil Aviation Authority) regulation compliance and customer service and assistance.
We use photographic and thermal imaging sensors, laser scanners and gas detectors on our drones. These sensors have been designed to inspect, detect and measure structural damage or failures.
We are specialized in surveys that can be very expensive and/or hazardous if carried out manually, especially due to the extreme working conditions required.
Our goal is prevention and preservation by replacing manned tasks with drone missions, which are less expensive, faster, more efficient and much safer.

As a digitization partner of the German economy, Vodafone counts start-ups, medium-sized companies as well as DAX groups among its customers. No other company in Germany networks more people and machines via its mobile network than Vodafone. No other German company offers more gigabit connections in the fixed network than the Düsseldorf-based company. And no other company has more television customers in the country.
With around 49.6 million mobile phone cards, almost 11 million broadband, 14 million television customers and numerous digital solutions, Vodafone Germany with its 16,000 employees generates service revenues of almost 13 billion euros.
As a gigabit company, Vodafone is driving infrastructure expansion in Germany: Today, Vodafone reaches almost 24 million households in its nationwide cable-glass-fibre network, over 11 million of them at gigabit speed. By 2022, Vodafone will provide two thirds of all Germans with Gigabit connections. With its 4G network, Vodafone reaches around 79 million people. Vodafone's machine network (Narrowband IoT) for industry and commerce spans almost 95% of Germany. Since mid-2019, Vodafone has also been operating the first 5G network in Germany and will reach around 10 million people in 2020. In 2021 Vodafone will expand 5G for 20 million people.
Vodafone Germany is the largest national company in the Vodafone Group, one of the largest telecommunications groups in the world, with a 30 % share of total sales. Vodafone has around 625 million mobile, 27 million fixed-line and 22 million TV customers worldwide.
The Revenue is in 2018/2019 was around 11billion Euro

entityDescription:
At Synelixis we aim to pioneer in transformative technologies and deliver customized solutions that empower businesses and communities worldwide. Since our founding in 2007, we have been dedicated to developing effective and high-quality automation and system control solutions. Our commitment extends across key areas, including Corporate Software Development (B2B), Cloud Services, Precision Agriculture, Smart Irrigation, Internet of Things (IoT) integration, and more. 
Driven by innovation and expertise, we continuously advance our capabilities in Big Data analysis, Artificial Intelligence, and Blockchain technologies. Synelixis engineers are dedicated to staying at the forefront of technological advancements, ensuring the delivery of reliable, consistent, and cutting-edge solutions. Our client-centric approach is reflected in the tailored solutions we offer for large Information and Geoinformation systems, coupled with our unwavering commitment to customer satisfaction. Our technology, reliability, and consistency have garnered international recognition, leading to enduring partnerships with industry leaders and esteemed research institutions worldwide. 
Synelixis has established long-term partnerships with major industrial organizations and universities. Synelixis is a registered partner of Cisco Systems and in 2017 signed a business partnership with Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), with which it has participated in numerous competitions and joint exhibitions. As part of the collaboration, Synelixis' SynField precision agriculture solution was integrated with HPE's Universal IoT platform. 
Synelixis has successfully been assigned a variety of projects from the Public Sector or wider Public Sector Organisations and has implemented a plethora of research and development projects, offering services such as new application or platform design/development. Synelixis has also participated and successfully completed a number of European Commission funded programmes and can boast collaboration with important industrial and academic partners in over 50 research projects and has served as Project Coordinator or Technical Coordinator in over 15 projects. 
Synelixis processes are ISO 9001:2015 and ISO/ EC 27001:2017 certified for the quality management and information security of its services. Synelixis guarantees, in any circumstance, the development of optimal and verified solutions that fully meet the requirements of its customers: at Synelixis we manage technology development, time and cost in the best possible way, providing affordable services while keeping strict schedules. Furthermore, Synelixis striving to improve our environmental performance and manage our environmental responsibilities in a systematic way - while contributing to sustainability and providing value for the environment - has adopted the ISO 14001: 2015 standard which sets out the requirements for Synelixis' environmental management system.

entityDescription:
Eurecat is a Research and Technology Organization located in Catalonia (Spain). Eurecat's Digital Technologies Division, based in Barcelona, with 100 professionals specialising in Computer Science, Telecom Engineering, Physics and Mathematics, with ca. 30%
of the staff holding a PhD degree, and a 9.5 M€ turnover (2019). The Division is organised in five Technology Units namely Big Data & Data Science, Smart Management Systems, e-Health, MultiMedia Technologies and IT Security. It performs applied R&D projects under direct contract by Industry and also has a string participation in public funded projectes, particularly EU's H2020.
Data Science and Artificial Intelligence are underlying, transversal technologies with multisector applications (mobility, logistics, retail, agrofood, industrial manufacturing I4.0 and Cibersecurity). The Division's staff consists of skilled data engineers and data scientis with strong background in Big Data technologies and algorithmic knowledge. In terms of facilities the division features a private cluster, an OpenStack based platform developed by Eurecat capable to provision, configure and deploy a whole Big Data stack through an UI assistant matching different project requirements. This platform currently allows to deploy Hadoop environment clusters (including HDFS, YARN, Hive, Pig and Sqoop) as well as Spark, Elasticsearch and Kafka clusters. The Datura hardware resources are 308 CPU 
cores in 11 servers, with 4,48 TB of RAM and 585,12TB of storage space. The network connection within premises is of 20 Gbit/s and located in a private CDP meeting the operational thermal and redundancy requirements. This facility has been recently updated with 8 GPU NVIDIA Cores anhancing the computing power to perform demanding AI, Deep Learning and similar computations.

entityDescription:
RadioPoints s.r.l. is a spin-off company of the University of Rome “Tor Vergata”, founded in year 2020. The mission of the company is to transfer to the appropriate markets some of the most recent cutting-edge research results in Radio Communications.
Its scientific team consists of distinguished researchers with many years of experience in the fields of wireless/satellite communication systems, signal processing, RF sensing/localization/tomography.
Notwithstanding the young age of the company, its experienced team has already taken part in several projects for Italian and European customers, including:

- Projects funded by the European Space Agency (ESA): ARIADNA extended study named “The Flower Constellation Set and its Possible Applications”, in 2006. Multipurpose Constellation project, in 2009. TESHEALTH (Telemedicine Services for Health) project, from 2010 to 2011. AIS End-to-End Testbed Development and "Miniaturized Low-Weight Space Antenna for AIS VHF Applications, from 2012 to 2014.

- Projects funded by the Italian Space Agency (ASI): DAVID satellite mission (DAta and Video Interactive Distribution) during the year 2003; WAVE satellite mission (W-band Analysis and VErification) during the year 2004; FLORAD (Micro-satellite FLOwer Constellation of millimeter-wave RADiometers for the Earth and space Observation at regional scale) during the year 2008; CRUSOE (CRUising in Space with Out-of- body Experiences) during the years 2011/2012. TESEI (Development of a GNSS multifunctional and reconfigurable terminal).

- Project jointly funded by ASI and ESA: Alphasat “Aldo Paraboni” Payload (Technology Demonstration Payload – TDP 5) scientific experiments for broadband satellite communications in Q/V band.

- Projects funded by the European Commission: MAGNET (My personal Adaptive Global NET) European FP6 integrated project, from January 2004 to December 2005; SatNEx European network of excellence, from January 2004 to December 2005, MAGNET Beyond European FP6 integrated project, from January 2006 to June 2008; QV-LIFT, H2020-COMPET-2016 Project.

- Projects funded by the Italian Ministry of Research (MIUR): SALICE (Satellite-Assisted LocalIzation and Communication systems for Emergency services), from October 2008 to September 2010; ICONA (Integration of Communication and Navigation services) from January 2006 to December 2007, SHINES (Satellite and HAP Integrated NEtworks and Services) from January 2003 to December 2004, CABIS (CDMA for Broadband mobile terrestrial-satellite Integrated Systems) from January 2001 to December 2002.

entityDescription:
Machine Prognostics (MP) is a Norwegian company developing machine monitoring systems able to monitor critical and complex assets, e.g. ship engine propulsion gearbox, for the maritime and O&G industry. Our rapid and ambitious go-to-market strategy relies on a technological cross-innovation from the aerospace sector. Our novel sensor and algorithms initially developed for monitoring helicopters critical components, e.g. helicopter main rotor gearbox, are re-engineered to be used with maritime assets in our product called “Foresight Maritime” referred to as Foresight in this proposal. This cross-innovation approach dramatically increases the commercial potential of MP in the Maritime sector by introducing disruptive yet, trustable aerospace-proven/certified algorithms embedded into our sensors. 

Our vision is to empower maintenance crews all over the world by providing them with reliable actionable information about the health status of their machinery; anyone can understand Foresight data without prior training. Our user interface has been designed around the maintainer for ease of use and to provide clear, unambiguous information. When components show wears, Foresight removes the guesswork by providing time estimates of equipment remaining useful life and can even automatically trigger work-order when connected to the maintenance planning system of the ship/platform.

entityDescription:
Spade is a creative agency specialised in product design for Space exploration. 
We imagine new ergonomics for microgravity, and give shape to human culture outside of Earth.

We have entered a new space era : the upcoming private space sector and the perspective of a journey to Mars are leading to a commercial revolution in Space. The future pioneers won’t just be military or scientific, but rather philanthropists, explorers, voyageurs and even tourists, having much different journeys than yesterday’s astronauts. 

The popular imaginary would let us think that space stations are slick white minimalist environments, where everything is integrated and ergonomic. It is in fact, quite the opposite : at present, Space is surprisingly crowded with dysfunctional objects manufactured for a world with gravity, where weight and direction applied. As a result, practical problems continuously arise and are currently solved with black duct tape and velcro strips: the astronaut’s best friends.

We, at Spade, believe in better planned environments, cleverly-designed objects, and specific ergonomics for manned spaceflights.

entityDescription:
Surrey NanoSystems began as a spin-out from the University of Surrey's Advanced Technology Institute in December 2006. Surrey NanoSystems initial goal was the development of commercial systems for producing carbon nanotubes at temperatures compatible with back end silicon processing. The company's initial financial backer was the IP Group PLC and The University of Surrey.
The first development project was the creation of a range of nanomaterial growth platforms known as NanoGrowth. This work - and the focus on producing materials to support the continued scaling of semiconductor devices - led to an evolution in the capability of the CVD deposition tools under the NanoGrowth Catalyst brand.
In 2012, Surrey NanoSystems' low temperature nanomaterial growth capability led to a project partnership to develop super-black coatings to enhance the performance of sensitive electro-optical imaging systems in a satellite application. This partnership with NPL and ABSL SPACE PRODUCTS resulted in the creation of Vantablack - Vertically Aligned Nanotube Array BLACK - an array of carbon nanotubes with remarkable properties for trapping light. 
Today Vantablack is now a globally recognised super-black coatings brand that stands for ultimate performance and quality of service in critical technology driven industries. The original CVD Vantablack coating is no longer manufactured as it has been superseded by Vantablack spray coatings that solve serious challenges in space, optics, automotive sensing and aesthetics.
We currently operate out of two world class R&D and production facilities in the UK based near Brighton, East Sussex. Vantablack coatings are the sole focus of the company.

entityDescription:
The Basque language is the oldest living language in Europe. Most linguistics, experts and researchers say that the origins date back to the Neolithic, but there is evidence that it could be even older. In fact, it could be at the seeds of articulate language. URA (that means water in basque) won´t transform the way we communicate, but the way that we transport in-space.

URA Thrusters combines all the skills and IP from the Propulsion team of AVS and Imperial College as well as the expertise in production, integration, quality/product assurance and industrialisation of complex Space and scientific equipment. URA is formed by four key assets that will disrupt the status-quo of current propulsion systems by the use of the ultimate green propellant: WATER.

Satellite primes have a strong interest in developing alternative “green” propulsion solutions, due to the prospect of Hydrazine regulation, cost reduction, and operational benefits from eliminating this toxic fuel. Due to launch ride-share restrictions, costs and mass/volume constraints, the small satellite propulsion market will be completely dominated by green propellant systems.
Water, as a high-density (liquid) storable, completely non-hazardous, low-cost fuel is of particular interest. It facilitates ride-share launches without the increased risks to other payloads from corrosive, highly pressurised, or high-energy density alternatives. The ability to load propellant at the spacecraft or propulsion system assembly facility instead of the launch site saves time, reduces risk and cost of the integration.

Handling costs for green propellants can be two thirds of the cost for hydrazine, amounting to cost reductions of order $100-500k depending of the type of spacecraft and mission operations. In the long term, water-based thrusters will gain a decisive market advantage when combined with asteroid mining or refuelling ventures, either in-orbit or making use of in-situ resources for interplanetary missions.

AQASS is focussed on managing and understanding aquatic systems, water resources management and governance and supply, ecology and environment such as pollution, and general human impacts, scientific research to support policy documents, due diligence and project oversight, and managing field surveys and subsequent spatial and statistical data analysis. entityDescription:
Plantae provides a real, simple and technological solution for irrigated agriculture and professional gardening, with Radio Frequency sensors to inform customers about water necessities and crop data, all managed in real time from a web/app site HaaS.

IoT solution based on moisture, temperature and conductivity measurement sensors at different depths that send data through a standard cellular communication (GPRS) gateway to the HaaS. Farmer and other customers can access to the administration panel and receive alerts and reports.
 

The solution offers a number of different sensors connected to a gateway by a radio frequency communication protocol (LoRa), with very efficient and very low rates in electronic components. The gateway (powered by a solar panel) send all data to the cloud, where farmers can customize their fields and program different alerts and reports about water needs and state of crops.

Sensors are also customized with some algorithms and other agro analysis in relation to soil texture and other conductivity parameters, which will be enriched and improved extracting data from satellite sources like Copernicus. All managed from the platform to help customers to water depending on their crop, location and kind of irrigation strategy. 

Other skills and Strenghts:

-	LOW COST SOLUTION: product price setup pack (4 moisture sensors) by <500€, HaaS yearly fee 395€/year; 
-	PLUG & PLAY: Technology: no wires (LoRa Technology, NB-IoT testing through IoT Activation Programme Telefonica), easy to install.
-	ALERTS AND REPORT: HaaS: water and climatological reports, water alerts, easy to use.
-	SCALABLE: start with one sensor and Scale in irrigated lands whenever your needs are
-	DIFFERENT RANGE OF SENSORS: Plantae is easy to customize for different depth depending on crops (e.g. pistachio from 20cm-60cm moisture measurements, beet from 15-30cm...).
-	RELIABLE: More than 100 customers in several crops and locations. Partners strategy running.
-	Customization: sensors are customized with mathematics algorithms and Artificial Intelligence depending on crop, soil and customer water strategy.
-	CE Mark

entityDescription:
The Parco archeologico del Colosseo
The Parco archeologico del Colosseo was established by DM no. 15 of January 12, 2017 , with the purpose of creating an institution endowed with special autonomy to ensure the protection and valorisation of the central archaeological area of Rome and to implement the agreement underwritten between the MiBACT and the City of Rome on April 21, 2015 .
The territory within the remit of the Park contains both areas and monuments of direct state competence (Colosseum, Domus Aurea, Arch of Constantine and Meta Sudans, the Roman Forum and the Palatine), both in Rome (Circus Maximus, Imperial Forums), as well as the rich ecclesiastical patrimony consisting of the churches that stand on Via dei Fori Imperiali and on the Palatine and its slopes (such as the basilica of Santi Cosma and Damiano, San Bonaventura and Sant’Anastasia al Palatino), owned by various organisations (Fondo Edifici di Culto of the Ministry of the Interior, Vicariate of Rome and others).
Mission
The mission of the Parco archeologico del Colosseo is a constant work of education to memory, expressed in its relationship with an extremely varied public and a commitment to establishing a continuous relationship with the new generations, so relating the origins of our history to the future through the connection with Rome’s whole cultural system.
To achieve these objectives the Park is committed to the protection, conservation, research and valorisation of its archaeological, monumental and landscape heritage.
The effort to convey a knowledge of places to the public also takes place through the use of new digital technologies capable of communicating the complex character of the Park with a more comprehensible and immediate approach.
Its autonomous management gives the Park a more direct approach to its current and potential partners, with a view to increasingly being a driving force for the economy of the city and the country.

SADL is the acronym for ‘Spatial Applications Division Leuven’.
SADL is a long standing cooperative initiative of several research groups of the Department of Earth & Environmental Sciences of KU Leuven. The overall topic is the Geographic Information Science and Technologies (GI S&T) and their applications for physical land management and socio-economic assessments.
SADL paves the way to transfer and validate research expertise and results in civil society. To this end, research projects are conducted and scientific consultancies are performed for public authorities and industry. Moreover post- and para-academic educational and training programmes are offered. This set of activities is completed by participation in more fundamental research programmes and academic education so that a seamless transition is possible between theory and applications.
SADL has within KU Leuven the statute of R&D Division.

entityDescription:
Plant-for-the-Planet children and youth initiative was launched in January 2007. At the end of his school presentation about the current Climate crisis, nine-year-old Felix Finkbeiner announced his vision to his classmates:
"Let’s plant one million trees in every country on earth!"

The goal of the children and youth initiative is to inspire people around the globe to plant a trillion trees. Trees are the cheapest and most effective means of binding CO2 
One trillion trees could buy us 15 years to reduce greenhouse gas emissions to zero and mitigate the climate crisis. 

In 2011, Felix spoke at the UN Headquarters in New York and announced the Trillion Tree Campaign. The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) handed over the long-established Billion Tree Campaign, along with the official world tree counter, to Plant-for-the-Planet. The former children, now young adults, developed the Plant-for-the-Planet App to motivate others to get involved in planting.
So far, more than 13.6 billion trees in 193 countries have been planted and reported to the children of Plant-for-the-Planet. 

The children teach and empower others to become Climate Justice Ambassadors. More than 88,000 children from 74 countries are already participating. 

On the Yucatan Peninsula in Mexico, Plant-for-the-Planet plants a new tree every 15 seconds. This project demonstrates just how easy it is to make planting trees so effective on a large scale. The initiative uses the
Plant-for-the-Planet App, products and campaigns (such as "Stop talking. Start planting.") in order to plant trees and motivate others to get involved in planting.

Company description: TopView S.r.l. is an Innovative UAS Engineering SME founded in 2013. Initially focused on the development and implementation of proprietary drones, today the company adopts a broader strategy, mainly engaging in activities for the integration of drones into business processes. The core business is made up of three macro-areas:
1.Specialized flight operations. Optical and thermographic inspections, and aerial photogrammetry, as well as experimental operations in complex scenarios;
2.Design and implementation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS); TopView designs and prototypes both UAS and payloads with specific sensors;
3.U-space and digital aviation: digital products and services for drones integration in the VLL airspace.
Over the years, the company's activity has involved the design and implementation of complex systems, such as payloads and sensors for drones in different application niches, integrating them with customized IoT sensors. This led to present PV-Watch (the first inspection service of photovoltaic systems with drones) at the Solar Expo in Milan in 2014. In the same year, the company received authorization for UAS flight operations by the Italian Civil Aviation Authority (ENAC) for experimental activities.
In 2015 The Company received its first Horizon 2020 Grant with EASY-PV project, aimed at reducing the costs of solar power plants inspections. Since then, TopView has been involved in many R&D projects by various organizations.
In 2016, together with a few other Italian companies (Leonardo, ENAV, IDS, EuroUSC Italia) The Company participated in the definition of U-space, the set of services aimed at regulating the safe and efficient access of drones in European airspace. With the European projects, the research activity has been consolidated and has been recognized by key players in the aerospace sector, including SESAR JU, Eurocontrol and Leonardo. Over the years, TopView has gained specific expertise on EGNSS downstream applications and U-space domain, participating in many projects as Partner or Coordinator with the project CERTIFLIGHT EUSPA (2022-ongoing). The project proposes to use the Galileo OSNMA function to certify the flight tracks of drones and ultralight aircraft within VLL airspace, developing a first prototype of U-space Legal Recording service;
In many of these projects, TopView has contributed to develop services and prototypes, also leading the related field testing and validation campaigns.In 2020, despite the effects of the pandemic, the company consolidated its mission with new research projects and consulting services, and with an important strategic collaboration agreement with Telespazio and D-flight (ENAV). Thanks to these R&D efforts and the know-how acquired, in 2021 TopView was the first company to concretely adhere to the "U-space Manifesto" launched by D-Flight, the Italian provider of unmanned air traffic management services. In fact, it has released a first version of Pollicino ™, the proprietary drone tracker that allows drones to interface with the U-space services of the national provider, promoting situational awareness and safety of operations in VLL (Very Low Level) airspace. Internal R&D activities also include Urban Air Mobility, with a patented concpet of a drone taxi for the transport of passengers.

entityDescription: Europe's Spaceport is situated in the northeast of South America in French Guiana, an overseas department of France. In 1964 the French Government chose Kourou, from 14 other sites, as a base from which to launch its satellites. When the European Space Agency came into being in 1975, the French Government offered to share its Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) with ESA. For its part, ESA approved funding to upgrade the launch facilities at the CSG to prepare the Spaceport for the Ariane launchers under development. Since then, ESA has continued to fund two thirds of the spaceport's annual budget to finance the operations and the investments needed to maintain the top level services provided by the Spaceport. ESA also finances new facilities, such as launch complexes and industrial production facilities, for new launchers such as Vega-C and Ariane 6.

entityDescription:
Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne is a higher education establishment, part of Université Paris-Saclay, which gathers 15% of France research.
Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne cutting-edge research’s strength concerns Genomics and post-genomics for precision medicine and genome-related industry (innovative biotherapies, synthetic biology…), Applied mathematics for finance and genomics, Information and communication technology (ICT), as well as research in Robotics and for Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) or Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV), and Space technology. Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne extends its research with applications in close partnerships with two main R&D Clusters: Genopole the first French biocluster dedicated to innovative biotechnologies (see https://join-the-biocluster.genopole.fr/A-Business-Accelerator.html) and the Cluster “Drones Paris-Region” dedicated to UAS (see http://www.clusterdronesparisregion.com/), and in the framework of the French government program Careers and Qualifications Campus – Aeronautics and Space, currently under development where Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne is the leader.
Humanities and Social Sciences encompasses Economics, Law, Sociology and History. where research focus on market balance, compared public and private law, sociology of work, visual sociology and arts and music.
Finally, Université d’Évry-Val-d’Essonne’s campus life is vibrant and multicultural. Seminars, exhibitions, arts and cultural activities, sports: everything is in place to foster a dynamic campus at the heart of the Évry community. Strong links with local actors make the Université d‘Évry-Val-d’Essonne a privileged partner in numerous solidarity and innovative projects aspiring to create the society and the world of tomorrow

entityDescription:
Heraklion is the capital of Crete and one of the Mediterranean region's most fascinating and vibrant cities. The Chandax of the Arabs and Byzantines, the Candia of the Venetians, was one of the island's major ports and markets, and at times one of the most economically active towns in the wider region. Heraklion is the fourth largest city in Greece. According to the results of the 2011 census, the municipality's population is 173,993 people and it extends over an area of 684.3 km2 (264.2 sq mi).
The Municipality of Heraklion employs 751 workers. Heraklion has been selected as one of the Smart21 Communities of 2012, 2013 and 2014 by the Intelligent Community Forum and has been awarded European distinction and the second European Prize in the Dosta!-Congress Prize as recognition of the excellent efforts and its municipal program for the implementation of its social services pertaining to social inclusion and anti-discrimination. Furthermore Heraklion nominated Best City Destination and Gold Award Winner in Greek Travel Awards in Stockholm, was also one of the Winner for UNESCO Learning Cities Award of the 2019, with its ‘Fit for All’ programme, through which Heraklion has found an innovative and fun way to bring its citizens and the refugees residing in the city closer together by promoting equity and inclusion through sports and educational activities based on subjects such as local culture and tradition.

Thanks to AQCLab's assessments, organizations can not only evaluate and improve the quality of their software and data, but also obtain a quality certification in ISO/IEC 25000, issued by a certification body such as AENOR.

ENGIE Impact applies data analytics, multi-disciplinary expertise and global reach to accelerate sustainability transformation of organizations around the world. entityDescription:
The Chair for Circuit Design and Network Theory is dedicated to the design and modeling of integrated circuits in CMOS, BiCMOS and III/V technologies, as well as emerging "beyond moore" nano-technologies, e.g. those based on carbon nanotubes, silicon nanowires and organic as well as polymeric devices.
The focus is on analysis and design of analog and mixed-signal circuits. Other areas of work include the design of FPGA, PCBs and hybrid assemblies, digital signal processing and algorithms for complete information systems. Applications include high-frequency systems, wireless communication from low-frequency-range up to 220 GHz, optical data transmission up to 80 Gbit/s, high-precision positioning systems, energy-adaptive systems with intelligent, dynamic control and wake-up features as well as energy harvesting. In addition, the professorship has experience in the development and optimization of high-end audio systems and speakers.

entityDescription: Port of Tallinn is the biggest port authority in Estonia and its strategic goal is to develop the competitiveness of Estonia as a maritime country. Its harbours are navigable and easily accessible through the year and deep enough to receive all vessels passing through the Danish Straits. Estonia’s geographical location is favourable for handling both north-south and east-west passenger and cargo flows. Tallinna Sadam owns two passenger harbours (the Old City Harbour and the Saaremaa Harbour) and two cargo harbours (the Muuga Harbour and the Paldiski South Harbour). In terms of the number of passengers served, Tallinn Old City Harbour is the third-largest harbour on the Baltic Sea (after Helsinki and Stockholm) and the fourth-largest in Northern Europe. The Muuga Harbour is Estonia’s largest cargo harbour. Tallinna Sadam offers port services as a landlord port, i.e. it owns, administers and develops berths and port basins, leases land to cargo operators, organises vessel traffic in port basins and ensures safe navigation in port waters. Tallinna Sadam owns passenger terminals and other facilities required for passenger service but cargo harbour superstructure belongs to cargo operators. Waste management service in harbours is provided by AS Green Marine, an associate of Tallinna Sadam that offers innovative waste handling solutions.

entityDescription:
CATUAV is the European private drone company with longest trajectory. CATUAV capabilities include design, development and integration of special purpose platforms and Unmanned Aerial Systems as well as Ground Control Stations, sensor characterization and integration.
Our technology covers the full chain value, from UAV manufacturing and operation to image processing, offering a whole solution to most Drone Applications needs. 
Since 2000 CATUAV has been carrying on a continuous R&D process that has led to several complete and functional UAV systems. Some of our main developments are 12 different UAV platforms, 3 Ground Control Stations, Communication & Control and telemetry software and hardware and mission specific flight planning software.
CATUAV has been awarded by numerous institutions being the most relevant GSA Galileo Masters, Social Innovation Drone Award, Drones for Good and TOP10 of the world recognition by Drone Industry Insights.
BCN Drone Center are the drone test site facilities built on 2014 and owned by CATUAV. They count with an official segregated airspace (TSA-31), runway and bioclimatic building. They are located just one hour away from Barcelona city center and its international airport. Meteorological conditions allow UAV flight testing more than 300 days a year. These facilities offer everything needed for UAV design, development, testing and certification. More than 1,000 users from 90 nationalities have performed testing and activities in the facilities.

entityDescription:
Nimbus Srl is an aeronautical company, certified UNI EN ISO 9001: 2015 and ISO 45001:2018 which designs and manufactures innovative Unmanned Aerial System (UAS). 
Nimbus is an operator authorized by the National Civil Aviation Authority (ENAC) and is inscribed under the Italian Federation of Aerospace, Defense and Security (AIAD). Besides, since his home-made products and licenses, Nimbus SRL is one of the companies that joins “Exclusive Brand Torino”, an institution that gather the most innovative companies in Piemonte. 
Moreover, Nimbus has been certified as a recognized entity by ENAV (Italian Civil Aviation Authority) and has been authorized to operate as an examination center (OPEN A2 ONLINE PROCTORED) for the issue of the UAS Remote Pilot Competence Certificate in the OPEN A2 subcategory, as required by Reg. (EU) no. 2019/947. 
Nimbus’s team consists of high-qualified mechanical, mechatronic, SW, electronic and aerospace engineer, which designed and produced our Nimbus PPL series 418 (quadcopter), Nimbus 612 EVO Plus XL (esacopter) – also with DDSS configuration - the “Nimbus VTOL” and the “Nimbus box”. 
Our UAS can address different scenarios, as visible-light video footage, visual and infra- red survey, structural analysis of industrial construction, agro-tech activities, VOR and ILS operations in airport facilities, high-voltage power lines inspections, delivery activities in the healthcare sector and many others. 
Our professional UAS are distinguished from the rest of the market for the construction and for the flight management features that meet the active and passive safety priorities: the use of soft material, propeller protection, no sharp edges, four/six dual- power motors, proprietary electronics with in-flight safety and emergency management controls. 
Moreover, they are equipped with pilot stations made by two remote commands (main and secondary), which are fitted with telemetry station and PC dedicated to control:
- the remote pilot aircraft;
- the different Payload typologies.

entityDescription: BABLE GmbH is a for-profit SME founded in May 2017. BABLE GmbH creates it revenues from three different income stream (1) listing fees for company products on the BABLE Platform, (2) subscription fees for the automated services in the BABLE Toolbox (similar to an app-store) and (3) consulting fees for supporting cities and companies directly in their path towards implementation projects. BABLE GmbH offers an exchange platform for the Smart City community and provides a digital toolkit to facilitate implementation of smart and sustainable solutions in cities. It enables innovative companies, public authorities, and experts to exchange information, ideas, products, services, and Use Cases as reference projects. The BABLE Platform provides neutrally described Smart City Solutions as blueprints and complementary services to its community. The platform provides transparency and matches the demand and supply side. The idea is to enhance economic potential, reduce costs and to open new business opportunities. Some of the features offered include: market consultation, technical expertise, innovative procurement, promotion mechanisms (own Use Cases, local SMEs etc.), building capacities and providing space for dialogue with other cities, companies, and research institutes.

The
Environmental Protection Agency of Aosta Valley (ARPAVdA) is a
multidisciplinary agency dedicated to environment protection and
monitoring (air and water quality, soil contamination, environmental
noise, waste, resources management, renewable energies, ...). Since
2003 ARPAVdA has structured a research unit focused on Climate Change
Impacts on the mountains. The Climate Change Unit conducts studies on
the cryosphere and the biosphere based on the integration of field
observations, remote sensing, and modeling. Considering the
cryosphere, ARPAVdA research activities are focused on glacier mass
balance, snow hydrology (snow water equivalent modeling at regional
and watershed-scale) and permafrost (thermal state monitoring, rock
glaciers movements). Considering the biosphere ARPAVdA works on
ecosystem carbon balance, ecosystem response to climate
change/extremes and vegetation phenology. In particular, ARPAVdA runs
a CO2 flux site (IT-Tor) belonging to the ICOS (www.icos-ri.eu/) and
Fluxnet (fluxnet.fluxdata.org/) networks. ARPAVdA observation sites
contribute to several international networks like GLORIA, LTER,
GTN-P, Phenocam,…. Since the last five years, ARPAVdA is also
devoted to the analysis of climate change impacts on socio-economic
sectors (such as agriculture, tourism, natural resources management,
...) Since several years CCU is collaborating with international
research groups as well as local stakeholders (protected areas, NGOs,
…). ARPA VdA is highly active and successful in acquiring external
funding from national and international sources. Concerning EU
programs, since 2008 ARPAVdA has been involved in more than 30
European funded Projects (Interreg, Life, FP7, ..).

entityDescription: IFSTTAR became the new Université Gustave Eiffel on the 1st January 2020. The French Institute of Science and Technology for Transport, Development and Networks (IFSTTAR), Université Paris-Est Marne-la-Vallée (UPEM) and four selective higher education institutes are merging to create a research and training centre for cities and regions. Cities and regions are constantly changing. On this basis, 6 training and research institutions, which specialise in the fields of sustainable cities, are combining their expertise and know-how to create a university of international standing and of a new type: Université Gustave Eiffel. entityDescription:
Nueva Mater Dei is a licensed nursing home located in Spain.The Nursing Home allows residents to enjoy the atmosphere of their wonderful care environment, with the tranquillity of feeling totally secure and cared for.
Nueva Mater Dei provides seniors with exceptional and high-quality nursing care. In a warm, inviting atmosphere they offer both short term rehabilitation and long term care. The company offers 24/7 specialized healthcare and residential services to elderly patients. With its personalized approach, Nueva Mater Dei increases the quality of life of its residents significantly. From rehabilitation services to memory care, their residents reap the benefits of having a compassionate and resourceful staff that caters to their every need. They stand on the pillar of superior senior care in a nurturing environment, which combined with their facility's advanced services and amenities, offer their residents and their families peace of mind.
The entire complex has 5.000 m2. It is made up of large gardens to walk in nearby. The building’s structure allows a convenient distribution of care zones, common areas and private spaces, in order to achieve a fulfilling degree of serenity and independence at the residents’ rooms.
Comfortable and specially designed furnishings invites to a clean and cosy ambience. The residence´s classic interior is designed to be both homely and comfortable, with spacious lounge areas for socialising and enjoy regular entertainments. A luminous dining room with appetizing cooked food. To enjoy our “Spanish good weather” the building offers large terraces.
All of our facilities are adapted to older people. Our residents can relax and enjoy themselves with family or friends, or take the opportunity to meet new people.
We are proud of the nursing home environments we create for the people we support. It’s why we are constantly looking to improve our existing buildings while also investing in innovation. Our Nursing Home lead the sector in environmentally friendly design and are built well above the specifications required by the regulatory standards. Rooms are spacious and airy. Careful interior design gives an elegant but homely feel, which is comfortable and friendly. Nueva Mater Dei recognizes that social, economic and environmental factors interact and influence the exposure of individuals and ultimately coincide to determine population health.
Nueva Mater Dei addresses a number of issues, including management of chronic conditions, social inclusion, access to online services and management of daily activities, which can help older people stay more socially active and provide support to those with dementia. Study and analyse the emergence of innovative ICT-based products, services and systems for ageing well and managing chronic diseases, including innovative systems to control the COVID-19.
We are active in the wider world of active and healthy ageing, and have many partnerships across the sector that support older people and help to increase activity in the healthy ageing market.

Nueva Mater Dei provides seniors with exceptional and high-quality nursing care. In a warm, inviting atmosphere they offer both short term rehabilitation and long term care. The company offers 24/7 specialized healthcare and residential services to elderly patients. With its personalized approach, Nueva Mater Dei increases the quality of life of its residents significantly. From rehabilitation services to memory care, their residents reap the benefits of having a compassionate and resourceful staff that caters to their every need. They stand on the pillar of superior senior care in a nurturing environment, which combined with their facility's advanced services and amenities, offer their residents and their families peace of mind.

Comfortable and specially designed furnishings invites to a clean and cosy ambience. The residence´s classic interior is designed to be both homely and comfortable, with spacious lounge areas for socialising and enjoy regular entertainments. A luminous dining room with appetizing cooked food. To enjoy our “Spanish good weather” the building offers large terraces.
All of our facilities are adapted to older people. Our residents can relax and enjoy themselves with family or friends, or take the opportunity to meet new people.
We are proud of the nursing home environments we create for the people we support. It’s why we are constantly looking to improve our existing buildings while also investing in innovation. Our Nursing Home lead the sector in environmentally friendly design and are built well above the specifications required by the regulatory standards. Rooms are spacious and airy. Careful interior design gives an elegant but homely feel, which is comfortable and friendly. Nueva Mater Dei recognizes that social, economic and environmental factors interact and influence the exposure of individuals and ultimately coincide to determine population health.
Nueva Mater Dei addresses a number of issues, including management of chronic conditions, social inclusion, access to online services and management of daily activities, which can help older people stay more socially active and provide support to those with dementia. Study and analyse the emergence of innovative ICT-based products, services and systems for ageing well and managing chronic diseases, including innovative systems to control the COVID-19.
We are active in the wider world of active and healthy ageing, and have many partnerships across the sector that support older people and help to increase activity in the healthy ageing market.

entityDescription:
FullBrand was born as a spin-off of Little Bull of the Armando Testa group to design and implement marketing and communication strategies based on Brand Experience and Brand Innovation. Through Brand Experience services, FullBrand develops an alternative communication to the traditional Above the line approach, coordinating the different languages to use, creating and producing content. Through Brand Innovation services, FullBrand imagines, designs and creates prototypes of products or services for its customers according to its Innovation model defined Application Transfer. FullBrand has offices in Italy and Brazil. Fullbrand has already developed several solutions using proprietary and open source AR and VR Technologies, for immersive reality devices and stereoscopic monitors, in single player or multi-user mode, using gamification techniques. Fullbrand is focused on developing VR and AR solutions for staff training and is developing its experience in telemedicine applications.
From 2016 until today, in collaboration with the Municipality of Sestriere (Turin) we have provided telemedicine services to residents and tourists of a mountain centre located at 2,000 metres, which passes from a resident population of less than a thousand to a population of 35,000 during the winter holidays and which is 45 minutes from the first hospital. After these years of experience in the sector, the conclusion is that the solution for the current needs of the Health Service is not Telemedicine as such, but the virtualization of the health service of which telemedicine is one of the tools. The exclusively telemedicine approach is ideological, that of virtualization is concrete. Virtualization minimizes the infrastructure and works on all possibilities, like a pianist on the piano keyboard. Virtualization is necessary because the superstructure has become predominant over the structure and is suffocating it. It is a matter of managing the health resources needed to provide the service where it is needed, focusing on prevention (e.g. mass dermatological examinations) and self-organization of subjects (e.g. non-competitive sports medicine examinations promoted by mothers). Sestriere's experience has made this clear. We must not have the taboo of a direct visit. Because what we have shown is how service management virtualization works in terms of service delivery. This trend is perfectly in line with the general virtualization of services. In commerce (and Amazon proves it) all channels are used to provide the user with the best service at the best price.

Feedback Italia is an Italian private company founded in 1999 in Moncalieri, Northern Italy, and specialized in secure real-time communication since its foundation: audio, video and data. As the Internet was not publicly available at the beginning of our business experience, we immediately specialized in developing solutions specifically tailored for satellite communication, with particular attention regarding bandwidth optimization and utilization. For example, our systems still natively support MULTICAST and any combination with UNICAST which may be necessary, without the need for additional external devices.
Thanks for this granular management of the network resources, our frameworks have been widely deployed at Universities, Governments and Health Organizations worldwide, by assuring their operativity even in the most demanding operational scenarios.
Moreover, supported by intense collaboration with some Italian Universities, we have acquired vast know-how in terms of security, including the hardware. Our solutions are natively compliant to the GDPR regulation and implement the highest standard available, as the usage of military-grade encryption algorithms and the development and production in Italy of specific secure devices according to the customer’s needs (smartphones, laptops, and wearables).

Più Sviluppo was founded in 2010 by Francesco Marchis. The
company’s mission is based on the fundamental belief that it is necessary to
create “Development” (hence, sviluppo
in Italian) for the business system, in order to give value to their ideas and
their business.



Più Sviluppo model is based on the concrete paradigm of “doing”,
and allows companies to attract and aggregate all the necessary skills for the
development of a complete business project from the start and in a fast way,
limiting investments through the transformation in equity of the contributions
provided to the project be them workforce, tangible or intangible assets.



Each company is unique, and as such it must always be
treated and managed. This is why Più Sviluppo method cannot be standardized. In
this way, Più Sviluppo solves concrete problems, simplifying bureaucracy,
certifying companies according to regulations, finding non-refundable resources
and managing innovation, in a logic oriented towards results and objectives.


In the last years Più Sviluppo devoted itself to
gather competencies in order to tackle projects in the fields of production
automation, e-learning, satellite-based telecommunications and others.

entityDescription:
ACIF-CCIM (Industrial and Commercial Association of Funchal - Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Madeira) is a business association and also Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Madeira Archipelago. It is a private and non-profit multisectoral Association, founded in 1836.
ACIF-CCIM represents employers and companies acting in Madeira Island, defending its interests. As Economic Partner, our action is directed at up-holding the free competition between companies.
This Association has about 800 associated companies, from all sectors (commerce, industry, services and tourism) most of which are SME. To better protect the interests of its members and provide services according to their needs, ACIF-CCIM has 17 employees in addition, spread over six departments (Events and Communication; Training and Projects; Associates and Partnerships; Legal; Administrative and Financial; ICT).
ACIF-CCIM is responsible for developing a variety of activities, in particular a wide range of business services, including information and support for businesses; vocational training; company missions; fairs; conferences; events; representation and defend of the interests of its members; reinforcing the role of business associations on both national and international levels, among others.
We have developed, over the years, several projects for companies, with particular emphasis on pioneering initiatives in the tourism sector - particularly in the area of energy efficiency, training-consulting, e-commerce and applications for mobile devices, trade and services, among others. They were co-financed in several funds like EEA Grants, CIP, Interreg MAC, Interreg Atlantic Area, COSME, H2020 and Structural Funds.
With regard to our participation in European networks ACIF-CCIM began its experience in 1989 with Euro Info Centre and has continued in 2008 as Enterprise Europe Network partner, until now. ACIF-CCIM has also represented in Madeira Europe Direct network.
