entityDescription:
Caledonian Photonics Limited is a micro-SME in the field of robust, miniaturised solid-state lasers. The company has expertise in design for manufacture, reliability and environmental insensitivity, with experience of the academic, scientific and defence markets. 

For the last 2 years, Caledonian Photonics has been involved in the development of narrow-linewidth lasers targeting the Quantum Technologies (QT) market. These developments have led to Caledonian Photonics' involvement in 3 Innovate-UK funded projects to further develop this technology and allow QT applications such as cold-atom gravimetry, inertial navigation and timing to leave the laboratory and operate robustly in the real-world.

In 2018 Caledonian Photonics won a DASA contract titled “Low Size, Weight, Power and Cost Monolithic Lasers For Man-Portable Applications”. This contract enabled Caledonian Photonics to demonstrate the production of novel monolithic optical assemblies and their use within laser resonators. Caledonian were subsequently awarded a follow-on contract to apply this technology to OPO systems. 
Dr Stephen Lee, founder and CEO, has 23 years of experience in solid-state lasers and their integration into optical systems. He developed this during his 6 years at Coherent as a senior laser design engineer engaged in new product design and introduction of broadly tunable Ti:Sapphire lasers for bioscience applications. Stephen then spent 10 years at Thales UK in the Defence Lasers product line where he acted as design authority for the defence lasers product line.

entityDescription: RU.DE – Associação de Desenvolvimento Rural / Rural Development Agency) is a private non-profit entity, established on 19th December 1991. It aims to promote the sustainable development of rural areas, as a way of attracting people and new activities, retaining populations and diversifying the social, economic and cultural basis of the Cova da Beira subregion. Its intervention territory is the subregion called Cova da Beira and includes the municipalities of Belmonte, Covilhã and Fundão. This sub-region has a total area of 1.373km2 and a current resident population of 87,471 inhabitants. RU.DE has been implementing the LEADER Programme since 1992. During this period, RU.DE has supported, with the LEADER Programme, more than 400 projects which represented an investment of more than 30 million euros in the territory. In the present programming period (2014-2020), RU.DE is the manager partner of the Local Action Group (LAG) Cova da Beira 2020. The LAG COVA DA BEIRA 2020 partnership involves 111 organizations representing different areas between the public, private and civil sectors. RUDE's intervention is based on logics of proximity and territorial cohesion, experimentation and innovation and, above all, on participatory methodologies with the involvement of local actors, creating responses to social, environmental and economic challenges. RU.DE is a recognized player in the strategic social and economic definition for the region and generates dynamics in its intervention territory through the generation and monitoring of innovative initiatives, especially on rural development, thus contributing to competitiveness, sustainability of the territories and quality of life for populations.

LuxConnect is a multi-Tier and multi-tenant Data Center facility and dark fiber provider. It was founded in 2006 as a private limited company owned by the Luxembourg State. LuxConnect acts as a facilitator and incubator in the ICT industry and has been instrumental in the creation of LU-CIX, the Luxembourg Commercial Internet Exchange. 
Being carrier neutral, 37 carriers are currently colocated within LuxConnect Data Centers. Due to its central position in Western Europe, LuxConnect tenants enjoy very low latency connections to Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Paris and London. Hence, data stored within LuxConnect Data Centers can be delivered fast to the bulk of all the major European consumer markets. 
LuxConnect’s optical fiber backbone encompasses over 1,500 km of fiber throughout Luxembourg. The backbone redundantly connects all commercial Data Centers in Luxembourg and gives telecom operators a choice of 12 country outbreaks to interconnect to and from Luxembourg.

In 2019 LuxConnect founded the company LuxProvide which will own and operate in 2021 the High-Performance Computer (HPC) Meluxina.

entityDescription:
TravelAi is a European Space Agency BIC programme Alumni that relies on the use of Galileo and GPS technologies. With a multi-country team based in the UK (HQ), Portugal and Finland, the all engineering team has built a Technology Stack to help understand how citizens around the world use transport systems. Be that by public or private transit, human powered or motorised and without the limitations of geographic borders or even requiring CAPEX heavy physical or sensor infrastructure because we leverage the ubiquity of smartphones.

This automatic software development kit (SDK) can be embedded into existing Android and iOS apps to allow our B2B clients to identify the route, mode of transport and time that their customers travel so that they can better meet their needs and optimise their services for them. Including travel by car, bus, bike, train, tram, metro, plane and by foot. This technology is used by transport service providers such as train and bus operators, municipalities and their transit authorities, and infrastructure owners all wanting to solve mobility related challenges. 
We have also identified use cases for the same SDK that uses our automatic multi-modal detection solution to automatically carbon footprint an individuals mobility habits by applying the relevant carbon factor to the distance travelled by by the user. 

There are also applications to identify how transport systems improve social mobility by helping to capture end-to-end origin-destination matrices style journey histories. Even encouraging more active travel by virtue of our ability to capture both human powered travels and motorised.

COVID19 has revealed another application for our IP stack. Contact or spread tracing is a critical tool health professionals use to identify how transmitters of a pathogen infect others. Helping to isolate those who pose a risk while simultaneously providing data for epidemiologists to profile a pathogens characteristics. Providing the opportunity to equip medical professionals, governments and citizens with a tool to fight this global pandemic.

entityDescription:
The Department of Biology at the University of Florence has a long history that has its roots well before the founding of the University itself. It is in fact the heir to the naturalistic studies that brought prestige to the city of Florence and contributed to the development of natural sciences worldwide. Indeed, it is from the mid-18th century that the Museum of Physics and Natural History was founded, located even then in Via Romana in one of the Department's current locations. Still, the Department of Biology houses in the building on Via La Pira the Italian Botanical Society, founded in Florence in 1888, which traces its origin to the first botanical society in Europe (the Florentine Botanical Society) founded in Florence in 1716.
On this distinguished past the Department of Biology has not rested, and in recent decades, through continuous renewal, it has now moved to the forefront in many important areas of biology. The disciplines in which the research conducted by the Department of Biology is currently an international excellence are numerous: microbiology, genetics, physiology, botany in all its aspects, zoology with a particular contribution from ethology, ecology of both marine and terrestrial environments, anthropology, cytology and histology, comparative anatomy, and, as a common thread, the history of biology and natural sciences with evolutionary studies.
The solid scientific basis on which the Department of Biology is founded is its interest in experimental research, and within this framework it should be emphasized that the scientific work conducted by researchers and technicians in the Department is strongly oriented toward basic research, but carefully and increasingly considers its applications, responding to current needs for innovation and development. Building on robust basic knowledge, researchers in the Department of Biology recognize that good research always has within it the preconditions for possible applications and are therefore interested in offering their knowledge and technologies to develop potential applications.

Building on the strong interest in basic scientific research and its applications, the Department's teaching and technical staff is able to handle a good deal of teaching in basic and applied biological and natural sciences disciplines of different educational tracks: biology, natural sciences, biotechnology, at the level of bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs. Teaching in experimental disciplines such as biology finds its natural complement in intensive laboratory and field exercises that provide students with a practical foundation for their future profession.

Facilities
The rich and multifaceted history of the Department of Biology still surfaces in the facilities in which its various components are housed and interact effectively with each other. On the one hand, the historic buildings in the center of Florence, in Via La Pira, Via del Proconsolo and Via Romana, which are also home to the Museum of Natural History, represent the link with the more properly naturalistic disciplines while the premises at the Scientific Pole in Sesto Fiorentino particularly accommodate the physiological and molecular disciplines.

entityDescription:
PortExpertise is a Belgian independent consultancy of maritime port professionals. Partners of PortExpertise are international experts and have at least 15 years of experience in among others strategy, financing and operations in maritime and port related sectors. They performed on research assignments and project management in more than 300 maritime ports and maritime terminal projects worldwide. The company has agents in Europe, Middle-East and Asia. PortExpertise is active in Worldbank and European Union projects, assisting international organizations, maritime authorities, port communities and the big five consultancy firms in port related projects.Further relevant references are PortExpertise’s representation of Belgium in the Expert Group on Maritime Simplification; Project manager for the Port Community Service Platform Project of 4 Flemish ports; Assistance to the Belgian SafeSeaNet national competent authority in major SafeSeaNet related matters; Projects are performed in EU’s top 10 of maritime Member States next to a long list of non-EU locations, which include among others: PortExpertise has an impressive proven track record on Port Community System and Maritime Single Windows on national, European and global level ever since 2006 with the PCSP (Port Community Service Platform) project, preparing the platform for the Flemish ports. Soon afterwards PortExpertise facilitated the European priority project (2012-EU-21019-S) AnNA (Advanced National Networks for Administrations 2013-2016) dealing with the adoption of the national Maritime Single Window and electronic data transmission for the fulfilment of reporting requirements for vessels entering and departing European ports in accordance with EC Directive 2010/65/EU. The next years similar projects enabled to expand this expertise on data exchange platforms related to Maritime/Port Environments and Inland Water Way transport, both for public and private entities/organizations. To name a few: Belgian Port Community System (PCS) a platform that offers services for 5 Belgian Maritime Ports;Pakistan Trade Facilitation (Project No. 1260332); DG Move Support action for contributing to the establishment of a European Maritime Single Window environment data set (Service contract MOVE/D1/SER/2018-377/SI2.789555); Revision of the Reporting Formalities Directive with the aim to establish European maritime single window environment (Contract MOVE/A3/119-2013); RIS Enabled European IWT Corridor Management (CoRISMA) 2012-EU-70004-S); MAiDEN, the Maritime Information Data Exchange Network Search & Rescue services, enhancing the interoperability between 5 coastal search and rescue partners (EASME/EMFF/2017/1.2.1.3); Maritime Single Window service delivery plan for Belgian authorities. Currently we are active in the Port of the Future project called DockstheFuture (No 770064) addressing (among others) the challenges related to simplification and digitalization of processes in maritime & port sector.
PortExpertise’s acted as Project manager of the Belgian Maritime Single Window (BMSW), related to Europe’s Reporting Formalities Directive. In this role PortExpertise developed a System Requirements Specification for the Belgian Maritime Single Window including i.e. the list of data elements, their technical definition and semantic meaning and further on analysed the national reporting requirements. They assisted DG MOVE into the first data harmonisation activities on the Maritime Single Window Data, by updating the country fiches, and developing a web based tool to facilitate harmonisation of this date from 23 Member States.

entityDescription:
Hadean’s distributed compute platform offers a breakthrough in the power and scale of cloud-based IT infrastructure. Global organisations can now harness the full force of unlimited cross-cloud compute to solve their most complex problems, in real-time.

Hadean was founded to remove computational bottlenecks by enabling scaling without engineering and ops effort. Taking a first-principles approach to distributed computing, we developed our foundational technology - the Hadean platform - that provides the necessary and sufficient primitives and the strong execution guarantees to enable programmers to write networked, dynamically-scaling, distributed apps. entityDescription:
The Bosch Group is a leading global supplier of technology and services. It employs roughly 410,000 associates worldwide (as of December 31, 2018). The company generated sales of 78.5 billion euros in 2018. Its operations are divided into four business sectors: Mobility Solutions, Industrial Technology, Consumer Goods, and Energy and Building Technology. As a leading IoT company, Bosch offers innovative solutions for smart homes, smart cities, connected mobility, and connected manufacturing. It uses its expertise in sensor technology, software, and services, as well as its own IoT cloud, to offer its customers connected, crossdomain solutions from a single source. The Bosch Group’s strategic objective is to create solutions for a connected life. Bosch improves quality of life worldwide with innovative products and services that are “Invented for life” and spark enthusiasm.
The Bosch Group comprises Robert Bosch GmbH and its roughly 460 subsidiary and regional companies in over 60 countries. Including sales and service partners, Bosch’s global manufacturing, engineering, and sales network covers nearly every country in the world. The basis for the company’s future growth is its innovative strength. At nearly 130 locations across the globe, Bosch employs some 68,700 associates in research and development.
The company was set up in Stuttgart in 1886 by Robert Bosch (1861–1942) as“Workshop for Precision Mechanics and Electrical Engineering”
The special ownership structure of Robert Bosch GmbH guarantees the entrepreneurial freedom of the Bosch Group, making it possible for the company to plan over the long term and to undertake significant upfront investments in the safeguarding of its future. Ninety-two percent of the share capital of Robert Bosch GmbH is held by Robert Bosch Stiftung GmbH, a charitable foundation. The majority of voting rights are held by Robert Bosch Industrietreuhand KG, an industrial trust. The entrepreneurial ownership functions are carried out by the trust. The remaining shares are held by the Bosch family and by Robert Bosch GmbH.

CybExer Technologies is a NATO-awarded Estonian cybersecurity company. We have wide- ranging experience in providing and maintaining highly sophisticated cyber security training platforms with a special focus on cyber capability development. Our platforms are the key to our successful delivery of a plethora of cybersecurity trainings and exercises aimed at ordinary users, technical responders and the very top of strategic leadership.
 
Cyber Range Solutions - CybExer’s flagship service is the development, operation and maintenance of next-generation, state-of-the-art, cyber ranges. Irrespective of the cyber range – be it our proprietary ranges configured for immediate use or those custom developed for our clients – our development principles are focused on ensuring highly scalable, flexible, and high-availability ranges. Cloud-based, On-Premise or Hybrid Cyber Range.

Security Testing and Research - The traditional use-case of a cyber range is related to security testing and research. For example, in security testing, different tools and solutions can be safely targeted with attacks to assess their security and identify vulnerabilities before their actual use in an operational environment. Moreover, with security research, continuous efforts to analyse exploits and vulnerabilities can be conducted.

Organisational Resilience - Last but not least, cyber ranges and their applications for training and testing can provide valuable input for organisational and operational risk management, crisis resolution, and human resources development. It is not just the specific skills of IT specialists or the robustness of security tools that matter but also the wider, organisational capacity to collectively prevent and manage cyber incidents through a broad array of processes, procedures and technologies. Lastly, cyber ranges ensure continuity of operations (COOP) as testing of new changes (patches, updates, code updates, etc.) may be tested in pre-production before being delivered to staging and production environments.

Custom Built Cyber Ranges - Our team has built numerous highly efficient and unique cyber ranges. We offer customized solutions to all of our clients and thus provide unique learning, training and testing opportunities. Our cyber ranges have three hosting models: cloud-based, on-premise, or hybrid cyber ranges.

entityDescription:
Morpheus Designs is a consulting firm specialising in the design and analysis of high performance thermal management and lightweight components using the design freedom offered by Additive Manufacturing (AM) technology. We believe that fundamental rethinking and redesign of products can result in better components in many applications.

Morpheus Designs offers a range of engineering solutions related thermal management and light-weighting using additive manufacturing. The main areas of consulting that Morpheus Designs will offer are:

1. Heat exchanger design and analysis:
- Concept generation: From a customer’s system requirements, Morpheus Designs can offer conceptual design, with detailed size and performance requirements, so the customer can assess if they can benefit for the AM solutions that can be provided. Advice about integration, cost, post-processing and other factors can be provided too.
- Thermal 1D analysis: Thanks to unique state-of-the-art analysis tools, Morpheus designs can validate their thermal design for a range of applications and conditions.
- FE analysis and lifing: To evaluate the structural performance and lifing of their customer’s products and designs, Morpheus Designs can provide Finite Element Analysis (FEA) services.
- CFD simulations and Validation: In order to validate their customer’s products and designs in terms of thermal and flow performance, we can provide CFD analysis services that can offer great insights into the performance of our clients design and help reduce. Both CFD and FEA can lower development costs by minimizing physical testing and help verify and validate the components.
- Thermal optimization: Morpheus Designs can combine their expertise in thermal analysis and optimisation to offer their customers with state-of-the-art optimization methodologies for thermal components.
2. Structural optimisation for lightweighting
- Topology optimisation: Topology optimisation is a method that calculated the minimum distribution of material based on the loads and constraints of a problem. Thanks to the experience within the team with such techniques for additive manufacturing components.
- Lightweight cellular structures: Morpheus Designs will develop tools for the generation of lightweight lattice structures that can be beneficial for a number of applications.
3. Design for AM process
- Design of AM components, applying process rules and limitations.
- Design of small-scale prototypes for experimental validation
- Build preparation solutions integrated within the same framework as the analysis and design tools. Including:
 - 3d printing files generation
 - Support structures automatic design, based on internal library
 - Scanning strategies for complex, very fine parts for heat exchangers and other complex parts such as lattice structures.

entityName: Istituto Nazionale per le malattie Infettive Lazzaro Spallanzani IRCSS
entityDescription: The National Institute for Infectious Diseases (INMI) "Lazzaro Spallanzani" is an historical public institution operating since 1936 in the field of infectious diseases. In 1996, it was officially appointed also as research institute for infectious diseases. In 2009, a transplant center was opened at INMI, for the first time in Italy inside an institute for infectious disease. INMI is the Italian centre of excellence for the care and basic, translational research in patients affected by infectious diseases. The mission of INMI is to provide high-quality clinical care for patients with infectious diseases with a special interest in HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, viral hepatitis, severe infections, emerging/re-emerging infections and infections in the immunocompromised host; to assist in the development of a global response in Italy and abroad to emerging/re-emerging diseases, including both highly contagious, naturally occurring and deliberately released, microorganisms; and to help integration among clinical, epidemiological and pre-clinical research with the aim of enhancing the diagnosis, care and prevention of infectious diseases. The Institute has epidemiologic, diagnostic, patient care and research facilities, all placed in a large campus, located in the central area of the city.INMI covers an area of more than 130,000 square meters with 15 buildings. The mission of the institute is; to provide state of the art clinical care for patients with infectious diseases with special interest in HIV, viral hepatitis, tuberculosis, emerging/re-emerging infections and infections in the immunocompromised and transplanted host; to assist in the development of a global response to emerging/re-emerging diseases, including both highly contagious naturally occurring and deliberately released microorganisms; to promote integration among clinical, epidemiological and pre-clinical research with the aim of enhancing the diagnosis, care and prevention of infectious diseases. INMI research agenda is focused on blood-borne pathogens, TB and emerging infectious diseases, HIV/AIDS and viral hepatitis for basic, pathogenetic, diagnostic, epidemiologic, care/treatment and prevention purposes. The available equipment allows to perform full range of genomic, transcriptomic and proteomic analysis, in addition to classical imaging, cultural and immunological studies. The availability of high containment laboratories allows to perform research activity on high threat pathogens.

entityDescription: Seascape Belgium offers services to marine offshore and coastal operators, managers, policy makers and funders focusing on knowledge based solutions for sustainable management and development of our seas and oceans. Established in 2017, Seascape Belgium specialises in the coordination/management of multidisciplinary marine science projects in support of policy/industry, and the provision of high-level advice to various stakeholders, including regulatory bodies, policymakers, industry and NGOs. Seascape Belgium staff have long standing experience with science communication, event organisation, stakeholder engagement and facilitation of science-policy interfaces. entityDescription:
GIVE is a visionary design and engineering startup based in Athens, that started at the end of 2016. We provide technical innovation, product design, and advanced engineering analysis, specialized in the whole range of advanced engineering analysis, ranging from lightweight materials, structural analysis & optimization all the way to CFD, multi-body dynamics, electromagnetics and more. Through a solid experience in the world of the automotive, aerospace and motorsports, we derived speed and accuracy, as well as a passion for beautiful detail and efficient performance. We have been involved in a wid range of projects focused manily in the automotive and aerospace fields, while we have been also heavily involved in project work for the energy sector. Our work concerns advanced analysis, such as statics, non-linear structural analysis, FRA and modal analysis, crash (dynamic) behavior), composites, coupling of structural analysis with multi-body dynamics, etc, while optimization (topology, topography, free size, generic, etc) and CFD have also been critical to our business so far.

The company - founded in October 2016 - has been supported by own financial investments and earnings coming from our project work (contract work for the industry) that have all been “bootstrapped” back to our own R&D in the fields of vehicle electrification and product development. In 2019 Elin Verd became a minority shareholder with a first-round investment into GIVE (creation of holding company PBOT), helping develop a prototype electric vehicle (today at TRL7), as well as a solid business concept and strategy behind it. GIVE’s turnover has been increasing since 2016, with our estimation being that this pattern of growth will be maintained due to our products/services maturity status.

Besides however the contracted work, we believe it is imperative to stay close to relevant R&D projects, and GIVE has been involved in both national and international research calls. Currently we have been accepted in a national call for future development of energy management systems with integration of different energy sources (program ICBase), while we are also working on a EUROSTAR collaborative project with partners from Cyprus and Korea for the design, analysis and production (including prototyping and testing) of a hydrogen powered inspection drone (HyFly).Furthermore, we have created an internal program so as to stay close to the academia supporting two internships each year, PhD and master theses (currently we are the industrial supervisor of a PhD on autonomous driving) as well as a number of student teams that GIVE helps mainly with technical help and support (formula student, moto student, etc.). Keeping close to the academia brings us not only closer to the current state-of-the-art, but also close to the best students and ‘pool’ of talent. We are currently also awaiting response from a Marie Curie research program for the support of 4 industrial PhD researchers.

entityDescription:
Open Thing CIC will provide benefit to individuals, families and businesses across the UK through improved air quality, stronger community links and promoting and encouraging environmental sustainability. Open Thing CIC will develop open-source devices and software for the benefit of this community. Individuals and groups will be able to access designs, instructions, kits and complete devices and a virtual community sharing information. Through Open Thing devices and software they can learn about the environment of their local area, and compare this to other sources of data across the UK and globally, and the other Open Thing devices. Through a simple dashboard, everyone will be able to understand how our daily cycle changes the world around us and measure how behaviour changes impact this. For example, kits to monitor air quality, which collects data to a dashboard showing how human behaviour (such as idling cars) impacts on air quality. The WHO has declared air pollution as the biggest environmental threat to global health, resulting in 7 million premature deaths a year. Seeing graphically how idling raises pollutants such as Nitrous Oxide in the air in real-time will empower schools and communities to inform and change behaviour. 

 enabling community/society to understand their impact on the environment 
 enrich information about how our behaviour impacts on the environment 
 change behaviour through informed feedback
address: Bournemouth Eagle Lab, County Gates House 300 Poole Road

The Institute is a centre of fundamental research in physical chemistry, electrochemistry and chemical physics (short history). The research work is characterized by many cross-links both within the Institute and also with other institutions in Europe, the U.S.A., Japan and other parts of the world. Much of the scientific work is concerned with fundamental research, but several groups, in particular in catalysis and electrochemistry, are also making contributions in more applied aspects. Besides the research activities the Institute is strongly involved in training of both undergraduate and graduate students, supervising their diploma and Ph.D. theses, and in teaching at universities.
In the Institute work at present about 165 full-time employees and approximately 45 graduate students. Roughly 70 per cent of the personnel are engaged in research, the remaining staff provides technical and administrative services.
Members of the Institute publish each year approximately 250 research papers, for the most part in impacted international journals (in 2017: 159 articles in journals with an average impact factor of 4.84), several books or chapters in monographs, and a number of communications in proceedings of scientific meetings.

entityDescription:
The ambition is to offer clinical lab performance with the ease-of-use of a pregnancy test at a consumer price tag.
Antelope Dx offers a diagnostic testing device that performs accurate tests at home, in less than 15 minutes. It allows the individual to have on-the-spot access to key health parameters where and when it matters: testing accurately, yet in an affordable, lifestyle way. Today, only 2 successful home tests are available, the glucose test and the pregnancy test. They measure highly abundant proteins and are not complex. It is a difficult combination to bring highly accurate, easy to use tests at an affordable price tag for the individual at home. This is exactly what Antelope aims to do.

Photonic chips, complex measurements at low-cost
The recipe for success lies predominantly in the architecture of the Antelope consumable and reader. The Antelope platform is based on an innovative lab-on-chip technology that can perform a sensitive test on any bodily fluid, without requiring complex user operations or sample preparation.

The company's mission is the research, development, preliminary design, production and marketing of high-tech products.

PlanetWatch create, validate and monetize real-time air quality data (PM1, PM2.5, PM10…), obtained from sensors connected to its network. Data are then recorded on the Algorand blockchain,creating an immutable ledger. Token rewards are issued for any contribution to our ecosystem. 

The PlanetWatch global network consists of air quality sensors and people who care about the environment (PlanetWatchers). Sensors are installed by individuals inside or outside their homes or carried with them on the go, which leverages the installation of additional sensors by PlanetWatch in partnership with transport and telecommunications companies, local authorities, etc.

This approach allows us to rapidly deploy low-cost, real-time,high-density air quality monitoring networks which complement governmental infrastructure.

entityDescription:
EasyWay Systems Ltd. was established in 2015 by a team of highly trained consultants, project managers and software developers who’s been working together on large scale enterprise IT projects going back for many years. Our vision is not only to execute customer projects, but create with customers. The diversity of knowledge provided by the consultants and developers not only supports the development cutting edge software solutions, but also innovate in the processes. We provide service for the full life-cycle of a software project, from requirements gathering, development, test, quality and project management to maintenance.
We are committed to quality and reliability and these commitments are embedded deeply in our development processes. 
Our company has a bit of space heritage as well, as one of our technical management team member was part of the Hungarian Space Furnace software development and maintenance team, and also worked at NASA MSFC. He is also one of the founding member of the Hungarian Space Cluster.
Among our customers we have large organizations and enterprises both in the public and the government sector, specializing in the energy and transportation industry.
One of our focus area is security, where our portfolio scales from PKI based security solutions to IoT security for device and key distribution management. 
Our vision while joining the Space Community is to get involved in software development in Flight Hardware and also create value added Ground Based Services to distribute the processed information collected in space for the everyday use.

entityName: AIVP - The worldwide network of port cities
entityDescription:
AIVP is the only international organisation with a global presence that, for more than 30 years, has been bringing together all the public and private development stakeholders in port cities. AIVP has had the privilege of bearing witness to the changes underway in cities and ports the world over; we have accompanied our members in the implementation of new strategies that allow them to more effectively face up to the changes that impact economic, social and environmental development in port cities: urban-port integration, global reorganisation of economic routes, the challenge of societal integration, climate change, energy transition, the development of the cruise industry, etc. Currently, AIVP has more than 180 members worldwide and a network of more than 1900 stakeholders including:
- elected representatives of cities and other local maritime and river organisations,
- port administrations and national authorities, urban and port operators,
- businesses established in port cities,
- service providers for port-city projects, architects, landscape architects and urban planners,
- universities and research institutes.

The German Sport University Cologne is Germany’s only, and Europe’s largest, university in the field of sport and exercise science. All relevant sport science issues are dealt with at this unique university in Germany, shared between 19 academic institutes. Humanities, social and business disciplines are also represented here, along with life sciences. These are complemented by four affiliate institutes as well as 5 transfer centres.

The German Sport University utilises its excellent interdisciplinary research opportunities to ensure its position as a leader in both national and international sport and exercise science and has a unique capacity to conduct transdisciplinary research with other universities and institutions worldwide. Aware of its responsibility towards both sport and society, the university continually invests in innovation and emphasizes the growing significance of a physically active lifestyle in terms of health, social politics and economics. Fields of research cover the ethical, sociological, economic and educational aspects of sport as an integral element of society; questioning the influence of exercise or lack of exercise, training and nutrition on healthy and ill people across all age groups.

entityDescription:
Ø MISSON: DTL is an innovative drone technology company aiming to facilitate the widespread adoption of Beyond Visual Line of Sight (BVLOS) and autonomous UAV flight in unsegregated airspace - an aim shared with the UK’s Civil Aviation Authority (CAA).
Ø APPROACH: DTL aim to provide clients support with ‘all things drone’. We will do this by capitalising on our extensive transferable technical knowledge from other industries to identify Use Cases, utilising our extensive networks to establish strong partnerships and by drawing upon decades of project management experience to integrate both partners and technology to create solutions to meet our clients’ specific needs.
Ø SCOPE: DTL intend to be involved in both operation and development drone systems as well as supporting our clients with SME consultancy advice. As a rapidly expanding industry DTL believe it is important to be immersed in the design and operation of systems if our capabilities and knowledge base are to remain market-leading and ahead of our competitors. 
Ø FOCUS: DTL time and resources will be focused on the development and support of Use Cases where the adoption of drones offers safety, environmental and/or cost reduction benefits to clients.

entityDescription: Národní centrum zemědělského a potravinářského výzkumu, v. v. i. /National Center for Agricultural and Food Research, v. v. i. (CARC; before 2025 Crop Research Institute CRI; before 2007 Research Institute of Crop Production) was established in 1951 as the Central Research Institute of Crop Production. The basic aim of the CARC is the development of scientific knowledge in the fields of integrated crop production and production of hygienically-safe foodstuffs, and the creation of bases for sustainable development of agriculture and environmental protection. During 60 years of its existence, CARC has been the leading research institution in crop production in the Czech Republic. The mission of CARC is primarily strategic and applied research in crop production, food and agricultural engineering but includes pure research. From this point of view, CARC fills the space between the basic research implemented at universities and the Czech Academy of Sciences, and the specialized applied research implemented at private institutes and field stations.

entityDescription:
The Spanish Road Association (Asociacion Espanola de la Carretera – AEC) is a non-profit organization founded in 1949 whose main goals are the advocacy, promotion, research and development of better and safer roads. The Spanish Road Association was in addition officially declared of “Public utility” by the Spanish Government in 1998.From its creation, the Association has adapted its activities to the social and economic changes happened in each moment. 
At present, its actions are focused on the following areas: research, road safety, environment, new technologies, urban mobility, infrastructure service quality. Article 2 of its Statutes indicate that the Association has the following key objectives, among others, “… Promote innovation and development, aside from studying, disseminating and, in appropriate cases, proposing those lines of activities to supplies effective solutions to road sector problems and in all other areas of the same (road safety, environment, maintenance, financing, materials, new technologies and any other of interest) …”. This is the reason that AEC regularly organizes many education and social campaigns targeted at the technical sector: researches and technical reports, congresses, seminars, training courses, publications, informative campaigns, information exchange with other similar organisms all over the world, etc… 
All these actions are possible through the existing cooperation agreements with different organizations from the public sector, private companies, federations and associations. Moreover, the Spanish Road Association is the Spanish NRA (National Road Association) of the International Road Federation (IRF) and a founding member of the European Road Federation (ERF).It is also a founding member of the Latin-American Institute (IVIA), which is formed by research and technological centers from South America, and collaborates with other international institutions as the European Commission, the European Transport Safety Council (ETSC) or the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
In 2005 AEC received the most important international award from the IRF, the “Global Road Achievement Award” in its category “Advocacy and Lobbying”. The prestige and the value of the activities of the Spanish Road Association was then recognised all over the world. In 2013, AEC has received, in cooperation with the Inter-American Development Bank, the “Global Road Achievement Award” in its category “Road Safety, for the road safety assessment specifically developed by AEC for the Bank. 
The Spanish Road Association has been working in the field of road safety, both in the Spanish and in the international context, during the last 30 years. The relevant projects described in the firm’s references guarantee the maximum degree of experience and competence in road safety training.

entityName: Neath Port Talbot College (Trading as NPTC Group of Colleges)
entityDescription:
On 1 August 2013, Neath Port Talbot College and Coleg Powys merged. It is now one of the largest Further Education providers in Wales covering 30% of the landmass in Wales. The College offers an exciting and varied programme of full and part-time courses across its eleven campuses to more than 270,000 residents stretching across south to north Wales.
Operating out of nine campuses, the College now covers two local authority areas; Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council and Powys County Council. Within Neath Port Talbot County Borough Council, it operates as a tertiary college in its constitution providing post 16 education and training for the great majority of pupils from the local schools as well as being a significant partner in 14-19 projects in the local area. 
The College provides vocational education and training in almost every industrial and vocational area. In Powys, the College is the main provider of vocational training and delivered at the levels of activity agreed with each organisation providing funds to the College including the Welsh Government, Powys County Council, schools and HE institutions. Across both counties the College plays a leading role in the provision of community based learning and leads one of the largest Work Based Learning Consortia in the region.
The College also delivers bespoke training for industry and business across Wales and beyond working through its dedicated Business Development Unit. 
A recent development is the Group’s Drone Academy which is a specific department set up within NPTC group of Colleges, to facilitate business support and training for drone maintenance and operation. The academy has nine drones and trained personnel to deliver training and CAA approval. We also have an agreement with ECITB, to deliver their courses as a Wales centre, as well as the recently created drone competence certification scheme.
We have also partnered with RUAS, a well-respected drone company to deliver wider support and development in drone activities.

entityDescription:
Stockholm Environment Institute: bridging science and policy
We are an international non-profit research and policy organization that tackles environment and development challenges.
We connect science and decision-making to develop solutions for a sustainable future for all.
Our work spans climate, water, air and land-use issues, governance, the economy, gender and health. Stakeholder involvement is at the heart of our efforts to build capacity, strengthen institutions and equip partners for long-term change.
Our knowledge and findings are accessible to decision-makers and civil society: as our own open access material, in leading academic journals, and repackaged for effective decision support.
To promote debate and share knowledge we convene decision-makers, academics and practitioners and engage with policy processes, development action and business practice worldwide.
We are:
- International: SEI has offices in five continents and works locally, regionally and globally.
- Trusted: decision-makers and the academic community recognize us as an independent and non-partisan institute.
- Credible: our research is objective and supported by rigorous peer review.
- Relevant: our work makes connections across the natural, physical and social sciences, allowing us to take new angles and offer robust, insightful policy advice.

entityName: Centro de Ciências do Mar do Algarve
entityDescription:
CCMAR is an interdisciplinary research center gathering experts (about 250 integrated members, of which approximately half are PhD holders) unified by the motivations to understand, explore and protect the potential of marine resources. Our teams work in synergy on three thematic lines: 1) GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES, 2) OCEAN MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION, and 3) MARINE PRODUCTS AND RESOURCES. Our research feeds many disciplines, from oceanography to biotech and biomimicry, from aquaculture to biomedical applications, from fisheries and ecology to food sciences. Our results and methodologies are disseminated to society, translated into innovation for businesses, and is the bases for training at all career stages, embedded within the system of the University of Algarve – though CCMAR is financially autonomous.
For its activity, CCMAR has repeatedly been classified excellent by the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology and ranked first among the marine science centers. Indeed, yearly in CCMAR we start approximately 50 funded projects from various funding bodies, we disseminate knowledge to researchers and companies in more than 220 ISI publications and a couple patents, and we host several conferences and outreach events. In addition, thanks to our integration in the network of the European Research Infrastructures (EMBRIC including EMBRC, AQUAEXCEL2020, AssemblePlus) we attract researchers from around the world to conduct their research in our facilities, making of CCMAR a hub for research and innovation.

Company description: The Southwestern State Enterprise (SWSE) was established pursuant to Art. 163 of the Forest Act, based on Order No RD 49-106 dd. 13.04.2011 and Order No RD 49-210 dd. 04.06.2011 of the Minister of Agriculture and Food. The enterprise is responsible for the management of forest territories within the boundaries of eight administrative districts, namely Blagoevgrad, Kyustendil, Pernik, Sofia City and Sofia District, and of individual forest management units in the districts of Lovech, Pazardzhik and Plovdiv. Their total area amounts to 958,320 ha, of which 680,660 ha, or 71 percent are state-owned forest territories. The structure of SWSE comprises a central administration and 38 territorial units, being 6 state hunting enterprises (SHE), and 32 state forestry enterprises (SFE). All of them are part of the forest service in Bulgaria, which has over 140-year-old history and traditions in the care for the Bulgarian Forest.
The main tasks of the enterprise are aimed at sustainable management, maintenance of the ecosystem diversity, conservation of the biodiversity and the forest resources in the state-owned forests, and comprise of:
• Implementation of the forestry and hunting management plans, as well as maintenance and/or restoration activities in the state-owned forests;
• Activities for protection and conservation of the forest territories and anti-erosion measures in the state-owned forests;
• Design and construction activities in the forests and the lands falling in the state-owned forest territories;
• Planting of new forests in farm land;
• Provision and rendering of public services;

entityName: Sapienza University of Rome - Dipartimento di Scienze della Terra
entityDescription:
The DES at Sapienza University of Rome was formally born in 1985, by joining of the institutes of Geology and Paleontology, of Mineralogy and Petrography and of Geochemistry. In spite of this, it can be considered one of the oldest department of Earth Sciences in Italy since its roots can be dated back to the setting up of the chairs of Mineralogy and Natural History by Pope Pio VII on November 13th, 1804.
The study of Earth Sciences at Sapienza University of Rome has seen the succession of distinguished scientists such as Gian Alberto Blanc, first professorship of Geochemistry in Italy (1928) and Federico Millosevich, first professorship of Petrography in Italy (1938). Outstanding scientists are also Ettore Onorato, who early studied minerals by X-ray diffraction (1926), Felice Ippolito, who established the magazine “Le Scienze” (1968), Mario Fornaseri, who studied the geochemical and petrographical characters of the Alban Volcanic Complex (1963), and Bruno Accordi, who first studied the dwarf elephants (1972).
The DES is proud to host the rich collections of the historical museums of Mineralogy, Geology and Paleontology, which forms the most significant academic collection of Earth Sciences in Italy.

entityDescription:
HLRS is a research and service institution affiliated to the Information Centre of the University of Stuttgart. It is one of the three national supercomputing centres in Germany and one of the three members of the GAUSS Centre for Supercomputing, offering services to users from academia and industry. The world leading experience of HLRS in supporting users from the engineering domain at large in parallel programming, in the development of productivity tools for parallel programming including integrated development environments, in the expertise in applying software engineering methods to the HPC domain and in cloud computing, Big Data and Machine Learning projects.
HLRS has been the first national supercomputing centre in Germany and is offering services to academic users and industry. Furthermore, it has, together with the Steinbuch Computing Centre Karlsruhe funded two solution centres (Energy and Automotive) to support activities of stakeholders in this domain. With the co- founded SICOS GmbH, HLRS is in constant contact with SMEs willing to use HPC to improve their business.

entityDescription:
Railview is a leading research data services company specialising in the visualisation of infrastructure subsurface defects. We have world-class competencies in customising and developing bespoke radar visualisation algorithms that can tackle infrastructure inspection challenges to allow our customers to plan preventative maintenance for their transport infrastructures. We are specialists in visualising subterranean and subsurface assets - providing clear and distinct 3D images. 

We have taken conventional GPR and developed an algorithm to develop and visualise the subterranean environment looking at assets in order to monitor their condition. These are effectively X-ray specs for infrastructure. Using specialised bespoke software to accurately control the transmitter and receiver the algorithms produce 3D images of the subsurface infrastructure assets. Railview won the Idea of the Year 2019 award at the North East Innovation Awards in November 2019 for this innovation.

We are advancing the quality of Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) for underground areas in rail infrastructure such as ballast, sub-ballast (including drainage systems), sub-grade, water pipes and utilities, tunnel linings and tunnel track systems, retaining walls and bridge surface structures. Gathering images and interpreting the results is a difficult task and our algorithms are constantly being tested and developed to produce better images.

Providing a GPR survey requires a skilled operator with a GPR licence to perform surveys: the interpretation of radargrams is generally non-intuitive to the inexperienced eye. A high level of expertise is required to design, conduct and interpret an effective GPR survey. 
At Railview we have experienced GPR licenced operators who can survey various underground issues in several areas:
- Culvert mapping

- Retaining walls

- Sub-surface chemical storage

- Utility mapping

- Land purchase

- Archaeological surveys

entityDescription: In France, 25% of the population lives in areas subject to the flood risk. Among them, the majority lives in cities. It is a tremendous challenge for the crisis unit to operate with tools they can trust during the extreme episode and to anticipate with forecasting systems.TENEVIA brings a new vision of environmental monitoring through innovative solution that help authorities prevent flood risk. For the past 7 years, TENEVIA has been developing solutions for Measuring, Monitoring and Forecasting the evolution of rivers.When implementing flood prevention strategy based on early warning systems, the first step is to deploy sensors to observed and monitor the water in real time. Two critical features are sought : water level and flow rate.Water level sensors enable to alert the authorities of threshold exceedance. For this, TENEVIA has developed CamLevel, a sensors designed to monitor river, canal (…) by providing water level measurement and threshold detection. The idea is to make a CCTV camera become a sensor by implementing CamLevel Software within. The main benefit are :• to provide a vision of the site in order to help the crisis manager by facilitating the decision making;• To attest the quality of the measurement;• to locate the sensor further from the river and doing so, to limit the chance of being washed away.CamLevel is robust, non-immersive and operating in extreme conditions.Out of the same camera, it is possible to go further on the hydrometric information by calculating flow rate. The sensor CamFlow enable to trace thousands of surface velocity vectors out of a burst of image. By adding topographical and bathymetrical information, the sensor provides to the users velocity measurement (m/s) and flow rate (m3/s) information. This information is very useful for dimensioning protective structures (such as dikes) and calibrate models. It is however a difficult and expensive information to obtain. The second step is to anticipate the flood. Doing so, TENEVIA has developed a simulator that enable to gain time on the risings waters.The solution HydroCore, based on forecasting model simulates the behaviour of a catchment area in order to transform the precipitations into flow rate. The information provided enables cities to have valuable and accurate information on the state of the watercourse up to 48 hours before a flood.

The Council has a revenue budget of over £1bn, with 123 local Councillors representing the 550,000 residents of Cornwall,delivering services to every community across the County.
The Council has a workforce of around 5,000 and is the biggest employer in Cornwall. The Chief Executive and Strategic Directors form the Council's management team, which leads the work that provides services across Cornwall.
Council staff and services are based in offices, depots and facilities across Cornwall. Advice and information about Council services are available through an extensive network of our Information Service (One Stop Shops), call centre and our website.

entityDescription:
KERDRY gets more and more involved in Research and Development to increase skills and expertise in three major technologies: metallic coating, optical coatings and patterning by photolithography.
Metallic coating: Kerdry has a capacity to treat large dimension mirrors up to 1.4 meters diameter (Ag, Al, Au).

History
Centrum dopravniho vyzkumu, v.v.i. (CDV), Transport Research Centre in English, is a public research institution, established according to the law 341/2005 Coll. on public research institutions, and the only one research body under the Czech Ministry of Transport. Established in 1993 as a legal successor of then federal (Czecho-Slovak) Transport Research Institute, CDV has continued in a more than 60-years tradition.
In 2007, CDV became a public research institute. Since 2014, CDV has also been an appraisal institute in the fields related to transport and civil engineering.
Present
Through its research focus, CDV – Transport Research Centre, covers the key needs of transport development in the Czech Republic at national, regional and local levels. The institute covers traditional fields, such as road safety, construction technology, maintenance, repairs and reconstruction of transport infrastructure, including geotechnical aspects and diagnostics of transport structures, impacts of transport on the environment, transport economy, multimodal transport, traffic psychology, traffic education, traffic demand modelling, management systems, geographic information systems, check-in and parking systems, telematic controlling systems, etc.
Research outcomes are directly applied in practice through different methods.

entityDescription: Future Needs Management Consulting Ltd is an interdisciplinary SME focusing on policy assessment and recommendations, on socio-economic impact and on business development for social and technical innovation solutions. Our staff has over 12 years’ experience of working in interdisciplinary teams on research and policy involving social problems. Our team leverages know-how from the fields of economics, social science, business administration and industrial design to assess social and economic impacts originating from the evolution of technologies in different fields such as information & telecommunications, education, healthcare, transport, regional development, culture and finance. We use insights gained from impact analysis studies to materialise data-driven innovation and to create sound policy. One of our core values is to pursue Responsible research and innovation (RRI) and to ensure that the projects and initiatives we are part of are aligned with this principle. RRI implies that societal actors (researchers, citizens, policy makers, business, third sector organisations, etc.) work together during the whole research and innovation process in order to better align both the process and its outcomes with the values, needs and expectations of society and includes impact metrics related to open access, gender, ethics, science education, etc. Privacy and security by design in both research, data science, and technology development is our second horizontal principle, ensuring that systems we contribute develop are as free of vulnerabilities and impervious to attack as possible and data processed always comply with the GDPR regulation. Our commercial services focus on helping our business clients develop R&D roadmaps aiming at product and service commercialisation, eliciting user requirements for the development of new products and services and supporting project management. We help our clients from the public and non-for-profit sectors to carry out Impact Assessments and policy evaluation. Future Needs also offers networking, dissemination, exploitation and community building services. We do so by working with a variety of stakeholders ranging from technical specialists, key industry players, policy-makers and citizen groups.

entityName: Eigen Vermogen Instituut voor Natuur- en Bosonderzoek
entityDescription: EV INBO is the contractor and legal entity of the Research Institute for Nature and Forest (INBO). INBO is an institute of the Ministry of Environment, Nature and Agriculture and is the Flemish research and knowledge centre for nature and its sustainable management and use. It has about 200 employees. Through its scientific research, INBO supports all agencies dealing with open space in the Flemish government, as well as organisations involved in nature conservation, forestry, agriculture, hunting and fishery. INBO also provides data for international reporting and publishes its results as open data. Via EV INBO, the core INBO research is supplemented, where INBO’s government-supplied financial means are insufficient for deploying a complete and future-oriented research program. This offers the possibility to tackle new research themes with immediate or mid-term policy relevance. EV INBO has been involved in several EU-projects and currently co-ordinates the ALTER-Net network.

entityName: National Institute for Research and Development in Forestry  “Marin Drăcea”
entityDescription:
The National Institute for Research and Development in Forestry “Marin Dracea” - INCDS was established in the year 1933 under the name Forest Research and Experimentation Institute (ICEF), and during 1974-2015 period as Forest Research and Management Institute (ICAS). In the year 2015, based upon the Government’s Decision 318/2015, INCDS was reorganized as national research and development institute under the coordination of National Authority for Scientific Research and Innovation (ANCSI) of the Ministry of Education and Scientific Research.
INCDS “Marin Dracea” is certified as an institution part of the Research and Development System of National Importance and as a Excellence Centre at national level in the field of Forest Biology and Forest Management (classified as ”A”-level). It is licensed for forest management planning, ecological reconstruction and watershed management, forest risk assessment, forest cartography, geodesics and photogrammetry, seeds quality and conservation, and pesticides testing for certifying purposes.
The scientific research and technical development are driven towards priority objectives of forestry sector, in the framework of national and international research programs, specific to the following domains:
-forest ecology,
-forest measurements,
-genetics,
-protection,
-silvotehnics,
-wildgame and fish management,
-management planning,
-watershed management,
-forest shelterbelts
-ecological reconstruction.

On international level, INCDS “Marin Dracea” is member or is cooperating with prestigious international entities: e.g. International Union of Forest Research Organizations (IUFRO), European Forest Institute (EFI), International Co-operative Programme on Assessment and Monitoring of Air Pollution Effects on Forests (ICP-Forests), Long Term Ecological Research European and International Networks (LTER-Europe, ILTER), International Plant Genetic Resources Institute (IPGRI), International Seed Testing Association (ISTA), European Association of Remote Sensing Laboratories (EARSeL), Forest Technology Platform (FTP), European National Forest Inventory Network (ENFIN).

Heiderich is an international consultancy and coaching firm specialized in crisis & issues management.
 
Who We Are
 
Based in Paris, La Réunion & Tunis, Heiderich is leading international provider of crisis management, crisis PR and business continuity services, helping organizations protect their people, performance and reputation from the impact of major disruptions.
We handle preparation, coaching, tutoring, media training, crisis simulation, we respond to real-life crises in complex, difficult and sensitive or in contestation situations, as well as in post-crisis image reconstruction.
 
With more than 300 references in more than 50 countries, many are the companies and organizations have requested over the years our services in crisis management and communication, such as Thalès, Air Liquide Benelux, Leroy-Merlin, the World Health Organization, the World Bank, not to mentions States and governments, cities and communities, administrations and professional administrations.
 
Our consultants come from different backgrounds and come from international firms and companies. They have high experience in crisis management as they have managed a significant number of crisis and complexes situations.
 
What We Do
 
Crisis Preparedness – We assist organization to prepare for the crisis they might put at risk their operations, assets, management and reputation. We help them in particular in identifying crisis scenarios, in defining their crisis management policy, organization, procedures, documentations and plans, as well as response plan designed for specific scenarios.
 
Crisis communication plan – We assist companies and organizations in defining the risks to their reputation, their communication strategy, in determining their response strategy and in the preparation of statements and Q&As.
 
Capacity building and training – We prepare, and train our clients’ management and operation teams in crisis management in order to allow them to face crisis situations.
 
 
24/7/365 rapid-response crisis management team – We assist companies and organization during crisis situation in the situation analysis, the communication and response strategy definition and the definition of action plans.

entityDescription:
The Globe UAV team has been working since 2014 on the idea of using the mobile Internet for full communication with drones.
In March 2016 Globe UAV GmbH was founded as a private company without external investors.
The limitation of the range, especially in the city due to its topography and the many signal absorbing obstacles that use the usual video transmission, leads to the need to use the coverage of the mobile network.
Our focus was on the communication part without losing the human interface of the mind. The idea of an easy to use ground control station with all necessary information on one screen. Since then we have kept the 3 main parts of the flight screen: Live video takes up most of the screen, along with the map showing current position, direction, time and distance of the flight, and weather information. The third part at the bottom is the visualization of the main drone parameters: speed, power consumption, battery life.
One of our first ideas was to find a suitable drone to complete the system from one of the many drone manufacturers in Asia. Unfortunately the flight time was too short for all of them, so we decided to build drones ourselves.
The hardware design and production of each unit is now completely done in Germany.
A UAV, which should be ready for early reactions, we started to design the drones garage in 2018. We quickly gave up the idea of a beach shell-like protection for the drone and, upon request from the military, switched to a steel container, our first "SkyPort". Today we can offer drone hangars in three different sizes: mobile for integration into a truck, the standard SkyPort and the fully self-sufficient Twin Port.

The integration into alarm or dispatcher systems to optimize the pre-arm time of the operation is essential for many customers. A further option of the Globe UAV Ground Control Station is the post-processing of the video analysis in real time and the distribution of the video stream to different devices.

Customers of Globe UAVs include government agencies, security and defense companies as well as airlines and shipping companies.
Recent projects supported by Globe UAVs Transport of human tissue in the centre of Hamburg, AED transport in Greifswald, monitoring of power lines near Leipzig (all Germany).

In the near future we will start VTOL operations and extend our radius of action from 40 to 100 km.

entityName: BIAS - Bremer Institut für angewandte Strahltechnik GmbH
entityDescription:
BIAS – Bremer Institut für angewandte Strahltechnik GmbH (BIAS, GER, engl.: Institute of Applied Beam Technology in Bremen): BIAS is a non-profit limited company founded in 1977 and is located in the north of Germany at the campus of the University of Bremen. The mission of BIAS is to provide research, development and technology transfer to promote the industrial application of lasers with its two core business units “Laser Materials Processing and Processing Systems” and “Optical Metrology and Optoelectronic Systems”. BIAS has carried out research in the field of laser based material processing for over four decades. A wide range of laser sources (up to 12 kW laser power) for laser joining, laser-based and arc-based additive manufacturing and laser-based micro production as well as
equipment for metallographic analysis (sample preparation, light microscopy for etched cross-section polishes, scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray system for element mappings etc.) and mechanical testing (quasi-static and fatigue) are available.

entityName: UNIV FIRENZE - Centro per la Protezione Civile dell'Università di Firenze (CPC)
entityDescription:
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence (CPC-UNIFI) has been constituted in 2018 within the University of Florence in accordance with the article 36 of the Statute of the University of Florence (Italy) and of the University Regulations on Service Centers. 
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence is part of the National Italian Service of Civil Protection, as it is Centre of Competence for Civil Protection in the field of geological risk prevention. The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence is currently composed of about 20 staff people (technicians, administrators, researchers, professors) and several temporary positions (research assistants, research fellows and visiting scientists).
The personnel of CPC-UNIFI is enrolled to the Earth Sciences Department of the University of Florence, one of the largest centres in geological sciences in Italy. The Earth Sciences Department has been recognised since 2005 as national Centre of Competence for Civil Protection in the field of geological risk prevention, until the establishment of CPC-UNIFI. The Italian legislation (Decree of the Italian Prime Minister of 27 February 2004; Decree of the Head of the National Civil Protection Department no. 252 of 25 January 2005, Decree of the Head of the National Civil Protection Department no. 3152 of 24 July 2013) entrusts it with the aims of technological and scientific support for safeguarding the integrity of life, goods, buildings and environment from any damage or risk of damage arising from natural and anthropic disasters. 
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence provides technical and research support to all the University's Civil Protection structures, management of emergencies, prevention and reduction of natural and anthropic hazards and risks. It integrates technical-scientific knowledge and the products derived from research, development and innovation activities as well as academic skills in the Civil Protection network and services in accordance with the article 1 of italian Law 30/2012.
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence has a firm reputation for its research expertise and practical problem solving approach to the geohazards and risk preparedness, prevention and management, which has led to the establishment of solid ties with numerous governmental agencies, private enterprises, national and international research groups as well as with regional, provincial and municipal authorities in charge of Civil Protection and environmental management.
The CPC-UNIFI is strongly linked to the UNESCO Chair on Prevention and Sustaible Management of Geo-hydrological hazards. The UNESCO chair is member of several important international consortia such as: International Consortium on Landslides (ICL) (founding member since 2002); International Consortium on Geo-disaster Reduction (ICGdR) (since 2014); Global Alliance of Disaster Research Institutes (GADRI) (founding member since 2015) and it is signatory of the ISDR-ICL Sendai Partnership 2015-2025 for global promotion of understanding and reducing disaster risk, launched by the International Strategy for Disaster Reduction (ISDR) and by the International Consortium on Landslides (ICL).

entityDescription:
PUT is a nine-Faculty university that educates about 16 000 students at 31 fields of studies. High level of education, qualifications of the teaching and research staff and conducted research make it one of the best technical universities in Poland. Currently in courses leading to Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees, 1600 postgraduate students and 600 students working towards a PhD. PUT employs about 1,300 university teachers. PUT takes an active part in scientific exchange and international projects and cooperate with many companies and research institutions both in Poland and abroad. Among the research and teaching staff are members of the Polish Academy of Sciences as well as three winners of the Foundation for Polish Science, termed the Polish Nobel Prize. PUT works in the field of education with approximately 160 European universities and in the research field with 70 universities located in
the USA, Great Britain, France, Germany, Brazil, China, Japan, Russia, Taiwan and Ukraine.
Practical experience. Contacts with numerous business partners are an essential part of university life. Our partners’ encouragement and advice help us not only to adjust our educational programmes so as to meet the requirements of the market, but primarily, to make our position among other universities stronger. The University cooperates closely with other educational institutions of EU as part of bilateral agreements and it is also a member of such associations: CESAER, SEFI, AUDEM
The PUT is actively seeking funding from national and the Framework Programmes, Structural Funds and other sources (National Centre for Research and Development, National Science Center and Erasmus+). The institution was involved in 29 FP7 projects, of which 6 were coordinated at our university (CSA actions), 19 H2020 projects and 11 Horizon Europe projects so far.

PUT has experience in project management and administration. Research and Development Office at PUT helps scientific coordinators to participate in externally funded projects by assisting and advising during the proposal stage and during the project’s implementation in areas relating to project administration, financial matters and human resources.

entityName: Institutul National de Cercetare-Dezvoltare in Turism
entityDescription:
The National Institute of Research and Development in Tourism - INCDT is the only institution in Romania specialized in scientific research of national interest in the field of tourism, having a vast experience accumulated over its 49 years of continuous activity. The role of INCDT is to substantiate the scientific basis for the development of Romanian tourism, to contribute to increasing the competitiveness of this sector, and to develop national and local strategies in this field.
INCDT has a close cooperation with the Ministry of Tourism, with the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Administration and Ministry of European Funds, as well as with other national and international tourism organizations. Also, INCDT is part of certain associations (European Cultural Tourism Network), clusters specialized in spa and health tourism (Innovative Cluster “Health Factory” - founding member, Regional Balneoturistic Cluster, North-West Transilvania), working groups (Ecotourism Label for Destinations - EU Ecolabel Label - established by the Ministry of Tourism), committees (Commission for Designation of Ecotourism Destinations in Romania, Inter-Institutional Commission for Assessing the Potential of Territorial Tourism, Commission of Evaluation of Tourism Investment Projects of the Ministry of Tourism), thus contributing to the development of the tourism sector through the expertise provided to them.
Our portfolio includes many types of projects (addressed both to public beneficiaries or private ones), as follows: strategies for both national and regional tourism development, as well as strategies targeting tourist destinations, including strategies by various forms of tourism; market studies, business and re-positioning /positioning studies; studies of assessment and exploitation of the natural and cultural potential of tourism and tourist product development; marketing research and strategies; documentations for the certification of localities as tourist destinations, spa resorts, or climatic resorts; databases used in the field of tourism; Tourism expertise for the development of ITC applications for the development and promotion of tourism products, pre-feasibility studies, feasibility studies etc.

entityDescription:
The Gran Sasso Science Institute (GSSI) is an international PhD school and a center for research and higher education in the areas of Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science and Social Sciences.
As a project supported by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the GSSI has been instituted as a new Italian graduate school of advanced studies in 2016, after a three-years succesful experimental period. Located in central Italy, the school welcomes professors, researchers and students selected internationally following the best graduate schools standards worldwide. The PhD program is organized in the scientific areas of Astroparticle Physics, Mathematics, Computer science, Regional Sciences and Economic Geography. Every year we offer Post doctoral grants and research opportunities thus facilitating the attraction of high-level resources in the fields of natural and social sciences.
Through a day-to-day collaboration and interaction, researchers and students have the opportunity to build a sound knowledge of the research methods and to experiment contamination of interests, innovative approaches and multicultural exchanges in all the GSSI activities. In addressing the complexity of today’s world, we are committed to removing all barriers between the GSSI areas of study and research, where interdisciplinarity and cross-fertilization underlie everything we do. Among our goals are the dissemination of scientific results towards society and the promotion of cultural events for generic public, citizens and schools.
Our main goal is to strengthen the scientific excellence in L’Aquila area, where many skills and highly specialized structures, such as the Gran Sasso National Laboratories of the National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN) and the University of L'Aquila, are already present. Further, our Institute intends to promote collaborations with many national and international institutions and to interact with public and private realities in order to stimulate innovation and knowledge based communities.
