COMTES FHT is a private R&D institute focused on metallurgy, materials development, and testing. Since 2007 the main facility is located in Dobřany near Pilsen/CZ. In 2016, COMTES FHT opened its sales office for German-speaking countries in Munich. In 2020 a new Technology Park was established near the main COMTES FHT's facility in Dobřany production facilities, offices and technical support for small and medium sized enterprices
As an accredited laboratory and provider of engineering services, COMTES FHT cooperates with prestigious companies, such as Skoda, Benteler, Schaeffler, Schmolz+Bickenbach, and others. We provide industry-relevant solutions to a variety of technical problems. In our metallurgical pilot plant we conduct laboratory and trial melts of up to 500 kg using vacuum induction melting technology. Our facilities are also equipped for forging, hot and cold rolling and heat treatment of metals. Special material based solutions are being developed using additive manufacturing technologies. Our materials testing laboratory offers comprehensive services including optical and scanning electron microscopy, mechanical testing, and measurement of the thermo-physical properties of materials. We also carry out optimization of complex technological processes using computer simulation.

DataminingLab UK is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Elder Research, Inc.

Elder Research is a recognized leader in data science consulting. We partner with commercial clients and government agencies to deliver value through analytic consulting and actionable solutions to business problems.

OUR MISSION
To provide our clients with analytic consulting that enhances our client's mission while maintaining a culture that values learning, humility, and work-life balance.
WHAT WE DO
We enable organizations to successfully extract value from their data and resources by delivering the most trusted and valuable strategy, training, and analytic solutions in the industry.
OUR VISION
Our vision is to be the most trusted and sought after analytic consulting firm in the industry with a diversity of experience that allows us to serve the best interests of our clients.
WHY ELDER RESEARCH?
We take an interdisciplinary approach to predictive analytics consulting, drawing from cutting-edge academic research and decades of successful experience in the engineering, finance, statistics, and software development fields. We value creativity, engagement, and organizational understanding as well as technical expertise. We are constantly learning, and it is the quality of our people as much as the power of our analytics solutions that delivers value for our clients.
OUR STORY
Elder Research is the most experienced consultancy specializing in data science and advanced analytics solutions. We create a sustainable competitive advantage for clients by combining creative people, proven systems engineering, and custom software to deliver actionable solutions that transform data into business value. Elder Research can provide analytics consulting support throughout the journey—from training and mentoring, to creating stand-alone analytic solutions, to helping build a team to develop solutions in-house. We solve business problems as well as data problems.
Founded in 1995 by Dr. John Elder, Elder Research is headquartered in Charlottesville, Virginia, with offices in Washington, DC, Baltimore, Maryland, Raleigh, North Carolina, and London, England.
Our commercial experience includes analytic engagements for industry leaders such as Capital One, Solidworks, Hewlett-Packard, British Petroleum, GEICO, John Hancock, Oppenheimer Funds, Target, nTelos, DentaQuest and AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals. Our experience in consulting with the federal government includes multi-year contracts to provide analytics services to many agencies including the Department of Defense, Department of Homeland Security, Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Social Security Administration, the U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, and others. Our contract vehicles with the General Services Administration (GSA) and NIST 800-171 data security standards make Elder Research a preferred vendor for many government organizations.

entityDescription:
Ecole Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées (also known as École des Ponts ParisTech), created in 1747 under the name École Royale des Ponts et Chaussées, is a higher education establishment that trains engineers to a high level of scientific, technical and general competency. Apart from civil engineering and spatial planning, historically the source of its prestige, the School develops high-quality programs and research associated with the energy transition. École des Ponts ParisTech provides a very high-level education in general engineering.

The Graduate School, underpinned by the excellence of its 12 research labs, develops Masters and PhD programs in mechanical and civil engineering, materials sciences, nuclear engineering, mathematics, information technology, environmental sciences, urban planning, transportation, economics, and sociology.
Through its subsidiaries or in its own right, it develops initial education and lifelong learning that are closely connected with different sectors of the economy.
It is therefore a key player in lifelong learning for senior executives in its prime disciplines.

entityDescription:
The French Interprofessional Technical Centre for Studies on Air Pollution (known as CITEPA) was established in 1961 and its legal status is a non-profit making organisation. Today, it has around 100 members (industry, trade federations and bodies, energy utilities, car manufacturers, eco-industries, consultancies, pollution measuring laboratories, public agencies, etc.). It constitutes an extensive interprofessional network in which relevant, up-to-date information is exchanged on legislative, regulatory and technological developments in the field of air pollution control and climate change mitigation. CITEPA brings together experts, particularly in industry, keen to take on their responsibilities on the basis of consultation and objectivity, with the aim of identifying and implementing ways of reducing emissions in a realistic and changing technical, economic and regulatory context. CITEPA has a staff of 20, three-quarters of whom are engineers. Its current President is Marc Larzillière and its Director Jean-Pierre Fontelle.
 
Since 2004, CITEPA has been certified ISO 9001: 2008, as awarded by the French Association for Quality Assurance (AFAQ), for its studies' and inventories' work. This certification has been renewed each year since 2004 as a result of different follow-up audits.

entityDescription:
With 20 years’ experience in coating technology and equipment engineering, THEVA manufactures high-temperature superconductors (HTS) for loss-free transmission of extremely high electric current. With its patented production technology, the company has a unique approach to superconductor manufacture. The company has invested over fifteen years in development to build Germany’s first commercial HTS production plant. Today, THEVA is the only producer of HTS wire in the EU. Thanks to its very high energy density, THEVA Pro-Line superconductor wire can replace conventional copper conductors in high-performance applications and opens up entirely new possibilities for the construction of electrical components. Manufacturers of cables, power switches, large electric drives and power rails can rely on the high quality and performance of the material. Due to its low weight compared to copper conductors the HTS wires are especially suitable for space applications.
Additionally to the HTS wire, THEVA also produces coils and other HTS wire related products and measurement systems, like the Tapestare measurement system.

THEVA stands for high-end high temperature superconducting wire products and measurement systems.

entityDescription:
Everbridge mission is to=: Keep people safe and businesses running. Faster!

We provide Software as a Server solutions for Critical Event Management

A critical event is a disruptive incident which poses serious risk or threat to assets or people. An effective Critical Event Management program and strategy is an integrated, end-to-end process that enables organizations to significantly speed up responses to critical events and improve outcomes by mitigating or eliminating the impact of a threat. Imagine your business continuity, disaster recovery, active assailant, emergency response, natural disaster, IT incident risk management, and mass notification all rolled up into an easy-to-execute, strategic plan with long-term benefits.
The four components of CEM include:

INTELLIGENCE
Proactively assess potential threats before they become critical events. With the right built-in risk intelligence and data feeds, supported by 24/7 analysts, your organization can leverage thousands of sources of data across weather, protest, social media, dark web, and hyper-local safety feeds to curate, filter and categorize risk events. This ensures a faster response to threats in order to avoid false positives and make better decisions.
CORRELATION
Align risk events to assets using a dynamic correlation engine that combines static location, expected location and last known location of people and assets. CEM can take this a step further by considering time elements to determine who or what is impacted by threats, in order to reach them faster and more decisively.
ORCHESTRATION
Automated workflows ensure that even when you and your team are not watching for threats, the system is doing it for you. SOPs, communications, and action plans can be automated and orchestrated during a crisis in order to speed up response and ensure that the appropriate action is taken for a particular threat.
ANALYTICS
With CEM, metrics are built-in throughout the process to ensure the right action is taken by the right people, at the right time, and to understand how effective actions were and how you can do better in the future.

The Governmental Agency for Information-Technology Development (KIFÜ) operates under the supervision of the Ministry of Innovation and Technology. KIFÜ carries out its activities defined in the government decree 268/2010. (XII. 3.) and 5/2011. (II.3) .
KIFÜ's activities can be divided into two major areas: 
- developing and operating IT infrastructure, and provision of services based on this infrastructure to national K12 education, higher education and academia, research institutes and public collections.
- project management and quality assurance of national or EU funded IT projects from preparation to implementation and to completion,
In the recent years our institute played a major role in implementing approximately 100 IT projects. Currently, we are involved in 20 ongoing projects and preparing 10 other projects. 
KIFÜ implements Hungary’s most extensive broadband infrastructure development programme, the SZIP (High-speed Internet Programme), which aims at providing with high-speed internet access by the end of 2020 each Hungarian household, enterprise, and public institute requiring that.
In 2018, KIFÜ was appointed to modernize the network access to meet the requirements of the modern age in thousands of schools, providing wifi access to students and teachers based on the principles defined in the Digital Education Strategy and within the frameworks of the »Diákháló« Programme.
Our more than 300 colleagues pay special attention to knowledge and experience sharing. We intend to enhance the country's digitalization, the digital transformation of Hungary.

entityDescription:
Entropy is a leader in providing thermal technologies and simulation solutions for rugged embedded environments. We continue to produce and develop leading products that will achieve, and help test, maximum operating performance for electronic systems in harsh environments.
With the current focus on interoperability, and the relentless increase of thermal power density in silicon devices, embedded systems and ruggedized chassis need a focus on driving SWAP-C optimisation more than ever. Our solutions, with new technology and excellent engineering, target the mechanical packaging opportunities this challenge provides and allows our customers to produce best in class products.
Using extensive experience working in MilAero packaging design, we also support: design of improved thermal solutions for all VITA-48.x and IEEE1101.x specifications, provide predictive life simulations to support VITA-51.x, and validate extended shock and vibration requirements in accordance with MIL-STD-810 and GEVS-SE.
Entropy specialises exclusively in the Defence, Avionics and Space giving our customers improved design confidence and reduced time to delivery that other solutions providers can not. We focus primarily on the root cause of thermal loading, which is typically the silicon core architecture of the product and have optimised the methods extracting heat from these devices. In order to be highly effective, our approach uses detailed chip level modelling of devices such as:
• Intel Core, Xeon and Atom processors
• Xilinx Ultrascale+
• Nvidia Jetson SoM, Quadro Turing, Pascal and GTX
• AMD Ryzen and Epyc
All our solutions are carefully validated against representative testing data. We are confident that by using first class experience in this challenging industry, by rigorously employing engineering fundamental principles, and the application of leading simulation skills that your product will be as ready for the field as possible.

entityDescription:
Founded in 1968 and independently managed since January 1st 2012, the University of Toulon (UTLN) places the University’s attractiveness at the core of its long-term strategic plan.
Well-established throughout the region, the University of Toulon works closely with the region’s social and economic institutions to tailor its academic programmes and research activities to their needs.
The University of Toulon is an interdisciplinary institution with 3 campuses. The University offers a hundred different degrees (excluding medical school) and operates 15 Research Units.

Some research activities at the university of Toulon involve spatial Earth Observation. In particular, the Mediterranean Institute of Oceanography makes use of satellite data to complement the biophysical observation and modeling of the ocean surface. It is also operating oceanographic HF radars for the real-time monitoring of coastal Mediterranean surface currents. These measurements can be very valuable for the calibration & validation of coastal altimetric missions or Doppler-based surface currents measurements.

The "Laboratoire Informatique et Systèmes" (LIS) is an engineering science laboratory, bringing together computer scientists and signal processing and control process researchers. LIS researchers are working in the field of deep learning, signal and image processing, optimal control.

entityDescription:
Eight Bells (8BELLS) is an independent Research and Consulting company specializing in selected parts of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) as well as in modelling and analysis for businesses, based in Nicosia, Cyprus. The company was established in 2016 by ICT researchers and market analysts pursuing the application of their research expertise and innovations in the ICT related arena.
In the consulting domain, 8BELLS delivers special advisory services in ICT that help our clients understand the market dynamics and profit from the ever-changing landscape. Working side by side with our clients allows us to better understand their business requirements and using a data-driven approach we create tailor-made solutions to support them. From identifying a new investment opportunity, through to evaluating, implementing and distributing it, 8BELLS can advise and support other companies and organizations in every step of the process. Business consulting includes also innovation management, technology transfer and exploitation (including market analysis, patenting, licensing, etc.).
The main areas of research and technical expertise are customizable solutions that enhance modern communications relevant to the area of 5G Mobile Technology, Network Function Virtualization (NFV), and management solutions for Cloud infrastructures. The company possesses a portfolio of cybersecurity solutions that can be used for risk assessment, cyber-hygiene, anomaly detection, and threat remediation.
The analysts of 8BELLS have a strong focus on R&D with a long track record in EU- and national-funded research initiatives. They have actively participated in (and coordinated) several R&D projects in the field of networking and telecommunications and have authored or co-authored over 80 papers in international refereed journals and conferences. Moreover, the company’s portfolio includes system engineering and integration services, network design and implementation, R&D consultancy, as well as targeted and customized innovative solutions. Our technical capabilities also include:
·Systems & Networks engineering: Including design, implementation and integration,
·Cloud Computing and Everything-as-a-Service:Design, deployment and maintenance of cloud computing infrastructure, Optimised resource provisioning in Infrastructure-as-a-Service architecture, Platform or Software as-a-Service for quick implementation and instantiation of cloud services,
·Privacy, Security & Data Protection:Cybersecurity Gap Analysis, Virtualised Cybersecurity, Privacy Impact Assessment, Privacy-by-design architectures, ethical and legal compliance of project activities, including compliance to the new General Data Protection Regulation,
·Software development:for 5G security, wireless network security, software quality assurance, machine learning applications, data analysis and visualization, cloud computing, etc.

As a highly innovative company, 8BELLS has achieved to participate in H2020 projects as peer partner, and in one national project of the Cypriot Defense Ministry.

entityDescription:
Professor Rolf Rossaint, a co-founder of Docs in Clouds, got the initial idea in 2004: Could telemedicine/telehealth be used to optimize processes for German emergency services, ensure quality of service, and improve the deployment of medical personnel? After 10 years of R+D, the Emergency TeleDoc system was conceived, and it hasbeen an integral part of the local emergency services of Aachen since 2014. With the help of our partner company,P3 telehealthcare, all ambulances were retrofitted with the TeleDoc system, and we established a communication hub staffed 24/7. Inspired by this success, other local communities are currently adopting the system. More information atwww.telenotarzt.de.

Since then, we expanded our focus on other fields, which benefit from telemedical applications. Our TeleDoc software now support general practioners, nursing homes and outpatient nursing services. Currently, our company is organized into three business units: Telecare (focuses on telemedicine for nursing and medical care), Medical Engineering Services and Innovation (Research & Development). Because biomedical engineering is a multidisciplinary field, our team includes both physicians and engineers, which work hand in hand. This interaction allows us to develop products and provide services that fit the current market need. Our physicians contribute with medical input; in addition, they are aware of the current clinical weaknesses and needs. Our engineers, in turn, develop solutions combining technical knowledge, innovation, creativity and practicality. What drives us: Bringing medical care to people, faster and more effectively!
Despite of the medical background, our products do not necessarily need to be applied in the medical field. In fact, they can be translated to other areas. This is the case of the TeleExpert system: specialists can offer prompt support anywhere in the world. Within this context, project costs, operational costs, and more importantly, time can be saved.

entityDescription:
GEO Solutions is part of the Cronos Group, an ICT Group of more than 6000 specialists in Belgium. 
Within Cronos, all "geo" activities were grouped in the CLUSTER GEO SQUARE (approximately 220 people with a turnover of approximately 30 M€), of which the company GEO Solutions (almost 80 people with a turnover of approximately 8 M€) is the largest and takes the service share for itself. GEO Solutions has offices in Edegem (HQ), Merelbeke, Leuven and Namur.
We position GEO Solutions as a "Geo-ICT" company, specialized in ICT applications where a geographical component is decisive for a good support of the business processes.
We use 4 spearheads: Geodata, Telematics, Geo-ICT/GIS, and Internet of Things (IoT).
From this angle we already work for many (semi-) government organizations. Some examples are: National Geographic Institute, AGIV/AIV, Flemish Department of Mobility and Public Works, Spatial Planning and Housing, Fluxys, Telenet, De Watergroep, Voo, Agency Roads and Traffic, Belgian Federal Police, Sibelga, Fluvius, Tourism Flanders, Province of Antwerp, Flemish Brabant, The Flemish Waterway, ...
 
For most of these customers, we work on projects that start from an 'enterprise' vision of the (geographical) assets of an organization that are necessary for the business processes. This can be management for heritage or land but also infrastructure, mobile workers, logistics processes, the network, the fleet, etc. Very important is often also the document flow behind these processes: financial documents, title deeds, municipal registers, plans, ...
 
One of our greatest strengths is our technological independence and architectural flexibility. Within the GIS niche market, we are undoubtedly most focused on the overall ICT operation of an organization and the main integrator of GIS in an existing and broad ICT architecture. We work on the basis of the enterprise architecture principles. For large organizations, this often translates as integration of GIS into a Service Oriented Architecture.
 
In terms of platforms and technologies, we work with both open source components and licensed products (Esri, Hexagon Intergraph, Mapinfo, Luciad, Bentley, ...). Besides being a privileged partner of TomTom, we are also exclusive Google Maps partner in the Benelux. 
 
We have specialized people in both java-GIS, .net-GIS and mobile GIS development. As far as geodata is concerned, we work together with private partners such as TomTom & Google and are very familiar with the public datasets of GRB, Mercator, Urbis, PICC, land registry, ...
 
Our services are provided by both individual consultants and consultants in a team, both in means and in result commitment. An important asset is that we can manage (large) projects from initiative to delivery completely ourselves in close consultation with the customer. For this we use proven methodologies.
As mentioned above, GEO Solutions has about 80 Geo-ICT specialists who cover the full picture of GIS profiles: GIS architect, GIS analyst, GIS data expert, GIS consultant, GIS project leaders, GIS developers, .net/java/… developers, ...

Hydrohm is a spin-off company from Ghent University (Belgium), that will bring electrochemical technologies for water treatment to the market. Electrification is an emerging trend, notably in road transport and the chemical industries, because electricity is a renewable input that leaves no residues. We believe there is a huge potential for electrification in the water sector. It allows for more local water treatment (e.g. on building level), and can replace a number of processes that now require dosing of chemicals, which come at an economic and environmental cost.
Hydrohm will develop and commercialize new electrochemical technologies, for wastewater treatment and drinking water production.

entityDescription:
With a history that dates back to 1969, INDAERO consolidates as a company in 2002 by manufacturing engraved plates and labels for AIRBUS. Two years later, it makes its way into the world of machining, expanding its services in the manufacture of aeronautical parts, and subsequently certifying itself to the EN9100 Aerospace standard.
In 2010, it expanded its area radius and began to export products in Europe, specifically to Austria and Poland. Two years later, it forms the GRUPO EMERGY business alliance in which, thanks to its strategic union with UNS, it achieves an immersion in the sheet metal transformation market, including laser cutting, folding and manual and robotic welding processes.
Since 2013, GRUPO EMERGY began to work with additive manufacturing, using high resistance thermoplastics to manufacture hybrid tools and soluble molds for composites. In 2017 it achieved international recognition thanks to its participation in the AIRBUS NH90 project.
In 2018, thanks to a wide investment in technology, among which 5-axis CNC's and a 6-axis Absolute Arm measuring arm stand out, GRUPO EMERGY manages to enter the Aerospace sector with high-precision machining for very important international projects.
Thanks to the avant-garde vision of its work team, its resilience and constant investment in technology, GRUPO EMERGY has today more than 1,750 square meters of facilities, which provide its customers with a comprehensive service and cutting-edge technology, at your fingertips.

entityDescription:
CoopCulture is one of the leading players in the field of cultural heritage in Italy and its core business is strictly linked to the promotion and the access of cultural heritage through specialized services’ systems and new storytellings.
CoopCulture works in almost every region of the country, managing 250 cultural sites including some of Italian main landmarks -such as the Colosseum in Rome, the National Archeological Museum in Naples, the Blue Cave at Capri isle, the Temples’ Valley in Agrigento- and many less known cultural sites and areas, historically and artistically very rich.
CoopCulture offers work position to more than 1700 employees who welcome more than 13,5 millions visitors per year, that benefit of multiple cultural products designed and implemented by our Research & Development division.
CoopCulture offers a wide range of products and services aimed to empower tourists’ cultural experiences:
· at museums and exhibitions, CoopCulture manages welcoming services, booking and ticketing offices, didactics, marketing & communication services, bookshop and culture concept stores;
· at libraries and archives, CoopCulture manages activities such as: library management, computerized cataloguing, public services for reading and borrowing, educational services and workshop activities;
· in order to give value to the so called overspread heritage and to all linked territories, CoopCulture is able to promote complex networking systems through integrated touristic cards and territorial digital platforms.
CoopCulture deeply works on audience development, aiming to enlarge audiences in terms of numbers, to wide the range of different cultural audiences (attracting the youth and the elderly, working for people with special needs, involving also people coming from different cultural and social backgrounds), and to increase the relationship with them.
The concept of deepening relations, diversifying audiences, engaging the so- called new users has recently been stressed through the powerful raid of the new technological paradigm and the digital revolution which have fully and deeply modified the access and the distribution of cultural products despite of social and economical barriers.
That is why, from the ‘90s till up today, all around Italy CoopCulture’s audiences have been able to count on several technological tools: from the audio and video guides, which started supporting guide tours at the end of the last century, to the first MP3’s for kids and the first audioguide based on the Italian language of signs. Later on, our researches for new ways of engaging people have brought us, first, in 2015, to the experience of the Critic Globus, a big egg placed at the second stair of the Colosseum, which visitors entered in order to record own evaluations about the Earth as “mother of life”, as main topic of a linked temporary exhibitions; then, in the same year, to analyze users’ needs while travelling within territories in order to design the ArtPlanner, a digital platform dedicated to local areas and overspread heritage and to those temporary citizens who want to explore and experience different cultural life styles by customizing their own itineraries; to Caracalla IV Dimension in 2017, a headset housing a mobile phone and dedicated software, which allows visitors to explore in virtual reality, the ancient Baths of Caracalla in Rome as they really looked like in 216 AD.

entityName: UNIVERSITY OF ROMA TRE - Dipartimento di Scienze
entityDescription:
Università degli Studi "Roma Tre" in Rome, Italy, is born in 1992 and currently has About 34.000 students. Its numbers saying that from the born it has had already about 100.000 graduates with about 1500 students with International Experiences (ERASMUS, etc.). The University has 98 Degree Courses (30 indergraduate, 45 master’s degree, 23 PhD), 42 Courses Post Lauream, 12 Departments among these, for the Italian's law 7 were eligible as Excellent Departments and 4 were elected as Excellent Departments (Law, Engineering, Math and Phisics, Science). 

The Science Department, is an interdisciplinary Department in which many skills converge to develop different and multidisciplinary kind of researches. Whitin the Science Department there is a group of engineers drived by Professor Fabio Leccese that leads the Electric and Electronic Measurement Laboratory involved in many research activities and, specifically, since 2012, in aerospace researches. 
In particular, the Laboratory studies how the typical topic of the Measurement Science can support and can produce proactive information in the development of the Aerospace activities. In this general context, the research is particularly focused on the evaluation of the Resilience of autonomous complex systems (as Satellites, Extraterrestrial devices, etc.) searching to evaluate their Operational Availability of the devices and so their Autonomic Logistic. The Laboratory has all the competences to design, develop and build electronic devices even for aerospace field.

More than 30 scientific papers heve been produced in this field, even with the collaboration of SeTeL s.r.l..

In reference to this project, our Laboratory, in collaboration with Se.Te.L., developed an ELT/S according to COSPAR-SARSAT specification.

entityDescription:
AQCLab Software Quality, although created as a company in 2019, is actually a spinoff of Intelligent Environments (previously registered with ESA), which was created in 2006. However, due to the specialization of AQCLab as the first internationally accredited laboratory for the evaluation of software product quality, in 2019 the management of IE decided to make it a company on its own and that is when AQCLab Software Quality was born. 

AQCLab is composed of highly qualified professionals (Engineers and PhDs in Computer Science) with experience in software and data quality, software development and maintenance methodologies, process and project management, governance and auditing, and business engineering. 

The company is committed to innovation, with continuous interaction with the university environment, as we consider research and innovation to be essential elements for the improvement and sustainability of information systems, having participated in more than 10 R+D+i projects in recent years.

AQCLab specializes in measuring, evaluating and improving the quality of software and data. As a result of this, AQCLab was accredited as the first and only laboratory at an international level that is accredited by ENAC (National Accreditation Entity) and ILAC for the evaluation of software product and data quality, following the good practices of the international standard ISO/IEC 25000.

Thanks to AQCLab's assessments, organizations can not only evaluate and improve the quality of their software and data, but also obtain a quality certification in ISO/IEC 25000, issued by a certification body such as AENOR.

entityDescription:
Beskid Plus is a family-owned company.I have been running it with my long-term friend since the early 1990s, and 10 years ago we were joined by our sons. Over 20 years back, we were the first in Poland to offer acid-free storage products for various kinds of collections. Since we have been working closely with the environment of Polish archivists and carefully following both European and global trends in archiving, we have been able to extend our range of products over the years. Currently, we are the leader in the Polish market of long-term archival storage products.
We know very well that proper storage of collections is not an abstract matter, interesting only to a few archivists who work in inaccessible institutions. It is a matter of importance to all of us, as those who benefit from culture, as readers and as citizens. It is a matter of preserving cultural heritage for future generations.It is our cultural “to be or not to be.”

We are aware of this responsibility, and therefore the best quality possible is what we care about at every step of the way: from the choice of paper, paperboard and cardboard, which we import from numerous places in Europe and worldwide, through dedication to every little detail at the stage of box and folder production, to proper packaging of finished products for transport and delivery.
Our storage products comply with the strict requirements ofISO 9706andISO 16245international standards. We are the leading supplier to the Polish National Archives, and in the recent years we have been gaining more and more clients abroad, most of all in Austria, Germany and Scandinavian countries. Our storage products are used to store and protect the most valuable collections of Polish and European archiving institutions, libraries and museums. I am certain that we can meet the needs of the most demanding clients.

entityDescription:
Experientia is an award-winning international user experience research and design consultancy.

We have operational offices in Turin and Milan, Italy, Basel, Switzerland, and Singapore. Using a human-centered design approach, our service designers help companies and organizations innovate their products and services through a qualitative understanding of people, their mental models and their behaviours.
Our services cover research & assessment, service design, interaction design, testing and solution deployment
We are an international point of reference for human-centred design. Our main skills are:
- Unique capabilities in ethnographic research —> We use ethnographic research and behavioural modelling to transform customer insights into practical, cognitive frameworks that can be widely shared and applied.
- User-centered innovation methodologies —> We balance user-centered design, research and solid design thinking methodologies to create meaningful and innovative solutions to complex challenges.
- Collaborative stakeholder engagement process
—> Our participatory methods include client stakeholders in the process to generate collaborative solutions to challenging issues.
- Unique expertise in design disciplines
—> Experientia staff is at the forefront of service and interaction design, creating extraordinary results through global understanding of design and experience in solid processes.
Our approach employs research-based methods to gain a thorough understanding of the challenge. Cognitive modelling then structures the field research insights into a behavioral and cultural framework. This allows us to map out hidden opportunities or adjacent possibilities of intervention that we use to design interface or service solutions.
Experientia’s rich qualitative research methodology includes strong expertise in desk, field and lab research, combining a variety of research methodologies, all driven by a strong emphasis on people’s contexts and behaviors, allowing us to support clients in gaining a deep understanding of the problem and its framework.These include focused desk research, foresight studies, contextual observation, heuristic evaluations, focus groups, in-depth interviews, ethnographic research and usability testing.
Experientia’s client roster features Italian and international clients, such as 3M, Amgen, Bologna Airport, Deutsche Telekom, DesignSingapore Council, EIT-Digital, Embraco, European Commission, FCA Group, Hitachi, Intel, Intesa Sanpaolo bank, Moretti Costruzioni, Netflix, Repower, Roche, Samsung Electronics, Sitra, Takeda, Tarkett, The Coca-Cola Company, UniCredit bank, Vodafone and Wistron
Our research areas are also very global. Over the last years we have conducted research in Australia, Belgium, Canada, Chile, Denmark, China, Egypt, Finland, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Malaysia, Mexico, Senegal, Singapore, South Africa, Sweden, Spain, Switzerland, Taiwan, UK and USA.

entityDescription:
Corsica Sardinia Elba Ferries – Step by Step…In 1968 Pascal P. Lota, from Bastia, founded the shipping company Corsica Line. The first ferry was the “Corsica Express”, capable of carrying 600 passengers and 60 vehicles.
From 1968 to 1981 the ferry company Corsica Ferries developed its main market: the passage between Italy and Corsica. 
The company grew and crossings to France were introduced. 
In 1973, the Company was renamed Corsica Ferries and became one of the world's largest shipping companies.
Step by step the Yellow Ships became a synonym for comfort and quality. 
1981: with the acquisition of the Italian company TTE, Sardinia Ferries joined Corsica Ferries. 
Now the company could also offer passages between Sardinia and Italy. The ship "Sardinia Nova" was the first yellow ferry to connect Livorno and Olbia. 
In 1996 the fast ferry (HSC) Corsica Express opened the route Nice-Corsica. The fast ferries made it possible to enter into the market of crossings between the French mainland and Corsica. Such a fast ferry was also used between Italy and Sardinia. 
In 2001 the Mega Express Class was introduced which made various new routes possible: between Toulon and the ports of Ajacco, Calvi, Ile Rousse and Bastia and between Livorno and Golfo Aranci (Sardinia). 
Today, the company has a fleet of 13 ships (8 Mega Express, 2 Cruise Ferries, 2 Day Ferries and 1 HSC Express) and operates services to Corsica and Sardinia all year round and to Elba and Balearic Islands, during the summer, and carrying more than 3.7 million passengers per year and over 1.2 million vehicles.

Cosmian is a software publisher focused on solving the data paradox : unlocking data access and sharing in the data economy while providing higher levels of security and privacy for sensitive and confidential data.

Cosmian software solutions (deployable in our client's on-premises IT or cloud environment) leverage cryptographic techniques to protect sensitive data during computation : data is protected via encryption and remains fully protected & confidential during its processing.

Besides securing data pipelines in data science and machine learning projects, this capability opens up new fields of use cases such as the possibility for two companies to virtually pool data for a common calculation without either company/entity seeing the other's data, without having to rely on a third party and without ever having access to the underlying data.

Xetal NV is a Belgian start-up founded in 2013 developing solutions based on an innovative high-resolution indoor people detection and tracking technology that does not need the wearables, phones or cameras. Our technology relies on proprietary positioning sensors based on temperature sensing. The sensors can be placed on walls, beds or ceiling. They can also be easily embedded in furniture, consumer products and alike. Each sensor allow to detect and track of one or more people with an accuracy of about 30cm. When such an accurate position information is used together with knowledge about the room itself, it is possible to understand what is happening in the room, what people are doing and determine what is likely to happen next. Xetal technology does not use cameras, audio or any other identification technology making it the perfect technology for when respect for personal privacy is a must.

entityDescription:
Organic Services is an international strategy and business consultancy for the food industry with particular focus on the organic sector. Drawing on more than 30 years of industry experience, we advise growers and grower groups, traders and certifiers as well as public and private organizations. Our mission: more sustainability and transparency throughout the food supply chain. Our services are interdisciplinary and tailored to the needs of our customers and project partners. We support clients in strategic business development and market studies, certification and accreditation systems and transfer knowledge by organizing conferences and study trips.
For more than 15 years Organic Services has been the global sales partner for Intact’s Platform ERP certification management solution, the international market leader.
Being experts in the field of integrity management solutions, we also offer three innovative software tools for various players along the supply chain:
· Check Integrity is a cloud platform that maps and links certification and transaction data along the supply chain. Based on the certified acreage, yield and transaction data, the system calculates a mass balance and shows in real time whether the quantities requested in a specific quality are actually (still) tradable. These plausibility checks reveal food fraud even before the product is sold on the market. By applying Check Integrity, farmer as well as companies can prove the integrity of their products towards their buyers, a great advantage in marketing. Check Integrity is a generic tool that can be used in all product chains. In the organic sector, the platform is known as Check Organic and prevents conventional products from entering the supply chain as fake high-quality organic products.
· Group Integrity is a tailor-made solution for the professional management of internal control systems of grower groups as well as of companies with contracted smallholders that produce for national or international markets. The online-based tool professionalizes data collection and processing. It prepares grower groups optimally for external audits and for the certification against private and public quality standards.
· Ecert Basic is the standard application of the Intact Platform ERP certification management for local and small certification bodies. Within a defined workflow, control and certification processes are well structured, and procedures such as deadline management are automated. The clear workflow increases transparency, continuity and comprehensiveness and allows for high quality standards.
The combination of the three systems Check Integrity/ Check Organic, Group Integrity and Ecert Basic considerably facilitates the collaboration between supply chain actors, for example between a farmer group and their external certification body. This creates synergies that can benefit the industry as a whole. The verification of product provenience underscores the integrity of supply chains in the market.

Saab Deutschland GmbH Product Unit EW (EWD) in Germany has been delivering solutions to the intelligence community and regulatory authorities worldwide for more than 40 years. We have developed our expertise specifically in the fields of radio signal measurement and analysis, SIGINT, ESM and Information Fusion.

We develop and deliver systems for radio surveillance, big data analysis and border surveillance. These include broadband signal acquisition, signal analysis, automatic detection and classification of radio signals, their demodulation, decoding and speech processing, direction finding and geo-location.

In summary, we focus on the following objectives:
- Radio signal analysis for all operational users for all dimensions
- Situational awareness and situation picture creation
- Border surveillance using technical means, including situation picture and sensor fusion
- Radio emission location, also in urban scenarios
- Fusion of data, different sensors (e.g. COMINT, ELINT, OSINT et al.)
- Detection of wrong / fake / missing transponder signals (AIS, ADS-B)
- Analysis of unidentified signals
- Monitoring of frequency spectra (ITU)
- Identification and geo-location of interference sources

entityDescription: The Institute of Marine Sciences of Andalusia, belonging for the Spanish National Research Council, has been located on the University Campus of Puerto Real (Cadiz) since 1986, when it moved from its previous building in the Port of Cadiz. The new location was chosen primarily so that the Institute could maintain very close links with the Faculty of Sciences of the University of Cadiz and to the planned Faculty of Marine Sciences, which was completed a few years later. Thus a compact nucleus of reference for marine research was created. An additional new building for the ICMAN, with laboratories and offices, was opened in 2008. Two years later another new building equipped for experimentation with aquatic animals was opened. In 2012, the Institute became a founder member of the CEI·MAR (Campus of International Excellence of the Sea/Oceans) which groups together several Universities and Scientific Institutions of Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

entityDescription:
The Department of Lands and Surveys "DLS" is probably the most important pillar of socio-economic development in our country, as it deals with the land, which is one of the leading factors for progress, prosperity and development in the Cypriot economy. With its present operational structure and responsibilities, through a wide range of Laws and Regulations, the Department is one of the most essential services of the Public Sector, making a most important contribution to all sectors of activity of the Cypriot society. The DLS provides the basis for the design of all development programs relating to immovable property, offering services to many public sector entities, such as local authorities, bodies governed by public law, banking and other organizations and more generally all citizens.
The Department is solely responsible for the provision of services in connection with all the rights relating to immovable property - registration, valuation, general assessment (for tax purposes), tenure, surveying, cartography, geodesy and hydrography, as well as the management of all property belonging to the State. An important strategic aim of the DLS is the consolidation of its multidimensional role and its modernization / transformation into a productive and modern organization.
Undoubtedly, the DLS is the main source of data relating to real property. The data in conjunction with the procedures generating and supporting them are the main and core asset of the Department. Their further use and utilization becomes an imperative need, as these data in order to be productive, should first of all be structured correctly and at the same time, through interoperability, be available primarily horizontally, across the Public Sector, to other bodies, businesses, researchers and ultimately the citizen himself.
The Administration of the Department has set as a primary objective, the implementation of a new IT Strategy, the "DLS IT Strategy", which has been prepared for upgrading the Information Technology in the Department. With the preparation of the Strategy, the Administration of the Department has at its disposal a powerful tool to coordinate and direct its future decisions. The University of A Coruña was founded under the Galician Universities Law 11/1989 on July 20th, 1989. The Constituent Assembly passed the University Statutes on the February 4th, 1992 and these were published in the Official Bulletin (DOG) on September 17th, 1992. The University of A Coruña is territorially situated in the Campus of A Coruña and the Campus of Ferrol.
It is a public institution whose primary objective is the generation, management and dissemination of culture and scientific, technological and professional knowledge through the development of research and teaching.
The University of A Coruña conceives its essential purpose as a quality public service aimed at achieving greater levels of welfare for the group of the society through the pursuit of social, scientific and technological advances in a framework of ethical values. Part of its mission is the formation of an open, critical, democracy and solidarity citizenship, capable of analyzing reality, diagnose problems, formulate and implement solutions based in knowledge and oriented to the common good.
The University of A Coruña explicitly expresses its commitment to the study and the integral development of Galicia, its social, cultural and linguistic identity, and it will promote its full integration into the European Higher Education and and the projection in Latin America. The University of A Coruña Foundation, a private charitable and academic foundation, has been created in order to provide the University with permanent social support.

entityName: ECoE - Big Earth Data Analytics Department (BEDA Dept.)
entityDescription:
The Big Earth Data Analytics Department, tailored to exploit EO data, allows the management and presentation of vast amount of EO data and the discovery of new information that is hidden in the data and promote the value-adding combination with non-EO data streams. In the last years, different data mining technologies have been developed to cope with the different volume, variety, velocity and veracity of space-based data in order to make the EO services and applications development more efficient and to benefit from all the information hidden within the data. The need to move geospatial data analysis, and more specifically EO data processing, into the “cloud” and to store and represent data in formats (e.g., data cubes) has been recognized by many organizations worldwide. Consequently, several organizations and initiatives worldwide have already begun or are preparing for the uptake of EO data into their Big Data infrastructures. The Department will research and develop technologies related to:

- Information extraction
- Visual exploration and visualization
- Crowdsourcing and data fusion 
- Geoinformatics.
The Big Earth Data Analytics Department consists of several researchers (Postdoctoral and PhD students).

entityDescription:
Since 2001, the Scientothèque project consisted of schools and extracurricular STEM workshops for the discovery and experimentation of the main scientific disciplines, for young people aged 6 to 20 from precarious backgrounds. Our mission consists of supporting schools by co-constructing STEM projects, including digital tools and train the teachers. We also aim to encourage, through our activities, meetings between different social, generational and cultural backgrounds. This action is carried out in close collaboration with the Experimentarium, Musem of Physics of the Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB).
The Scientotheque offers an approach of STEM disciplines including Fablabs adapted to the needs of young people and supported by active learning methods. The goal is to allow them to gain the knowledge needed for school through the experimental approach and the progressive construction of knowledge. It is well established that in our current world poor social economic background populations have less access to higher education. Moreover there is a serious disaffection with interest in scientific studies particularly among the female audience. Our aim is to counteract this general tendency, by working with disadvantaged populations and especially with young girls.
At the request of the teachers, we initiated a pilot project to set up training in digital educational activities in schools (Scratch MIT, “1,2,3…. Codez!” From Main à la Pâte, Robot Thymio and Fablab). This project is aimed at students aged 6 to 18. Our field of work is part of a vast network of civil society partners, both schools, non-profit and academic organisation. We are recognized within the framework of the implementation of the Brussels Social Cohesion policy and by the National Office for Children (ONE). The Scientotheque is also one of the partners in the pilot project initiated by the Brussels Region, "Fablab Mobile Brussels", bringing together the main Fablabs in Brussels, as well as other training initiatives in new technologies and creation.

entityDescription:

It aims at valuating innovating concepts from research to industry in the RF, microwave and millimeter wave fields.

CISTEME can provide support either through outsourcing service offering or through collaborative projects. CISTEME has obtained the CRT (Center of Technology Resources) French Label in 2005 from the Ministry of Research. Since 2013, CISTEME headquarters is located at ESTER Technopole in Limoges, 12 rue Gémini, Bâtiment 2, 87068 Limoges, France. The organisation has 35 employees.

entityDescription:
TELLUX, a French start-up, is the result of 10 years of research by dynamic researchers of INSA and University of Rouen Normandy, France. The name ​TELLUX, blend of ​Tellus (Earth in Latin) and ​Lux (Light in Latin)​, is a great synopsis of the activity of our Young Innovative Company (JEI status in France), which fulfills a promise that is both ambitious and highly technical: to analyze and measure the concentration of pollutants soil by means of hyperspectral imagery, and then to provide detailed reports. 
The striking force of TELLUX is a R&D team of ​three researchers, all PhD-holders, with complementary expertise in Informatics (Machine Learning) and Chemistry (analytical chemistry), with application to spectroscopy and hyperspectral imagery:
- Antonin Van Exem ​is a geoscientist researcher, working on visible spectroscopy (VIS) since 2009. He defended his PhD thesis in 2018 on hyperspectral imagery for sedimentology.
- Paul Honeine is a Professor at University of Rouen. He has been working on Machine Learning since 2003, and on hyperspectral data since 2010. He has published about 200 research papers in Machine Learning, including 1/4 on hyperspectral imagery.
- Mélanie Mignot is an Assistant Professor at INSA Rouen Normandy. She is expert in analytical methodologies, such as microcolumn chromatography. She has been involved in several European collaborations, including Pharmaceutical Chemical Analysis Laboratory (Geneva), and Organic Chemistry Laboratory (Brussels). She was also the laureate of the European Project ChromaFish. She has published more than 25 papers in international journals and conferences, receiving two best scientific presentation awards.

The striking force of TELLUX is a R&D team of ​three researchers, all PhD-holders, with complementary expertise in Informatics (Machine Learning) and Chemistry (analytical chemistry), with application to spectroscopy and hyperspectral imagery:
- Antonin Van Exem ​is a geoscientist researcher, working on visible spectroscopy (VIS) since 2009. He defended his PhD thesis in 2018 on hyperspectral imagery for sedimentology.
- Paul Honeine is a Professor at University of Rouen. He has been working on Machine Learning since 2003, and on hyperspectral data since 2010. He has published about 200 research papers in Machine Learning, including 1/4 on hyperspectral imagery.
- Mélanie Mignot is an Assistant Professor at INSA Rouen Normandy. She is expert in analytical methodologies, such as microcolumn chromatography. She has been involved in several European collaborations, including Pharmaceutical Chemical Analysis Laboratory (Geneva), and Organic Chemistry Laboratory (Brussels). She was also the laureate of the European Project ChromaFish. She has published more than 25 papers in international journals and conferences, receiving two best scientific presentation awards.

entityDescription:
CIHEAM IAMC is the 4th constituent institute of CIHEAM, the International Centre for Advanced Mediterranean Agronomic Studies, an Intergovernmental Organisation which was founded at the joint initiative of the OECD and the Council of Europe on 21 May 1962 under an agreement signed by the governments of seven southern European countries: France, Greece, Italy, Portugal, Spain, Turkey and Yugoslavia.
The 1962 agreement establishing the Centre stipulates that CIHEAM's mission consists in "providing supplementary education (economic as well as technical) and developing a spirit of international cooperation among agricultural personnel in Mediterranean countries". According to article 15 of this agreement, every country on the Mediterranean rim is potentially eligible for membership of CIHEAM.In the mid nineteen-eighties CIHEAM therefore began to open up to countries on the southern and eastern shores of the Mediterranean Basin. This initiative resulted in the accession of several new Member States: Tunisia (1985), Egypt and Algeria (1986), Malta (1989), Morocco (1991), Albania (1992) and Lebanon (1994).
CIHEAM is made up of four Mediterranean Agronomic Institutes (MAIs), located in Bari (Italy), Chania (Greece), Montpellier (France) and Zaragoza (Spain), and a General Secretariat based in Paris.
Since 1986, and as the 4th constituent institute of CIHEAM, IAMC pursues its three main complementary missions through
- post-graduate specialised education
- networked research
- facilitation of regional debate
with focus in the fields of Business Economics and Management, Geoinformation in Environmental Management, Horticultural Genetics and Biotechnology, Food Quality and Chemistry of Natural Products, Sustainable Agriculture, and has established itself as an authority in Mediterranean agriculture, Food and Rural Development.
In particular the Department of Geoinformation in Environmental Management has been employing EO data for over 20 years, on applications as agriculture, forestry and natural vegetation monitoring. These activities are undertaken both in the framework of education, as well as research, by participating in EU-funded projects since the late 1990s.

SPECIAL SECURITY
Enigma has been providing information security services for 25 years, having knowledge that is unique on the Polish market. We also ensure that special security forms an integral part of the solutions we oﬀer. This concerns both hardware and application solutions as well as all architecture and its implementation. The systems created by Enigma are based on in–house hardware and application solutions in terms of cryptography. These solutions employ highly-developed technologies and encryption algorithms. DigiFarm has been fortunate to receive funding and support from the EIC Accelerator from June (2022) to June (2024) for developing it’s novel technology of automatically delineated field boundaries using super-high resolution SatEO data which has been commercialised successfully across multiple public organisations in Europe including Lithuanian National Paying Agency, Sweden National Paying Agency and Macedonian National Paying Agency.

Our strengths are in energy technology and international business competence and in these fields we are in close cooperation with Vaasa region´s energy sector.

entityDescription:
Technoport is a technology business incubator that was launched back in June 1998 as a department of the Public Research Centre Henri Tudor[1]. In 2012 the incubator span-out of the research centre and merged with another public initiative supporting startups as well as foreign innovative companies establishing research and development centres in Luxembourg. 
Since 2012 the new Technoport is a limited company owned by two shareholders – the Ministry of the Economy (55%) and a public bank, the SNCI (www.snci.lu) (45%). The incubator runs 5 different facilities on two geographical sites representing a combined surface of over 16.000 sqm. It has a great mix of office and industrial spaces. 
The incubator is a generic incubator open to all kind of sectors. Within the 40 companies that it hosts in average at a given moment you can find a great mix between ICT, software, space, environment, material science, IoT and/or health tech companies. This mix has proven to be a great added-value in the past to create unexpected synergies and a good exchange among entrepreneurs. 
Mission and activities
Technopot’s core activity is to support entrepreneurs in the validation, creation and development of technology companies through a flexible, but thorough, staged selection process which accepts in average between 7-10% of the overall annual deal-flow into the final official incubation program[2]. 
The incubator targets also foreign companies that decide to establish a research and development centre in Luxembourg with a flexible ramp-up support scheme by hosting them during an initial settlement period. 
On top of that the incubator has also a soft-landing support scheme for foreign startup companies that are in an internationalisation process. 
Last but not least Technoport has established a joint venture with Vodafone Procurement Company called Tomorrow Street (www.tomorrowstreet.co). It is an innovation centre that accelerates leading edge technology through scaling late stage startups. The center hosts and supports the next generation of strategic suppliers to Vodafone, and is a technology hub that attracts entrepreneurs and talent to the fast growing tech sector in Luxembourg.
Over the years the incubator has built strong networks with different types of partners (investors, corporates, mentors, coaches, research centres, regulators, …) that support its environment. 
As of 31.07.2020 the incubator has accepted a total of 157 companies throughout the years
79 left the incubator with success after an average hosting period of 3.3 years. 
Among those that left 18 got acquired by foreign companies. 
[1] Today part of the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (www.list.lu). 
[2] The selection process can be found in the download section on www.technoport.lu

entityDescription:
Cesam Seed is an IT consulting and services provider in specific field called PLM : Product Lifecycle Management

Many companies have embraced PLM as a way of using software to manage a product from the dawn to dusk of its life.
PLM systems help organizations in coping with the increasing complexity and engineering challenges of developing new products for the global competitive markets. PLM describes the engineering aspect of a product, from managing descriptions and properties of a product through its development and useful life.
Product lifecycle management can be considered one of the four cornerstones of a manufacturing corporation's information technology structure. All companies need to manage communications and information with their customers (CRM-customer relationship management), their suppliers and fulfillment (SCM-supply chain management), their resources within the enterprise (ERP-enterprise resource planning) and their product planning and development (PLM).

Within PLM there are five primary areas; 
- Systems engineering (SE) is focused on meeting all requirements, primarily meeting customer needs, and coordinating the systems design process by involving all relevant disciplines. An important aspect for life cycle management is a subset within Systems Engineering called Reliability Engineering.
- Product and portfolio m² (PPM) is focused on managing resource allocation, tracking progress, plan for new product development projects that are in process (or in a holding status). Portfolio management is a tool that assists management in tracking progress on new products and making trade-off decisions when allocating scarce resources.
- Product design (CAx) is the process of creating a new product to be sold by a business to its customers.
- Manufacturing process management (MPM) is a collection of technologies and methods used to define how products are to be manufactured.
- Product data management (PDM) is focused on capturing and maintaining information on products and/or services through their development and useful life. Change management is an important part of PDM/PLM.

entityDescription:
The professorship for Big Geospatial Data Management is part of the Department of Aerospace and Geodesy (Fakultät für Luftfahrt, Raumfahrt und Geodäsie, LRG) at the Technical University Munich.
The research of the professorship concentrates on methodology of acquisition, organization, compression, analysis, and visualization of georeferenced or geometric data in large scales. The professorship puts emphasis on methods of distributed computing, machine learning, image and text analysis, randomized data structures, high performance computing and quantum algorithms.

Dundee Satellite Station Ltd operates a ground station at Errol airbase and will be offering a range of services to the UK and International Space sector including reception and transmitting facilities in VHF, UHF, L-band, S-band, X-band and Ku-band as well as a range of consultancy services around this from RF through to data processing software, and integration to existing systems.

We can provide consultancy and support from the initial design phase looking at comms options and link budgets, through to "premium" ground station support (e.g. signal analysis and recording, orbit determination, etc) during critical phases such as LEOP or following anomalous behaviour, and on to cost-effective routine operations for data up and down links.

In addition to these spacecraft-operation support services we will be receiving Earth Observation data in real-time with a view to supporting both time-sensitive commercial applications as well as providing a broad range of archive data access for research and general public interest purposes.

entityDescription:
UniDoc S.r.l. (following UniDoc) is a spin-off from the University of Salerno formed in October 2017. Its mission is the technology transfer activities focused on engineering research results in well-identified market sectors (such as digitization of public administration (PA) particularly in the healthcare sector). After the establishment, it was registered as an innovative start-up. It was naturally a candidate as a technology enabler for PA's innovation processes.
Capitalizing on skills and experiences of the founders, today it offers to the market, in partnership with large companies, technological solutions to promote the digitization process of the PA making it more effective. In particular, in partnership with the CSA consortium, it has been able to manage a huge amount of information obtained from the digitization of millions of hospital medical records. The enhancement of this heritage, in all the clinical/administrative processes of hospital companies, has focused almost 80% of the resources and activities of the spin-off. The huge amount (dozens of TB) and the specificity of the data processed in addition to their intrinsic value required conscious use of the technologies. 
With a set of Big Data tools specifically designed to deal with large amounts of data, unexpected knowledge was extracted, studying phenomena still unknown (of particular interest to pharmaceutical companies). 
In this extremely sensitive area, such as medical records, UniDoc has developed a flexible and reliable infrastructure to afford the topic of Big Data Analytics. All the analysis procedures are fed by well-known and (and therefore still widely used) data sources such as paper-based medical records after a robust process to appropriately digitize, normalize and qualify the output.
The market proposal includes a distributed computing solution designed specifically to process and analyze large amounts of data (of the order of petabytes) efficiently and perfectly scalable.
The solution comes directly from the world of scientific research and was initially engineered for genome analysis. In this area, the amount of data produced by modern sequencers (NGS) has required solutions that can compare and extract information from data strings in a reasonable time, out of the scope of a single computer. The solution was developed within the Department of Computer Science at the University of Salerno (from 2018 Department of Excellence) using distributed computing platforms (Apache Spark over Hadoop Cluster) appropriately declined for bioinformatics and genomic data analysis. The results have been published in prestigious international scientific journals. 
In term of interoperability of its solutions, UniDoc participated in the last two IHE-Europe Connectathons (In April 2018 it was held at the Fokker Terminal in The Hague (NH), and in April 2019 it was held in Rennes (FR)). The UniDoc technicians brought to both the conferences the core of the infrastructure, namely the clinical data repository. All the software modules passed the compatibility checklist and the interoperability of their interfaces has been proved. The repository has been designed to be compliant with the XDS/b (Cross Enterprise Document Sharing) profiles defined by IHE.

entityDescription:
New monitoring technologies are being progressively implemented in coastal ocean observatories. These new observing systems, such as IMOS, OOI, IOOS, VENUS, POSEIDON, COSYNA among others, are delivering new insight into coastal ocean variability, that triggers new theoretical and technological developments, increasing our understanding of open ocean, coastal and nearshore processes and contributing to a more science based and sustainable management of the oceans and coastal areas.
SOCIB is one of such systems, a Coastal Ocean Observing and Forecasting System located in the Balearic Islands, a new facility of facilities open to international access. SOCIB responds to a change of paradigm in the observation of our oceans and coasts, an observation that has evolved from being centered on a unique platform, the oceanographic ships with data availability being delayed in time, to an observation now based on multi-platform and integrated systems (using buoys, satellites, ships, autonomous underwater vehicles, HF radar, ARGO profilers, etc.), also assuring quasi real time quality controlled data availability for both researchers and society. This change of paradigm is very significant and allows being able to respond to the three key drivers identified by SOCIB back in 2009: (1) science priorities, (2) technology development, (3) response capacity to society needs.
SOCIB is a multi-platform distributed and integrated system that provides streams of oceanographic data and modelling services to support operational oceanography in a European and international framework, therefore also contributing to the needs of marine and coastal research in a global change context. In line with EuroGOOS, operational oceanography is here understood in a wide sense, including both the systematic long-term measurements of the seas and their interpretation and dissemination, and also the sustained supply of multidisciplinary data to cover the needs of a wide range of scientific research and societal priorities. This allows a quantitative increase in our understanding of key questions on oceans and climate change, coastal ocean processes, ecosystem variability, sea level rise, etc. and also drives us towards a more science based coastal and ocean management. It is important to note that in its present format and financial status, SOCIB isl not be carrying out direct research activities (except in specific areas directly related to SOCIB objectives) but provides support for them. The research activities are being carried out by IMEDEA, COB/IEO and UIB, among other organisations, in close coordination to SOCIB.

entityDescription:
The Department of Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and Informatics offers three (3) Programs of Studies (PoS) at undergraduate level (Bachelor of Science), in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and Computer Science. At postgraduate level the Department offers two (2) PoS at Master level (Master of Science), in Electrical Engineering and Web and Smart Systems and one (1) PoS at PhD level (Doctor of Philosophy) in all Departmental disciplines. The POS offered at undergraduate and postgraduate level are conventional in terms of the mode of delivery and type, however due to the recent outbreak of COVID-19 can also be delivered in distance or blended learning mode, depending on the epi
The Department strongly and actively supports the advancement of research and the generation of new knowledge through fostering exploration, innovation and novel application of knowledge at all levels and areas of the Department’s disciplines. The academic staff of the Department and research students are engaged in research funded projects through a number of research groups and laboratories. The main research areas explored by the Department are: Antenas and Microvaves, High Resolution Ionospheric measurements, Computer networks and Communication systems, Web and Mobile Systems, Artificial Intelligence, High Performance Computational Analysis of Engineering Systems, Medical Image Analysis and Recording, e-health systems and Services, Robotics and Automated Systems, Computational Intelligence, High Performance Computing and Embedded Smart Systems. The Department aims to provide excellent teaching and to create the environment for effective learning, both at undergraduate and postgraduate level, while improving the Country's competitive advantage through cutting edge engineering research activities as these apply to various economic sectors. Over the years the Department has built its research reputation at National, European and International levels and has created strong industrial links. Research activities can be identified along a wide range of fields, such as: engineering design, production planning and control, total quality management, supply chain management, PLC and microprocessors usage for automatic control, composite materials and their usage in engineering designs, micro and nanotechnology, mechatronics, energy management systems, rational usage of energy/renewable energy sources, buildings bioclimatic design, vehicle active and passive safety systems, vehicle electronic stability systems, environmental noise and transport 'smart' management systems.
The programmes of study are structured according to the scientific and professional needs of modern mechanical and automotive engineers. Our students systematically cultivate analytical and critical way of thinking, in order to be able to cope with diverse engineering problems. In addition, they are exposed to state of the art software and engineering practices. As a result, our graduates are able to continuously upgrade and cope with a constantly changing technological landscape. The Department currently offers two degrees at Bachelors' level, one in Mechanical Engineering and the other in Automotive Engineering. In addition to the general Mechanical Engineering direction, the Department offers the option to Mechanical Engineering students to specialize in the area of Oil and Gas.The Department offers at Master level the course in Manufacturing and Welding Engineering Design.

entityDescription:
Created in 2002, by the Autonomous Region of Aosta Valley, Fondazione Montagna sicura (Safe Mountain Foundation) is a non-profit foundation with its headquarter located in Courmayeur (AO), at the foot of the Mont-Blanc massif. Fondazione Montagna sicura is a centre for applied research, training and documentation focused on innovative applications of new technologies to mountain territories. The Foundation is active on several projects, pursuing various objectives, such as the promotion of mountain safety through research and dissemination activities, the analysis of hydro-geological risks, the promotion of sustainable development through pilot tests and best practices, and the study of climate change impacts on high-altitude environments and the cryosphere. Core activity of Fondazione Montagna sicura is the glacier-related risk-monitoring plan. Based on an annually updated GIS database of Aosta Valley’s glaciers, derived from historical data and several years of field research and observations, this monitoring plan aim to identify and investigate existing or potentially new risk situations across the territories of the Autonomous Region of Aosta Valley. The research and monitoring activities conducted on the dynamics of Planpincieux Glacier (Courmayeur - AO), as well as the
risk management actions undertaken for the potential GLOF (Glacial Lake Outburst Flood) of the Gran Croux Glacier (Cogne - AO), and the monitoring of rockfall-induced risk of the Brenva basin (Courmayeur - AO) are only the latest of several activities operated thanks to this plan. This knowledge become therefore a key tool for the numerous cross-border cooperation projects that, since its establishment, the Foundation has been committed to develop, together with universities (University of Turin, Polytechnic of Turin, University of Genova, .), research centers (WLS, ARPA, CREALP, CNR IRPI, EURAC, BFW, Geoformer, ETH Zurich, Geopraevent, IGE Grenoble etc.), and public administrations, aiming for a broad sharing of experiences and effective impacts on the territories affected by these issues.
