entityName: Botanical Environmental and Conservation Consultants Ltd
entityDescription:
Botanical, Environmental and Conservation (BEC) Consultants Ltd (www.botanicalenvironmental.com) is a group of professional and highly experienced ecologists. Since its establishment in 2000, this ecological consultancy has provided high quality specialist advice to a wide range of clients including the National Parks & Wildlife Service, Environmental Protection Agency, Local Authorities, European Commission DG Environment, Waterways Ireland, Coillte and the National Biodiversity Data Centre. Working from offices in Dublin, BEC Consultants is involved in projects throughout Ireland and at European Union level. The company has built strong links with government departments, state bodies, local authorities, university faculties, NGOs, local community groups (e.g. TidyTowns) and consulting engineering firms, and strives to work in tandem with these institutions to provide an excellent service.

BEC Consultants offers a wide range of expertise in terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecology. We specialise in ecological research projects such as the National Survey of Upland Habitats and the Irish Semi-natural Grasslands Survey. We also conduct Appropriate Assessments, Ecological Impact Assessments, habitat mapping, management plan preparation, specialist botanical surveys and practical conservation work, such as rare plant translocation. Much of the work the company has undertaken over the last two decades has been in the assessment and monitoring of EU Habitats Directive Annex I habitats.

All BEC Consultants staff are highly trained ecologists with a wealth of experience and, in many instances, a significant reputation in ecology, botany and conservation management. The senior staff are full members of the Chartered Institute of Ecology and Environmental Management(CIEEM), which requires adherence to a code of professional conduct.

Hyperborea Srl, founded in 1995, is a SME based in the Scientific and Technological Pole of Navacchio - Pisa (Italy). Hyperborea currently employs 25 staff members plus a team of 15 experts in Cultural Heritage and Digital Humanities with a long history of co-operation with Research centres and Academic institutions (including, among others, the Italian National Research Council, Scuola Normale Superiore and the Sant'Anna School for Advanced Studies in Pisa, along with European well renowned research institutions).
Our main product is Arianna 4 which is an outstanding tool for managing archives. It is also accompanied by Arianna web which is the software that allows to publish the archives already managed with Arianna 4.
Current customers include large enterprises, insurances, etc. for the private sector, and Ministries, State Archives, Universities, Regional governments and related Agencies, and local administrations, for the public sector. Furthermore Arianna 4 and Arianna web customers are Diocesan archives.
Hyperborea has achieved a pre-competitive technological maturity over recent years, focusing primarily on developing innovative solutions in collaboration with international and national partners, and within research projects. Such numerous cutting-edge techniques and methodologies gives Hyperborea the necessary scaffolding to collaborate with many national institutions (such as Municipalities, Provincial and Regional Authorities, Fine Arts Government Offices, and National Archives, Libraries and Museums), with large companies, SMEs and research organisations. Historical Archives were largely the mostly developed application field in the company, which developed solutions for digitalisation, indexing, categorisation and cataloguing documentary sources along with search tools, on-line access to high resolution images, services to support case studies and IT related consulting services. In the last ten years, the company has been specialising in research and development of innovative semantic based solutions and products for its cultural heritage customers as the Italian Ministry of Culture, Museums, Libraries, State and Diocesan Archives. For these reason Hyperborea is now involved in semantic enabled systems with the aim of supporting the work of specialists from the humanistic and with the broader vision of establishing a semantic integration platform for any kind of cultural sources.
Our R&D department is currently engaged in exploiting the International Image Interoperability Framework (IIIF -https://iiif.io/) open standards for enhancing its software solution, and in completing the process to become a member of this community. Furthermore, we strongly contributed to the new national standard for the archival sector: the UNI VADO standard (https://tinyurl.com/uni-vado). The specific title is: UNI 11769: 2020 Applications for cultural heritage (ABC) - Elements for the evaluation of applications for the description and ordering of archives (VADO).
Hyperborea is also President of the ICT department of Regional and National Italian confederation of crafts and SMEs and member of the District of Technologies for Cultural Heritage and Sustainable Cities to strengthen research activities between Centres of Scientific Excellence and the Industrial sector.

entityDescription:
Established in 1960, the Faculty of Organization and Informatics is an institution that reaches back more than half a century, which is a comparably long tradition when modern technologies studies are concerned.
Over the decades, the Faculty has beenproviding education to future experts in the field of information sciences and technologies, economics, organization, communication and other related fields.
All thenecessary infrastructure for educational and research purposesis provided within ourtwo buildings (FOI I and FOI II)including:well-equipped computer rooms, videoconferencing facilities, e-learning system, wireless Internet access throughout the premises as well as a modern library and the reading room.
Both FOI buildings are located in the vicinity of the town centre, the Student Dormitory Varaždin and the newly built Student restaurant.

- Competent staff being the leaders in their research and professional fields in Croatia with national and international recognition.

- Fast employment after the graduation, as well as the possibility of continuous further education.

- Regard for the students and their standard.

entityDescription:
ESTABLISHMENT

The second primary school was established by the Decree of the Ministry of Education on November 6, 1948 with the name II. Seven-year school in Varaždin. The school started operating on August 28, 1948, when the first session of the teachers' association was held, and classes began on September 6, 1948 with 7 lower and 7 higher classes.

POSITION

For the first 10 years, the school operated in several different locations, including in the first cathedral (opposite the FOI), and on September 15, 1958. classes began to be held in the building in Cesarčeva Street, where they are still held today. Until the school year 1983/1984. the building in Cesarčeva Street is divided by the 2nd and 4th primary schools, after which only the 2nd primary school is in the building. The building was built in 1932 and housed a Franciscan grammar school and barracks before school.

SCHOOL NAME

The school started operating as II. seven-year school Varaždin. From 1953 to 1990, the school operated under the name Osnovna škola "Ratimir Herceg", and from 1990 the school was named II. elementary school Varaždin.

OBSERVATORY

Thanks to a donation from one family, Second Elementary School has a modern, computerized telescope for its renovated observatory. In addition to being used for teaching astronomy, the observatory of Varaždin's Second Primary School is open for school excursions, but also for citizens through lectures and observations of celestial bodies.

entityDescription:
Aero Enterprise is specialized in the sustainable inspection and analysis of surfaces on primarily vertical (industrial) objects of all kinds. A big focus is set on (offshore)wind power plants.
The quality assurance system consists of flight robots, mobile ground stations, client-based analysis software and a database. In parallel to the high-resolution digital images, infrared data are also recorded, which can give an insight into the deeper layers of an object. The obtained information is GNSS- and object-referenced and is imaged for the customer in an analysis software in a virtual 3D environment.
Numerous tools allow the information to be qualified and classified, supported by AI. The digital recording of the actual states of the objects allows for the first time an "objectification", which is often subjectively judged by human beings, and absolute information of old and new data can be used as part of a change management.
The software and database form the ideal basis for the connection to industry 4.0 and integration of the data into an existing ERP environment of our customers.
We also provide a partner-program (SaaS), where experts and specialists in the wind energy business can use their own drones for data acquisition in combination with our Software package to do the analysis of the data. Finally with one-click a partner-branded report is generated to get situational awareness of their assets.
NOTE:
Since July 2020 AE is also part of Buss Energy Group ( www.buss-group.com ) and WINDEA ( www.windea.de ). In this embedded international consortium we are able to provide a large variety of extra services starting from the planning, projecting, installing ( with harbour- and ship management) inspection and quality control, maintenance & repair till to the end-of live phase with decommissioning of offshore plants.

entityName: University of Zagreb Faculty of Geodesy - Chair of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
entityDescription:
The employees of the Chair of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing actively participate in teaching on all study programs at the Faculty of Geodesy, University of Zagreb (undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate specialist and postgraduate doctoral studies) and in the lifelong education program of the Faculty of Geodesy. The employees of the Chair teach classes in the fields of photogrammetry, remote sensing, and geoinformation systems (GIS). Teaching processes include the usage of the commercial and open-source software for digital image processing in the fields of photogrammetry and remote sensing. A large amount of recorded material and field data collected in the framework of scientific and professional projects carried out at the Chair are available to students for the preparation of a large number of a diploma thesis in the fields of photogrammetry, remote sensing, and GIS. Many scientific types of research in the field of remote sensing, photogrammetry, and GIS are performed at the Chair, such as:
· developing automatic methods for processing and analyzing satellite and aerial imagery
· development of multisensor systems for close-range and aerial imaging
· development of unmanned aerial vehicles based on open source technologies
· developing new methods for spatial multicriteria analysis for environmental change monitoring
· application of new technologies in the preservation of cultural heritage and 3D modeling
· developing methods for collecting large amounts of spatial data based on active (e.g., laser scanner, radar) and passive sensors (e.g., camera)
· development of new methods for spatial and radiometric camera calibration
· developing methods for processing and analyzing data collected using multispectral, hyperspectral and thermal cameras
· application of terrestrial and aerial laser scanners for spatial data acquisition
· developing methods for processing large amounts of 3D data
· development of algorithms and software solutions in the service of photogrammetry, remote sensing, and GIS
· development of desktop and web GIS solutions for the purpose of performing analyzes and visualization of environmental changes
· developing and expanding the applicability of photogrammetry, remote sensing and GIS to related technical, as well as biotechnical, natural, social, humanistic and interdisciplinary scientific fields.
Scientific research and development of methods, algorithms and software solutions at the Chair is based on the available open-source programs, function libraries and programming languages such as Python, R, etc.

entityDescription:
Neutelings Riedijk Architects is a leading international architectural practice based in Rotterdam, The Netherlands. We offer a strong commitment to design excellence: realizing high quality architecture through the development of powerful and innovative concepts into clear built form.
PUBLIC BUILDINGS & MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENTS
Neutelings Riedijk Architects is specialized in the design of complex projects for public, commercial and cultural buildings. We have designed and built theatres, city halls, museums, libraries, hotels, schools, office buildings and mixed-use developments. We have wide experience in balancing the complex functions and logistics of these projects with their often delicate and urban contexts to give them the iconic significance in the public realm that their clients desire.
ORNAMENT & IDENTITY
In our belief, contemporary ornamentation results in buildings with a powerful expression that create new local identities in a globalized world. In 2018 we published the book ‘Ornament & Identity’, a multi-layered essay that presents the results of our search for expression and identity through a selection of thirty-six of our projects.
TEAM
Neutelings Riedijk Architects was founded in 1987 by Willem Jan Neutelings and Michiel Riedijk. Since 2020 the office is led by principal architect Michiel Riedijk and managing director Carl Meeusen.
We have an international team of talented, highly educated and motivated architects. For our international projects the work force at our office in Rotterdam is complemented by technical expertise through our association with local partners specializing in architectural engineering, cost calculation and site supervision. This arrangement allows us to put together a team of specialists to meet the specific requirements of each project.

entityDescription:
Innovation Centre Nikola Tesla (ICENT) is a non-profit institution whose function is to enable and accelerate efficient commercialization of new technologies in areas critical for the development of Croatian economy. It aims to become the leading Croatian research and development centre in fields of engineering, particularly of electronics, design, computer engineering, and information and communication technology and related applications that drives the Croatian economy towards competitiveness and sustainability. The strengths and capabilities of ICENT are built trough creation of: path for the scientific community to commercialize results of research, growth in interdisciplinary activities within the community, workspace and infrastructure for proof-of-concept and prototypes development, support to start-up companies to commercialize innovations developed, growth of intellectual property, growth of high-added value businesses and jobs, support of technological competitiveness, adding value to the European technological development thrust. 
ICENT is the host of Croatian Robotics Digital Innovation Hub (CROBOHUB), the key Croatian non-profit facility to support companies to become more competitive by improving their business/production processes as well as products and services by up-taking digital technologies and robotic solutions http://www.icent.hr/en/crobohub/.
CROBOHUB DIH acts as one-stop-shop, helping Croatian companies to digitalise their business through efficient orchestrating of various stakeholders in innovation ecosystem such as research institutions, business support institutions and businesses that may contribute to the development and application of advanced robotic systems in manufacturing. CROBOHUB also provides connections with investors, facilitates access to financing for digital transformations, help connect users and suppliers of robotic innovations across the value chain and foster synergies between digital and other key enabling technologies (such as biotech, advanced materials, etc.).
Through its project activities CROBOHUB became a part of network of DIHs and CCs developed by HORSE, L4MS, DIH2 and AI DIH NETWORK projects. It is also part of the EC S3 online catalogue of digital innovation hubs that contains comprehensive information on digital innovation hubs in Europe http://s3platform.jrc.ec.europa.eu/digital-innovation-hubs-tool/-/dih/1474/view.

Axon Vibe’s customer-centric Smart Mobility Platform/App understands and predicts real-world door-to-door customer behaviour by leveraging 24/7 smartphone location/motion data in a non-intrusive and GDPR-compliant way.
We help public transport operators and authorities to:
1. deliver proactive real-time travel assistance across all modes (e.g. handling disruptions, service changes, social distancing) to re-build confidence in public transport in the "new normal",
2. connect their customers real-world experiences with shared mobility services and commercial eco-systems around them to generate ancillary revenue through delightful contextual marketing campaigns, and
3. gather door-to-door, multi-modal customer behaviour insights and identify real-world usage/demand of their transportation infrastructure (rail and road) to optimise existing or launch new (first/last mile) services.
By predicting customers’ upcoming journeys based on their travel patterns, we anticipate upcoming pain points of individual customers in advance (e.g. disruptions, crowded vehicles/stations) and propose alternative services including active travel, shared mobility and mass public transport in the right context.
By delivering a smart, integrated and seamless navigation system we make the use of public transport and shared mobility as convenient as using a private car.

entityName: Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology Osijek
entityDescription:
The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology Osijek is a modern faculty that has constantly been developing in all areas of its expertise. The educational process consists of three levels with study programmes being continually upgraded and harmonised with recent scientific discoveries, economy and labour market needs. The Faculty’s research groups have participated in numerous domestic and European projects as either heads or associates.Cooperation with the economy, encouragement of entrepreneurship and transfer of knowledge and technologies are fundamental indicators of the Faculty’s development.The Faculty successfully cooperates with the most important electrical engineering and ICT companies. Furthermore, in collaboration with the economy, professional and development projects, studies and elaborations are carried out. During their studies, our students are introduced to the world of work, and are involved in solving real engineering problems through traineeships, work on their final papers and graduation theses.
The Faculty is the regional leader in the field of electrical engineering, computer science and information and communications technologies, and is strategically aimed at advancing its visibility and competitiveness in science and research, professional projects, students' education, close cooperation with the economy and local community. 
Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology Osijek (FERIT) is one of the three technical faculties of the University of Osijek. The Faculty has six departments with 56 PhD scientists and of around 2000 students. There are over 20 laboratories, among which the Laboratory for Renewable Energy Sources as well as two accredited the Electromagnetic Compatibility Laboratores and the Laboratory for High Frequency Measurements stand out. FERIT successfully participated in the implementation of several Croatian and European scientific and educational projects and has a long experience in providing education in the field of Telecommunications at undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate level. FERIT enables and continuously improves collaboration with the industry on common projects, workshops, student internships etc. FERIT provides a web platform called STUP offering students and associated companies’ direct contact related to student internships, trainings, workshops and job offers. The main areas of expertise are: renewable energy sources and energy efficiency, mathematical modelling and optimisation in power and electromechanical engineering, intelligent energy networks, image and video processing, intelligent control systems and robotics, wireless communication systems, communications networks and next-generation network services, applications and software quality, applied computational intelligence, embedded as well as distributed and ubiquitous computer systems.
FERIT has participated as either the lead beneficiary or partner in more than 50 national and international projects from 2008 until now. 
The scientists employed at the Faculty of Electrical Engineering Osijek participated in 38 scientific-research and technology projects financed by the Croatian Science Foundation, Interreg IPA Cross-Border Cooperation Programme Croatia-Serbia 2014-2020, Interreg V-A Hungary-Croatia Co-Operation Programme 2014-2020, European Regional Development Fund, Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek and projects in cooperation with the local community, financed by the European Social Fund.

The Department of Economics and Managementof theUniversity of Pisais a lively environment where research and teaching live side by side in the areas of economics, business and management studies, mathematics and statistics. It’s one of the biggest departments of the University of Pisa, including more than 70 professors and researchers, and more than 4,000 students both at the under and post graduate level, coming from every region of Italy as well as other European countries and the rest of the world.

In coming years, we aim to expand the opportunities for studying business, strategy, and marketing in English. This has a double aim: intensify the presence of foreign students in our Department and stimulate our students to live and work in an international context.

entityDescription:
Asynos GmbH provides end-to-end digital supply chain track-and-trace solution, enabling reduction in food fraud and wastage. We are transforming the food supply chain by digitalizing packages at the individual level with ultra-low-cost RFID/NFC-enabled tracking and freshness sensors, integrated with a SaaS/private cloud data platform.
Our solution:

- Increases supply chain transparency by providing traceability to the individual, serialized package and its production meta-information that can be shared with every value-chain participant and be easily read out via a NFC reader, and by providing transparent evidence of their quality standards through a technology-layer

- Monitors and improves food logistics through automated proof of origin; time-temperature compliance; an easy tracking/proofing system at the unit level

- Enables detection of counterfeit food products and beverages by destruction-free verification of contents in a box and providing transparency of quality checks from manufacturer onwards through the entire value chain

- Improves consumer confidence and experience by providing transparency about the origin and authenticity of the products; and notifications about expiration of food through a smart phone or smart fridge

- Supports food safety by testing realtime freshness of food using liquid and gas sensors that sense various attributes of the packaged food such as humidity, pH levels, and temperature

Company description: Asynos GmbH provides end-to-end digital supply chain track-and-trace solution, enabling reduction in food fraud and wastage. - Improves consumer confidence and experience by providing transparency about the origin and authenticity of the products; and notifications about expiration of food through a smart phone or smart fridge

- Supports food safety by testing realtime freshness of food using liquid and gas sensors that sense various attributes of the packaged food such as humidity, pH levels, and temperature

entityDescription:
Campera Electronic Systems is an innovative Italian small/medium enterprise (SME) founded to respond to the needs of the electronics market for high-performance, high-quality field-programmable gate array (FPGA) systems and custom designed intellectual property (IP). The company was founded in 2014 by Andrea Campera and Gabrielle Dalle Mura, two electronics engineers with extensive experience in FPGA systems development. The idea was to build a company with a robust workflow to provide custom designed IPs and FPGA design services as fast as possible and to the highest standards, all while offering excellent customer service.

Although relatively young, the company has been constantly growing and is now well established in the FPGA market. Its major client share comes from the military and radar market, who benefit from the company’s expertise in video and radar processing applications. Campera Electronic Systems also has strong collaborations with major research and academic institutes in Italy (University of Pisa, the National Institute of Nuclear Physics (INAF), National Institute of Astrophysics (INFN) and others),and continues to expand its collaboration network through a variety of research projects and applications.

Company Core Activity: High-performance FPGA design services, FPGA IP core design, embedded systems hardware prototyping.

Products: The company offers a set of IP core libraries architected, developed, verified, released and maintained through a rigorous and efficient process. The IPs are vendor-independent, ‘off the shelf’ VHDL cores for FPGAs (Xilinx, Altera, Lattice and Microsemi), optimized in terms of speed, power and resource usage. There is an advanced proprietary library for Video Processing, DSP, IO and HW. These libraries are the foundation of our future products.

Research and Innovation: CAMPERA-ES founders and employees have extensive research experience, also demonstrated by their publication record (see publication list). CAMPERA-ES has also strong collaborations with major research and academic institutes in Italy (University of Pisa, University of Rome, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki – Greece, the National Institute of Nuclear Physics (INAF), National Institute of Astrophysics (INFN) and others) and Europe. We continue to expand our collaboration network through a variety of research projects and applications, on a regional, national and European level. The company is a member of HiPEAC (https://www.hipeac.net/), the European Network on High Performance and Embedded Architecture and Compilation. By participating in this network, we gain access to a large collaboration in new research projects, we gain access to highly qualified researchers, get access to the latest research developments and influence the direction of computing systems research.

Games are a way to test out different scenarios, create new knowhow, as well as introduce people to new subjects and environments. A game takes a phenomenon and models it into a system that is easy to understand. In game design, we create a controllable environment that demonstrates cause and effect easily. entityDescription:
Nommon provides information, quantitative analysis and decision support tools for organisational intelligence and policy assessment. Our goal is to assist private and public organisations in creating sustainable value, by helping them make better-informed decisions in complex and uncertain environments.

We apply the state of the art in data science and systems modelling and simulation to integrate analytical and simulation models with supporting databases, offering our customers virtual laboratories to assess the impact of a set of potential strategies under different scenarios.

We work in sectors dealing with systems whose performance emerges from the complex interaction of interdependent policies and regulatory regimes, infrastructures, technologies, and demographic, socioeconomic and behavioural trends.

Nommon’s commercial operations are organised into four business units:
- Nommon Mobility Analytics, which analyses anonymised geolocation data from mobile devices (e.g., mobile phone records) and blends them with more traditional data (e.g., census data, traffic counts) to provide dynamic population mapping, trip matrices and other activity and mobility indicators. 

- Transport and Mobility, which provides decision support tools and consultancy services for data-driven transport modelling, with particular focus on the use of non-conventional data sources and on new, emerging mobility concepts and technologies, such as MaaS and CAVs. 

- Aviation, which provides products and services for the planning and management of airports, airlines and air traffic management systems. 

- Analytics Accelerator, which conceives and develops innovative projects and pilot studies in other areas, including Smart Cities and Urban Planning, Retail and Geomarketing, Logistics and Supply Chain, and Energy and Environment.

entityName: FAKULTET POLITICKIH ZNANOSTI SVEUCILISTE U ZAGREBU
entityDescription:
Faculty of Political Science of Zagreb University is the oldest political science educational and research institution in this part of Europe and the only programme of political science in The Republic of Croatia.
Generations of political science and journalism graduates have earned their BA, MA. and PhD degrees at the Faculty of Political Science, among them current academic and high school lecturers, scholars, government ministers and members of parliament, mayors, diplomats, journalists, publishers, media analysts and PR experts.
Since academic year 2005/2006 political science and journalism programs have been reorganized according to Bologna model into undergraduate and graduate programs. The Faculty also offers 11 postgraduate specialist MA programs. Faculty also has an integral doctoral program in political science.
In 1996 the Faculty founded its own radio station, Radio Student, adding to the quality of its journalism program through interlinking of academic and practical skills and encouraging student creativity. In 2012 it was joined by Student Television, and both media are autonomously run by students, under the guidance of faculty members and associated experts. In 2014 the Faculty launched student newspapers Global.
In 2019, The Faculty media outlets produced and broadcasted a specialized media promotion programme about the Croatian path towards full membership in ESA and the forthcoming opportunities for Croatian private and public R&D sector entities within EU space programmes.

entityDescription:
Solar System Resources Corporation Sp. z o. o. is a company developing technologies for the needs of space mining and recognition of space resources. The company also develops other technologies and services related to the broadly understood space industry, high-tech. The company's offer also includes testing and hardening electronics using a proton beam for the construction of devices operating in deep space.
The company is also a lobbyist registered in Poland and at the European Parliament. Protected legal interest: space mining, space technologies, research and development, commercialization and technology transfer, transatlantic cooperation.
The company is lobbying for stronger transatlantic cooperation, cooperation between the European Union and the US, NASA and the accession of EU countries to the Artemis and Artemis Accord program. The company aims to ensure US supremacy in space with a strong participation of Poland and the countries of the European Union, Ukraine, and perhaps in the near future also Russia.
The company is lobbying for a stronger focus of ESA and European Union programs on the acquisition and use of space resources, as well as fairer access to lucrative space contracts by other companies across the European Union and making the European space market more diverse. The company is also lobbying for an increase in ESA's budget.

entityName: OIKON SI, Institute for Sustainable Development Ltd.
entityDescription:
OIKON SI, Institute for Sustainable Development Ltd. was established at the end of 2020. It is a natural result of the excellent cooperation we had in the past with colleagues from the business and financial consulting field and the environmental field, thus creating a joint venture company in the ownership of two renowned firms in their expert fields.Market demand in environmental services requires increasing complementarity in competencies as well as experience from very different sectors. Today’s requirements at the EU, national and local levels, in terms of development plans, are growing in their complexity, requiring a strategic approach beyond individual and partial intervention. OIKON SI, in cooperation with the parent companies CEDARS (www.cedars.si) and OIKON from Croatia (www.oikon.hr), provides specialized services in the field of sustainable development planning, economic and socio-economic professional fields, various evaluations, etc. It also organizes, implements and facilitates the provision of existing services in Slovenia that OIKON already provides in Croatia. In this way, both companies utilize synergies, both in their domestic markets and in third country markets, by positioning their services under one company. OIKON SI works on finding answers from its professional fields that would support the successful implementation of the European Green Deal, the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility. 
OIKON SI’s portfolio:
Environmental Policy: Development of Strategic Plans, Policies, Program Development
Studies and Assessments: Environment and Nature Impact Assessment, Environmental and Nature Protection Reports, Feasibility, Renewable Energy, Mobility, Transport and Industrial Ecology Analyses, Program/Project Evaluations
Remote Sensing and IT/GIS: Earth Observation and Terrestrial/Aerial Remote Sensing data Collection, Processing and Analysis, Geo-statistics, Spatio-Temporal Modelling, Geospatial data Modelling and Analysis, GIS
Monitoring: Environmental and Nature Monitoring, Natural Resource Management, Design and Environmental Monitoring for Construction Projects, Agricultural Monitoring
Training: Environmental Protection, GIS, Curriculum Development and Training
Landscape Architecture: Landscape Studies, Landscape Assessments
Research: Ecosystem Research, Environmental Studies, Nature Protection

entityDescription:
Solargis develops and operates high-resolution and reliable global databases of solar resource and energy-related weather parameters, as well as solar energy evaluation software and map products. The company builds on experience in solar energy and photovoltaics for 21 years. Solargis operates online services, integrated within Solargis web-based platform (https://apps.solargis.com), which provide access to geospatial data, maps and software for planning, financing, performance evaluation, forecasting and for management of distributed solar power generation. We support the solar energy industry with technical consultancy aimed at optimising the development and operation of solar power plants. Serving the reliable global meteorological data and energy evaluation and forecasting software, we maximise the value of solar power and enable its better integration with electricity grids.

Solar resource data is calculated using in-house developed and validated models, making use of five geostationary meteorological satellites, operated by EUMETSAT, NOAA and JMA. We use also other satellite data (MODIS and sentinels) for evaluation of surface characteristics and for evaluation of sites where development of solar power plants takes place. Besides satellite data we use inputs from various reanalysis and forecasting global meteorological models operated by ECMWF, DWD and NOAA.

entityDescription:
We are world experts in environmental data analysis and interpretation. Our talented team of consultants use their knowledge and experience of sourcing, analysing and interpreting complex environmental data to create bespoke data analysis systems. We provide solutions for governments, local authorities, international organisations and property developers.

Aether was founded in 2008 by senior members of the UK’s national emission inventory team. The initial team of four has now grown to more than 20, based in Oxford.
By transforming complex emissions data into robust emissions inventories we can deliver demonstrable environmental intelligence that can be used to inform policy decisions. Policy makers are then able to make informed, evidence based, environmental and economic decisions towards helping to reach emission reduction targets.
Alongside our core business, our team can also provide guidance on how to establish a framework and the tools needed to calculate emissions inventories for future years.
Aether is at the forefront of international, national and local greenhouse gas (GHG) and air quality emissions calculation and review and we are respected internationally for our niche expertise in this area. We have significant experience in providing GHG emission modelling, the development of scenarios based on national statistics, local growth projections and specific local policies and measures.
We have key sector-specific experts (energy, industry, waste and agriculture/land use) who are internationally accredited in the collection, compilation, analysis and reporting/presentation of GHG emissions. Our core skills are in compiling, manipulating and presenting environmental data and we are experts with databases, spreadsheets, infographics and GIS.

entityName: COSTRUZIONI APPARECCHIATURE ELETTRONICHE NUCLEARI C.A.E.N. SpA
entityDescription:
CAEN is one of the most important spin-offs of the Italian Nuclear Physics Research Institute, founded in Viareggio in 1979. CAEN designs and manufactures sophisticated electronic equipment for nuclear physics research and is today among the world’s leading companies in the field: there are several hundreds of thousand CAEN Low/High Voltage and data acquisition channels now working in all the most important Nuclear Physics Laboratories over the World. In the last years CAEN diversified its offer, extending its market, taking part into national and international programs and becoming a real “Innovation Company”. In this way CAEN joined to its core business new experiences in new fields such as the UHF RFID, the microelectronics, the aerospace applications, biomedicine, and homeland security.
CAEN is known today as the only company in the world able to offer, besides a complete range of power supply and data acquisition systems, a large choice of Front-End modules implemented using ASIC (Application Specific Integrated Circuit) developed inside the company itself. CAEN portfolio includes today more than 250 products, ranging from power supply systems to data acquisition boards and crates. Besides catalogue products CAEN offers custom solutions dedicated to the different customers’ needs.
The quality of its products is monitored during all the production cycle and guaranteed by the UNI-EN-ISO 9001:2000 certification. 
In 2016 CAEN founded the division CAEN SyS (System and Spectroscopy) to take on the challenge to develop innovative products for nuclear safety and security, as well as other innovative projects concerning homeland security.

entityDescription:
Berring Data Collective is leading the global community of collaborative ocean data collection with fishers. Fishing provides an ideal ride for compact sensors, such as this one. As the net fishes it is catching data along with fish. 
Integration is more cost effective than manual or even automated in-situ ocean observation. But so what? this is only going to work where fishing takes place.
Well, therein lies the beauty of fishing for data. Fishing occurs exactly where data today are lacking. Our analyses show fishing is in the coastal seas where automated platforms can’t operate. 
It’s counter-intuitive that data are lacking close to shore, and these regions are where data is most important for stakeholders.
We are a startup operating and collaborating from Greenland to New Zealand. 
The thousands of fishing vessels going out to sea every day present a tremendous opportunity to fill the most pressing gaps in our sustained ocean observation. We provide both data collection as a service and a platform for centralized FAIR data management.

entityDescription:
Prusa Polymers a. s. represents one of the key companies of the Prusa Research group, a highly innovative and fast-growing 3D printing company founded by Mr. Josef Průša in 2012. Within a few years, it has become the leading manufacturer of FFF/FDM 3D printers, with roughly a 10% share of the global desktop 3D printer market. The product range was further expanded with the introduction of an SLA 3D printer and with in-house research, development, and production of filament (thermoplastic feedstock, a thin plastic strand) for 3D printing.
The outstanding quality of Prusa Research’s 3D printers was confirmed many times by recognized companies and media, such as 3D Printing Industry Awards (Personal Printer of the Year – 2019, 2018) or Make: Magazine (Best Overall, Outstanding Open Software, Best Value…).
Due to their leading-edge performance, the Original Prusa 3D printers are used by professionals in various industries, such as automotive, entertainment, medical, etc. Aerospace customers of Prusa 3D printers and filaments are represented by key players including European Space Agency (ESA), NASA, and SpaceX, as well as airplane production companies such as Aero Vodochody Aerospace, Blanik Aircraft CZ, Latitude Aerospace Solutions, and Magellan Aerospace.
Prusa Polymers a. s. has its own scientific research capacities, including laboratories enabling in-house material development, a significant part of which is focused on the development of new polymer blends adapted for ideal processing on FDM 3D printers. Using advanced equipment for laboratory development and industrial production of filaments for 3D printing, the company also focuses on testing of thermo-mechanical characteristics of such materials, and their printing properties. The quality of the R&D capacities is also backed by several projects supported by the Technology Agency of the Czech Republic (TACR).

entityDescription:
PoliHub is the Innovation Park & Startup Accelerator of Politecnico di Milano, managed by Fondazione Politecnico di Milano. The objective is to favour the growth of new deep tech startups which can develop products and services with high technological content and generate new opportunities for researchers, entrepreneurs, companies, and investors.
PoliHub supports 
- the creation and development of deep tech startups through technological transformation, providing services for acceleration, access to funding, mentorship, and advice.
- Italian and multinational companies in exploring new products, services, and business models through collaboration with startups at the Innovation Park
- relationships between startups, companies, experts, institutions, and investors built on sharing resources and skills, with the objective of accelerating technological progress and creating economic and strategic benefits.
PoliHub offers:
- access to capital– a structured process developed with the main national venture capital and business angel funds to bring risk capital to startups.
- Consulting Days– consultation sessions with professionals in law, the fiscal & rating sector, commercial sales & development, marketing plans & business model, IP consulting, product & growth consulting, and strategy consulting.
- Mentorship– access to a unique network of more than 100 PoliHub certified mentors that support startups in the construction and validation of their business models.
- Advisory– assistance from one or more advisors to support the development of a strategy to grow and reach annual objectives.
- Education– workshops on content and cutting-edge topics to investigate the state of the art in innovation, startups, growth strategies, and emerging technologies and applications.
- Workspace and facilities– PoliHub offers areas for co-working, private offices, event rooms, meeting rooms, and break areas.
- Community– a network of experts, startups, companies, institutions, and investors that interact during events, generating new business opportunities.

entityDescription:
BONN Elektronik was founded in 1975 for production and sales of RF components and systems. Very soon development and production of a wide range of different power amplifiers and RF-systems became the main activity.
BONN amplifiers have made their good name with high quality and reliability in worldwide stationary and mobile applications. Resulting from the increasing demand, the company had to build a larger building in 2010. 
For more than 40 years our aim has been to advise our customers comprehensively in planning and realizing RF- and microwave systems. We are performant and flexible in developing innovative solutions for our customers. Starting from the quotation phase via delivery and installation of the instruments including maintenance we offer a complete service all from one source. Our development and production teams work on the basis of ISO 9001 total quality management. For many years all our instruments already have complied with CE-standards and VDE safety regulations.
A complete range of measurement instruments, workstations and machines is supporting our engineers to solve most of the jobs inhouse.
EDA software for simulation and calculation of linear and non-linear RF-circuits
EDA based PCB design by means of up-to-date interactive topological auto-routers considering actual EMI practice
CAD-CAM connection from design software to most modern precision CNC milling machines and lathes
Spectrum and network analyzers up to 40 GHz
Photoplotter, recycling etching machine, tinning facility, climatic test chamber and special tools
Measurement setups for individual testing of all instruments for conducted emissions and instrument safety according to VDE regulations
Highly committed employees with long experience in RF technology solve complex demands as required by our customers. We are your competent partner and offer “the power you need”.
The success of BONN Elektronik in high power RF amplifiers led to the founding of a subsidiary in Budapest in 1991. BONN Hungary Electronics focuses on development and production of components and subsystems for mobile communication as well as customized RF synthesizers and oscillators (see product overview).

entityDescription: The PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency is the Dutch national institute for strategic policy analysis in the field of environment, nature and spatial planning. PBL is a part of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, though fully independent as far as the contents of its work is concerned. PBL is particularly experienced in integrated assessments of key environmental issues that go beyond a sectoral approach, analysing the causes and effects of environmental change. It evaluates and assesses policies at regional, national, European and global scale. PBL bases its studies on extensive data analyses, modelling and scenario analyses, maintaining an active dialogue with both the scientific community and policymakers. PBL is strong in biophysical disciplines, but also has expertise in the fields of economy and governance. Over the past decades, it has cooperated with international organizations such as the OECD, UNEP and IPCC as well as operated in European networks. PBL has leading roles in projects for DG Environment, DG Climate Action and DG Research & Innovation, contributing to climate policies and supporting EU policy development. PBL is also the eldest Collaborating Centre to UNEP for Reporting Assessment and Forecasting. Senior staff members serve on panels such as UNEP’s International Resource Panel, co-leading the work on Food and on Cities.

entityDescription: University of Zagreb Faculty of Agriculture (FAZ), founded in 1919, is the oldest and leading institution in the field of agriculture and related sciences in Croatia. FAZ consists of 7 divisions with 28 departments and 450 employees. The Faculty boasts 26 laboratories, 3 of which are accredited, and 8 experimental stations with a total area of 7,897 hectares. FAZ constantly strives to acquire, develop, and transfer knowledge to educate students, scientists, and professionals. By increasing food production, industry, natural resource management, and developing rural and urban environments, FAZ contributes to the overall quality of life in both national and global contexts. The study programs are aligned with the Bologna process: undergraduate, graduate, and postgraduate doctoral and specialist studies. In 2020 the company splits up and the engineering companies that formed it return to operate individually. Today, Hypertec is an innovative engineering company with high skills in the following industrial fields: Automotive, Automatic Machine, Machine tools, Oil & Gas, Aeronautics and Aerospace. An internal Academy - and one dedicated to our best customers -, allows us to better prepare our engineers to face the job market in a winning way. Kersnikova Institute is a non-profit cultural institution operating in the fields of investigative arts, culture, and educational practices, with an emphasis on a future society that is intertwined with modern technologies and science. As an active production platform, Kersnikova enables valuable interdisciplinary interactions between creative individuals, institutions and companies, produces and showcases inspiring works of art, enables intensive public debate, facilitates investigative learning workshops for all ages, and encourages creative individuals to collaborate with the economy in developing social and product innovations. 
Kersnikova Institute combines the contemporary investigative art activities of Kapelica Gallery with activities of Rampa mechatronics laboratory, the BioTehna biotechnology laboratory, which focuses on the artistic research of living systems, and the Vivarium, where animals, plants, and robots meet.
Kapelica Gallery is one of the leading venues for contemporary investigative art on a global scale. Its program, which consists of spatial installations, performances, sound research, and theoretical and critical lectures, focuses on scientific and technological applications, biopolitics, and urban phenomena, which addresses both professional and general public. The gallery’s program is focused on responding to profound changes in a society saturated with new technologies. The program is therefore built from artistic activities that reflect various social phenomena of the present and predict possible future scenarios.
The BioTehna laboratory is a place where complex art projects involving various biological systems are developed, experiments are carried out, and interesting connections between biological materials and technology are explored. At BioTehna, artists and scientists creatively and innovatively combine living systems with electronic technologies into hybrid or symbiotic coexistence, thus exploring the possibilities of their coexistence and coevolution.
Rampa is a laboratory for mechatronics where electronics is programmed, developed and various devices are assembled. The experimental environment is intended for individuals and groups, interested in creative research into new as well as outdated technologies. In conjunction with the other two laboratories, various approaches in the field of mechatronics are tested through possible connections to living systems. The activities of artists, scientists, and engineers of all three laboratories critically thematize the phenomenology of artificial life and thus create the conditions for a better understanding of life and its emancipated interdependence with modern technologies.
More than 25 years of daily activities have created hundreds of unforgettable moments and experiences that have given shape and meaning to contemporaneity as we currently understand it. Today, we transfer these experiences through non-formal investigative learning to children, youth, and the interested public by systematically implementing a capacity development program through interactive workshops led by mentors which are educated through our mentoring program.
The acquired knowledge, inspired by visions of all the possible futures is the starting point for establishing programs for the involvement of creative people in the processes of social and product innovation. By participating in innovation processes with the help of innovation catalysts, we introduce art-thinking and design-thinking for both communities and companies, for more radical, sustainable, and ethical solutions that create opportunities for a better future for individuals and society.

entityDescription:
Digiotouch (DIGI) is a fast-growing SME providing secure, sustainable Digital Transformation products and services. DIGI operates in four industry verticals - Digital Healthcare, Agri-Food, Industry 4.0, and Smart Cities. DIGI’s core competence is to digitize customers' legacy business processes, operations, and assets using two core products - Cloud based, secure Paradise IoT Platform and Digiotouch Edge. The company provides open standard based digital solutions powering next-gen devices and services for the EU Digital Single Market initiative. The Paradise IoT Platform includes several common service functions (e.g. remote monitoring, device management, visualization, end-to-end security, secure storage, privacy), and “Academy for IoT” - a Digital Learning Hub to educate the next-gen workforce on Digital Transformation. The Platform has been utilized by six organizations from the USA, UK, India, and Malaysia. On the technical front, DIGI is pioneering “Digital-First'' strategies which are broadly based on Blockchain, Cybersecurity, Intelligent Cloud & Edge Computing, ICT Standards (e.g. W3C Web of Things, IEEE P2145 - Standard for Framework and Definitions for Blockchain Governance), Machine Learning, and Mobile Apps. 
DIGI has been one of the winners of the EU Datathon 2018 competition. The ground-breaking industrial research & innovation activities of the company has received funding from several EU H2020 projects – upPE-T, BlockStart, DIH-HERO, DIGI-B-CUBE, Block.IS, Logistics for Manufacturing SMEs (L4MS), Fed4FIRE+, StandICT.eu, and Triangle. The company has also been accepted in the EIT Health Living Labs and Test Beds Programme to validate its business model and scale-up strategies for its digital therapeutics’ mobile app AMICA. DIGI is also experienced in managing consortia of cascade funding (e.g. FSTP) projects and has successfully completed and delivered several such projects. In addition to industrial R&D, DIGI has strong experience in market research, business development, product commercialization, and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The company has successfully integrated all the previous EU-funded project outcomes into its core products enhancing their commercial portfolio.

entityDescription:
We are a manufacturer of special bolts and have developed the ability to connect our products (via a fiber optic sensor) to qualify a tightening and control the integrity of the assembly. 
The principle is to integrate a fiber optic sensor housed in its center to screws, studs, and other threaded rods. 
The fiber optic technology used is a patented process based on optical interferometry and allows to calculate the minute variations in lengths by emission of a light (spectrum of a light wave). It is projected onto a set of mirrors and its feedback signals are analysed to determine the lengthening of the bolt to 0.5 µm/m of precision. 
The C-Bolt® can be installed at all industrial sites and in all areas of intervention. It is not only insensitive to rays (nuclear zone), magnetic fields, distances (maximum 3.5 km from its base), temperatures (from -268 to 320 degrees Celsius), ATEX zones, pressure (maxi 300 bars), wetlands (subaquatic), and frequencies. Moreover, by its passive constitution, it does not emit any disturbance.

CEMOSA ofrece sus servicios en las siguientes áreas: Ingeniería, Geotecnia, Seguridad e Higiene, Edificación, Control de Materiales y Certificación de Producto / Marcado CE.
Como laboratorio de control de calidad, CEMOSA lleva a cabo la supervisión técnica de los materiales de construcción, desde sus inicios. Avalada por más de 45 años de experiencia en campo, nos ha llevado a ser reconocidos como Organismo Notificado para la concesión del Marcado CE para determinados productos de construcción.

entityDescription:
RespectUs is a worldwide provider of export control compliance online solutions.
Export Control is the area of legislation that regulates the export, import, transit, brokerage, intangible transfer and technical assistance of controlled goods, software and technology. Those controlled items are prevented, or otherwise restricted (e.g. by the way of a Governmental license), from being sent to destinations where it is perceived the items will be used in a harmful way.
RespectUs will provide a one-stop-shop online platform to ensure the establishment of mechanisms within any company’s daily operational procedures that provide checks and safeguards at vulnerable points of the system. The use of this SaaS (Software-as-a-Service) will reduce the risk of illegal exports, and to be punished by criminal sanctions and important fines.
This one-stop-shop solution will reduce customer pains by offering full automation of screening and checks processes, help in classification of dual-use and other sensitive items, incorporating legislations of all relevant countries and assistance in reaching and proving overall export control compliance. The solution will be used internally by CEOs, compliance officers and product engineers, but also by licensing offices. 
The platform will be composed of different modules, each of them being able to be subscribed to individually: risk assessment, customer screening, product classification, end-use checks, license determination, sanctions & embargoes, knowledge base.

entityDescription:
The Institute of Satellite Geodesy and Inertial Sensing of the German Aerospace Center (DLR) is primarily dedicated to the research and development of quantum technologies, quantum sensor technology and innovative quantum metrological solutions for innovative terrestrial and space-based applications, including the realization of prototype solutions.
The primary research goals of the institute include:
- new developments based on innovative quantum technological methods, which will significantly contribute to the solution of societal and technological challenges,
- novel systems of quantum sensors - for example, high-precision inertial sensors - for space and terrestrial applications that make available and exploit the capabilities of the full spectrum of quantum physical and quantum optical insights, and building upon these
- groundbreaking geodetic applications, advanced reference systems in space and time, and quantum-based navigation solutions.

entityDescription:
The Maria Curie-Skłodowska University (UMCS) in Lublin is the largest university in eastern Poland. In the Ranking of Universities, "Perspektywy" ranks high among Polish universities in the category of "employer preferences", and in the Lubelskie Voivodeship, it has been in the first place for years. The University is at the forefront of universities in Poland in terms of the total number of foreign students. Currently, 1,900 foreigners from nearly 50 countries study here. UMCS initiated the Research in Lublin Program, under which, in cooperation with the Lublin City Hall, it conducts activities aimed at acquiring and employing outstanding scientists from abroad.
The university takes part in pro-entrepreneurial initiatives and programs in the Lublin region, participating, inter alia, in the project "Start-up Platforms for new ideas - Eastern Business Accelerator", where it provides specialized services for start-ups, and in the project "Innovation Incubator 2.0", whose task is to support economically useful results of research and development works and their commercialization.
The strength of UMCS is the academic staff and the research they carry out. Years ago, the University became the cradle of Polish optical fibers. Outstanding achievements in this field are achieved by the team of prof. Paweł Mergo. Many employees of the University can be proud of research of a breakthrough for society, ie: the introduction of a preparation increasing the immunity of bees to the Polish market; creation of industrial technology for the production of mutanase; development of a bio-fertilizer that stimulates the sprouting and growth of legumes and an innovative method of asphalt modification. The UMCS also conducts research on the innovative use of the laccase enzyme in the treatment of cervical cancer, and researchers from UMCS and the Medical University of Lublin have jointly developed a preparation of earthworm celomatous fluid, which in vitro destroys lung cancer cells in 75–5 years. 80%. It is worth mentioning the successes of employees conducting research in the field of biophysics, who broke the world record for resolution in infrared microscopy and discovered a new method of molecular imaging.

Company description: Ellinogermaniki Agogi (EA) is an educational organization of private law, officially recognized by the state. EA was the first Greek educational organization, which applied Open and Distance Learning in secondary level education in the year of 1993.
Since 1998, the organization has established a devoted department, the Research and Development (R&D) Department for the design, development and implementation of research activities in education, expanding the collaboration with Universities and Research Institutions across Europe. The R&D Department, which currently employs 13 full time researchers, acts as interface between the pedagogical research, the technological innovation and the school community.
Since its foundation, the R&D department has been actively involved in more than 11 European projects dedicated to Astronomy or Space exploration as well as many more which were partly related to these two fields. In 2012 EA worked with ESA’s education department to intergrade ESA’s interactive applications in the Go-Lab(https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/317601)platform. As part of the EU Space Awarenessproject(https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/638653)consortium, EA worked alongside ESA’s education representative and numerous ESERO offices designing and delivering e-learning resources for educators and educational resources for students. Following Space Awareness, EA was also part of the SpaceEU project(https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/821832)in which ESA Education was a member of the advisory board. EA is familiar with ESA’s educational content as it has been making use of them for many years not only internally in the school but also in the framework of EU projects and teacher training courses. EA also has a long experience in designing and organizing teacher training workshops and courses on Astronomy and Space exploration.
The work of the R&D Department also focuses on the following areas:
a) the development of methodologies and empirical research to investigate processes of learning and knowledge acquisition in various subject-matter areas (physics, mathematics, biology, history, etc.);
b) the collaboration with computer science departments and artificial intelligence labs for the development of computational models and AI learning systems;
c) the collaboration with Universities and private companies for the development and testing of educational software;
d) the design of technology-supported learning and e-learning environments.

entityName: Centro Interdisciplinar de Investigação Marinha e Ambiental
entityDescription:
CIIMAR was established in 2000 and mobilises a multidisciplinary, highly skilled and motivated team (474 members, incl. 210 with PhD) that works at the frontier of knowledge and innovation. The CIIMAR mission is to promote transdisciplinary research, technological development, and training, contributing to advances in scientific knowledge and sustainability of the marine and coastal environments. CIIMAR fields of expertise cover three research domains: GLOBAL CHANGES AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, AQUACULTURE AND SEAFOOD QUALITY, and MARINE BIOTECHNOLOGY, addressing important economic and societal challenges and contributing to achieving UN Sustainable Development Goals. To deliver our mission and build a shared understanding and valorisation of the ocean, CIIMAR is strongly involved in partnerships, public engagement, and literacy.
CIIMAR publishes annually about 450 ISI publications (60% Q1), supports over 100 PhD and MSc theses, and participates in relevant European and global knowledge and innovation networks (e.g. MARBEF, EUROMARINE, EPBRS, EATIP, ICES, EOOS, AtlantOS, GEO BON, MBON, European Marine Board). The centre features well-equipped laboratories, technological core platforms, and cultivation and animal experimental facilities approved by the Portuguese Veterinary Authority. CIIMAR integrates research infrastructures of national and European relevance: the European Marine Biological Resource Centre (EMBRC-ERIC), the European Multidisciplinary Seafloor Observatory (EMSO-ERIC), the Microbial Resource Research Infrastructure (MIRRI-PT), and the National Infrastructure for Chemical Biology and Genetics (PT-OPENSCREEN).

entityDescription:
VARIEL has been in the business for over fifty years. In 1964 the manufacturing plant was established as a division of a fastener assembly plant called Montážní podnik spojů Praha (Prague Mounting Joint Venture) in Zruč nad Sázavou. The company satisfied needs for fasteners used in a large scale of packaging and technology sheltering. VARIEL, as a joint-stock company was founded in 1993.
Originally this technology referred to utility sheds only. Till present they have remained a part of the company’s product range in a changed form. In the 80s company expanded its product range and included containers designated for accommodating of various kinds of technological systems which were principally designed for the use in telecommunication constructions. Since the mid-90s the technological and special containers have become leading products in the company’s product range.
At the turn of the century, the product range was expanded to include standardized ISO certified containers that are used primarily in the military and integrated rescue systems, but also in the civilian sphere. In addition to containers, fiberglass and composite products form an important part of our product range, the main market of which is the sector of mass transport vehicle production, especially rail vehicles.
Undoubtedly, Variel´s telephone booths and fiber glass postal boxes have remained our most popular products throughout the Czech Republic.
Variel is located on the outskirts of Zruč nad Sázavou, which is about 60 km southeast of Prague and 5 km far from the motorway D1 (connecting Prague and Brno). The company has its own railway delivery tracks that lead to the company from the nearby railway station.
The company employs approximately 170 employees. In addition to a high degree of know-how, the company also has very modern technological equipment. In its machinery we can find a wide range of very sophisticated CNC machines, e.g. 2D laser for sheet metal burning, 3D laser for profile burning, press brakes, punching machines, double-sided sheet bender, 3D tube bender, 3D printer, five-axis machining center, welding robot specially designed for container welding, modern paint shop with surface preparation by blasting, degreasing and phosphating, welding machines for welding steel, stainless steel and aluminum, top certified workstation for gluing etc.

entityDescription:
Climatic warming and the associated increasingly prolonged periods of drought are having a significant impact on our environment. Prolonged periods of drought weaken ecosystems and facilitate the conditions for vegetation fires (forest and field fires) to start and spread in Germany as well. According to the Federal Environment Agency, for example, almost twice as many fires occurred in 2018 and 2019 as in previous years. The risk is expected to increase much more drastically in the future!Settlement structures, infrastructures and our environment are increasingly at risk.
This also poses new challenges for insurance companies, especially in damage and risk management.

At the same time, artificial intelligence methods offer the possibility of using existing data resources to better prepare us for these growing risks.
Using the latest machine learning methods, Karuna Technology's research will leverage existing data from climate models as well as Earth observation satellites to accurately determine and control fire risks.
Karuna Technology is versatilely positioned to solve the problems that arise. Experts from the fields of deep learning and computer vision, key account management in the insurance sector, earth observation, space engineering and business development are part of the team.
For the development of the necessary algorithms, cooperations with renowned scientific institutes are in place. These include the European Space Agency (ESA), the Fraunhofer Institute for Computer Graphics Research, the Senckenberg Natural Research Society and the Technical University of Darmstadt.

in Quebec, Reaction Dynamics (RDX) is developing rockets to provide routine access to earth's orbit. The company addresses the environmental issue of launching satellites to orbit by turning recycled polymers into high-performance rocket fuel.

The company is vertically integrated and is building an eco-friendly launch vehicle featuring a proprietary hybrid propulsion system and can deliver the same payload to orbit as it's competitors for 1/3 of the price while emitting 30% less CO2. It’s one- of-a-kind, patent-pending hybrid propulsion technology enables these affordable launch services, with short lead times.

Its innovative approach solves the persisting issue with hybrid engines: limited performance over long duration burn times. This technology enables affordable, environmentally friendly and reliable launch services that can be rapidly scaled

PlanAdapt  is an independent global network-based  organisation  that provides knowledge services in support of effective, economically just and socially inclusive climate change adaptation and climate risk management around the world. We approach complex challenges through transdisciplinary mixed methods and engagement of doers and thinkers across the spheres of science, policy and practice. Our advisors and researchers are  specialised  in methods and processes to bridge the adaptation science-action gap. 
 PlanAdapt  focuses on a suite of advisory services that enable innovative and effective adaptation to climate impacts and management of climate-related risks. We are a group of ‘thinkers’, that conduct applied research and develop conceptual approaches for adaptation, and ‘doers’ in sectors and contexts where current and future climate risks matter. This mixture allows us to constantly calibrate our knowledge pool through balancing tacit, experience-based knowledge from our practitioners and explicit knowledge from research and theory.

The University of Rzeszow, constituted in 2001, is the largest university in the south-east of Poland (Podkarpackie region), educating over 17,000 students in 60 academic disciplines. It consists of 4 colleges: the College of Humanities, the College of Medical Sciences, the College of Natural Sciences, the College of Social Sciences, which are divided into 21 single-disciplinary institutes. 
The University, accredited to offer 18 doctoral and 6 post-doctoral degree studies, is proud of fruitfulcooperation with its stakeholders from both the social and economic environment, including enterprises, industry, central and local governments and other academic centers. Its infrastructure and human resources potential enable not only to create new quality in the area of scientific development, but also in commercial services. University serves as a platform for dialogue, exchange of ideas and creation of new solutions at theoretical and practical levels. Hence, its active participation in projects in the fields of basic and applied sciences. 
Within the College of Natural Sciences there are the following research centres: 
The Centre for Microelectronics and Nanotechnology with laboratories:
- Technological complex: MBE technology with all parameters control (e.g TOF SIMS, HR XRD, SEM, AFM, Raman spectrosopy) with clean room infrastructures
- Photolithography and electron lithography technological laboratory EDX Computer-aided technological measurements laboratory for students
- Student laboratory for conduction phenomena in semi-conduction structures
- Optical phenomena in semi-conductor laboratory for students
- Low-temperature luminescence science laboratory
- Science laboratory for magnetic transportation in nanostructures
The main area of its activity is focused around Quantum heterostructures for photonics and optoelectronics. The Centre realizes application projects from national financial instruments dedicated to heterostructures for IR detectors in wide range of applications from 1.2um up to 12um based on SLS-II type. It develops the technology based on II-VI semiconductors compounds also for IR applications as well as for Thz sources and detectors. The coherent laboratory allows to produce and verify all the necessary properties like crystallographic and chemical quality, structural and electronic properties of surfaces and interfaces.

- Manufacturing Engineering Laboratory
- Materials Spectroscopy Laboratory
- Mechanical and Electrical Systems Control Laboratory
- Environmental Research and Control Laboratory

- Applied IT Systems Laboratory
- Information Society Laboratory
- Applied Mathematics Laboratory
- Supporting Unit.

entityName: United Nations University -Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS)
entityDescription:
The United Nations University (UNU) is the academic arm of the United Nations and acts as a global think tank. The mission of the Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS) is to carry out cutting edge research on risks and adaptation related to environmental hazards and global change. The institute’s research promotes policies and programmes to reduce these risks, while taking into account the interplay between environmental and societal factors.
Research areas include climate change adaptation incorporating insurance-related approaches, environmentally induced migration and social vulnerability, ecosystem services and environmental deterioration processes, models and tools to analyze vulnerability and risks linked to natural hazards, with a focus on urban space and rural-urban interfaces. Research is always conducted with the underlying goal of connecting solutions to development pathways.
Beyond its research mandate, UNU-EHS is actively engaged in education. It offers the joint Master of Science degree programme “The Geography of Environmental Risks and Human Security” with the University of Bonn. UNU-EHS also hosts a number of international PhD projects and courses on global issues of environmental risks and sustainable development. The institute is based in Bonn, Germany

GEM’s mission is to become one of the world’s most complete sources of risk resources and a globally accepted standard for seismic risk assessment; and to ensure that its products are applied in earthquake risk management worldwide.
GEM builds capacity to assess and manage risk through open, transparent and collaborative seismic risk assessment at local, national, regional and global scales. entityDescription:
Fundación Instituto Tecnológico de Galicia (ITG, www.itg.es) is a private non-profit research and technology organization set up in 1991, that aims to improve the competitiveness of enterprises, organizations and professionals through research, technological development and professional services. It provides expertise in the design, development and implementation of complex ICT-based technology (software and hardware) for the monitoring and control of processes and infrastructures (mainly energy and water grids, buildings). Its main fields of activity are: Sensing and Telecommunication, Software Engineering, Energy Efficiency, Water Technologies and Construction Technologies.

ITG has a team of more than 60 people, most of them telecommunication, aeronautic, software and industrial engineers. The centre has participated in more than 70 R&D national and international projects and has provided services to 347 different customers during the last three years. ITG has been recognized as a National Technology Center by the Ministry of Economic and Competitiveness of the Spain Government (registration number 115). The entities that constitute its Board of Trustees are: the Regional Government of Galicia; the Universities of A Coruña, Vigo and Santiago de Compostela; the Confederation of Galician Enterprise Associations; the official Galician Associations of Civil Engineers, Industrial Engineers and Architects. ITG chairs the Executive Board of the Spanish Federation of Technological Centres (FEDIT) and is member of the World Association of Industrial and Technological Research Organisations (WAITRO). 

In the aeronautic sector, ITG is member of the following organizations and networks: European Network of U-space Demonstrators, managed by EUROCONTROL; European Organization for Civil Aviation Equipment (EUROCAE), where it is involved in the working-group “Unmanned Aircraft Systems” and contributes to the development of industry standards for unmanned vehicles; advisory Board of the Spanish Agency for the Aeronautic Security (AESA); Galician Association of Unmanned Intelligent Systems (AGASINT).At national level, ITG is member of the network of excellence “iMOV3D: New Technologies for Smart Mobility based on Urban Air Mobility”, funded by the Spanish Centre for Industrial Development (CDTI). This R&D network aims to increase the research capacities on 3 main fields: air vehicle autonomy, intelligent and autonomous control systems for urban air mobility, intelligent collaborative systems for the integration of UAVs in the urban space
