entityName: Institute for Chemical Processing of Coal
entityDescription:
Institute for Chemical Processing of Coal operates under Act on Research Institutes from the 30th of April 2010. It was established pursuant to The Resolution of Council of Ministers no 192/55 from 1955. The supervising body of the Institute is the Minister of State Assets.
The main recipients and customers of the Institute know-how are companies from power, waste-processing and coke-making industries, small and medium enterprises as well as organizations from government and self-government administration. The Institute participates in many R&D and implementation projects, cooperating with more than 50 national and international scientific and R&D centers.
The prior strategy of the Institute is to gear its research field to the development of low- and zero-emission heat and electrical energy production technologies, including clean coal technologies, CO2 capture and storage (CCS) and utilization (CCU) systems, as well as energy production from renewable resources.
The performance of many analyses on actual and perspective routes of the development of power, heat, waste management and coke-making industries is the basis of current research topics and action lines.
According to the Long-Term Research Program of the Institute the undertaken activities are focused on:
· thermochemical conversion of solid fuels for energy and chemical industry,
· environmentally friendly and economically effective residential and municipal heating systems based on natural and processed solid fuels,
· circular economy – waste to energy or residues to products,
· thermochemical energy storage by means of solid-gas reactions,
· effective and environmentally safe coke making and coal derivatives processing industries,
· advanced materials for novel energy generation technologies and e-mobility (including H2 transport).
All the activities are carried out with the emphasis to environmental protection issues, especially to the reduction of emission of greenhouse gases as well as gaseous and particulate contaminants.
Institute’s references include:
· cokemaking industry – 1770 projects,
· power industry – 1243 projects,
· coal mining – 276 projects,
· carbochemistry – 1135 projects,
· higher education – 209 research projects and scientific grants,
· international projects (including EU) – 125 projects,
· 37 scientific monographs,
· 2508 scientific and technical papers,
· 245 patents, 39 utility models and 34 trade marks,
· 276 organized conferences and scientific seminars.

entityDescription:
Roofit Solar Energy is an Estonian company headquartered in Tallinn which operates in the field of Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) and produces a 2-in-1 innovative product: a metal roof with integrated solar panels. It looks like traditional steel roofs and electrically is as powerful as conventional solar panels.
Roofit.solar focuses on the premium quality and safety measures. To date, there are more than 100 Roofit.solar roofs in Estonia, Germany, Austria, Denmark, Poland, Sweden, Norway, Latvia and Kenya. Apart from the excellent visual aspect and innovativeness of the product, the company promotes green energy to mitigate climate change. Unlike the use of fossil fuels, that emit high levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) and cause severe health and ecological damage, sunlight is free, renewable, infinite, and easily accessible. Therefore, our solar roofs help to reduce harmful effects of carbon footprint and diminish global pollution levels.
The team behind Roofit Solar Energy has experience in research, large-scale international energy projects, product development, export and high-quality service. We have an individual approach towards each client and do our best to provide them with premium quality solar roofs that are efficient and durable for decades to come. And this is just the beginning. We work hard to make solar metal roofs accessible for more and more people around the globe to change the way the world is powered.

entityDescription:
Having provided humanitarian aid over several decades in some of the worst hit places, SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL responds to the basic necessities of the most vulnerable, relieves their suffering, and enables them to retain their dignity and cope with even the most challenging of situations.
Based on the concept of need, this remit translates into delivering water, sanitation and hygiene aid, as well as food security and shelter. How? By supplying aid directly to those who need it, as quickly and efficiently as possible, and in a manner that is both sustainable, participative and effectively coordinated. But not only.
Working closely alongside those in need, SOLIDARITÉS INTERNATIONAL also has a duty and a responsibility to record and bear witness, as stipulated by its charter, so that people’s voices are heard and their realities exposed. This way, we can raise awareness among the media, the general public and decision-makers. This can only help us make our support more efficient and the way it is delivered more pertinent.
Taking aid further bearing witness.

entityDescription:
Holoxica’s vision is to “Solve 3D”.Holoxica is a research intensive SME specialising in disruptive holographic 3D solutions from motion video displays to static images. Our tech does not need any head gear where 3D images appear in mid-air, viewable naturally, just like "Star Wars". We have an experienced team delivering on extreme hardware, software and 3D graphics projects. We offer 3D light-field displays capable of showing colour motion video. We can convert any kind of 3D digital data into a hologram. Our technology is positioned beyond current AR/VR and can be a direct replacement for this.The main applications are in professional (B2B) medical, scientific, military, industrial and commercial markets.We have recently pioneered telepresence technology which allows full duplex (two-way) 3D video conferencing across a broadband network.
The Holoxica next-generation display technology is a step improvement over current AR/VR systems that use wearable goggles or glasses. Light field 3D displays do not require any eye-wear, whereby multiple people can view the 3D image and interact with it. Holoxica has built several generations of holographic video displays from simple segmented systems to HUDs, volumetric and light-field displays. We are a value-added reseller for the Looking Glass 3D Light field display, where we build a whole solution computing system, middleware, I/O and graphics software.
Holoxica has extensive, over 55 cumulative years’, experience in managing high tech projects in both consumer and professional electronics. This means taking ideas to proof of concept, prototyping and products. Our team’s areas of expertise include: medical imaging, 3D graphics software, embedded systems, 3D graphics design and display hardware engineering. We have a solid track record and experience of building teams to execute advanced projects. These include grants from the EU Horizon 2020 Programme, Innovate UK and Ministry of Defence DSTL/DASA contracts.

In addition to a big industrial player in the field of X-ray diffractometers its customers are research, university, and synchrotron laboratories.
Through its staff it has a number of collaborations and has been involved in numerous national and international research projects. It has expertise in various specialized X-ray optics not only for diffractometry, but also for other fields of laboratory and synchrotron X-ray techniques and technology, including

Company description: SPICI srl – Company for Innovation, Cooperation and Internationalization, is a Hub for innovation that, operating as an international accelerator and center for entrepreneurship, designs and supports entrepreneurial development, intergovernmental programs for scientific cooperation, technology transfer and internationalization for startups, university spinoffs and innovative SMEs, and develops digital transformation solutions for enterprises and public administration.
SPICI is an active and interconnected part of the ecosystem of knowhow, digital academies and scientific infrastructures of the Technological Pole of the University of Naples Federico II and within this highly valued context, SPICI provides advanced services for the Italian and European industrial and research system (in particular for startups and SMEs), which include scouting, acceleration, digital innovation, technology transfer, finance for growth.
Leveraging on the extensive and consolidated experience of the founders, SPICI works to encourage the attraction in Italy and Europe of capital, talents and innovative projects, providing specialized consultancy and financing guidance services.
SPICI operates both, directly and through its partners on the entire life cycle of startups, from the business conception phase to development on international markets, supporting teams and companies in the process of:
· information and guidance on business creation and entrepreneurial training;
· animation and scouting of new business ideas and management of pre-incubation and acceleration programs;
· accompanying the creation and development of businesses through tutoring, mentorship, coaching, team building, business development and management of incubation and co-working spaces;
· accompanying access to risk finance (venture capital, business angel);
· support for patenting and technology transfer;
· support for the development of digital transformation solutions;
· access to internationalization programs and initiatives.
 
SPICI, with the aim of supporting companies and public administrations in the process of digital transformation, operates its division FabriTech. It acts as a technological laboratory for the development of digital products — including softwares, mobile and web apps and physical products — and related organizational solutions which impact on the way the organization operates internally and within the market.
SPICI has managed several programs related to business acceleration, among these, there is the “CHINA-ITALY BEST STARTUP SHOWCASE - ENTREPRENEURSHIP COMPETITION” the bilateral platform aimed at promoting the internationalization of Italian and Chinese innovative enterprises (startups, spinoffs, SMEs) that offers the opportunity to get close, approach, do business and land in the two Countries and to meet investors, incubators, science parks and partners through an intense and qualified networking activity.

Siemens Healthineers is a global powerhouse in healthcare, combining the agility, independent-thinking, and responsiveness of a strategy consulting firm with the research and scaling capabilities of a leader in medical technology. Our mission is to enable healthcare providers to increase value by empowering them on their journey towards expanding precision medicine, transforming care delivery, and improving patient experience, all enabled by digitalizing healthcare. An estimated five million patients worldwide everyday benefit from our innovative technologies and services in the areas of diagnostic and therapeutic imaging, laboratory diagnostics and molecular medicine as well as digital health and enterprise services, such as consulting. With over 54,000 employees in more than 70 countries, over 120 years of experience and 18.500 patents globally, we will continue to innovate and shape the future of healthcare. 

At the heart of this leader in medical technology sits Value Partners for Healthcare Consulting. We are an independent and vendor agnostic strategy consulting unit at Siemens Healthineers with offices in Berlin, Erlangen, and Singapore. Our interdisciplinary team of doctors, nurses, health scientists and economists has successfully completed more than 500 projects worldwide since our inception 22 years ago. Embedding a strategy consulting unit into the global network of Siemens Healthineers’ technology leadership creates impactful synergies that our clients are profiting from. This combination generates value from how Siemens Healthineers shapes the technology landscape with its comprehensive and innovative portfolio but also beyond the product by a more profound understanding of our customers’ challenges and needs through the consulting business. As a result, we are shapingthe future of healthcare by our own groundbreaking technology innovations and help our customers unlocking their full potential by our wide-ranging expertise in strategic and transformational consulting services. With the help of our deep clinical and medical knowledge, digital platforms, and global SIEMENS network, we strive to build long-term relationships with our customers helping them to further improve healthcare delivery and provide better care at lower cost.

entityName: University of Ljubljana, Biotechnical faculty - UL BF
entityDescription: The Faculty’s mission is to offer higher professional education, undergraduate and postgraduate university study programmes, as well as research and professional and advisory services in the areas of living nature (biology, microbiology), agriculture, forestry and fishery (forestry, animal science, agronomy) and in closely related production technologies (wood science, food science, biotechnology).All the educational and research disciplines provided at the Biotechnical Faculty incorporate the issues of management of natural resources (soil, space, flora and fauna, water). The Biotechnical Faculty, with its research into environmental resources and its sustainable management orientation, is an institution needed by every nation in its efforts to define and preserve its identity. Research and education in the area of life and nature obliges the Biotechnical Faculty to provide the professional and scientific foundations and an appropriate atmosphere in society that will enable the creation and development of a sustainable symbiotic existence between man and nature.Environmental renovation and protection, preservation of the natural and cultural heritage, ecological and sustainable use of natural resources like wood, production and processing of high quality food and the use of modern biotechnology, are global challenges demanding a constant and strenuous search for the new and better and for furthering expertise that will be widely accessible and utilized in everyday life.Scientific research at the Biotechnical Faculty comprises basic, applied and developmental work. It enables research findings and accomplishments to be widely accessible in life. Professional and advisory services, as part of the research activities, keep the staff of the Faculty informed about emerging needs and issues of practice, facilitates their participation in resolving problems and thus becoming familiar with new ideas that can be successfully applied in teaching and research. A circle is created: basic research – applied research – education – professional work and development. Such an approach requires close linkage with production in order to meet the practical needs of individual professions and those responsible for social development. With a variety of educational and research programmes, the Biotechnical Faculty encourages interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approaches to education and integral research into developmental issues that are becoming more and more complex and influenced by the interests of various professions. In addition, it tries to promote and advance the highest quality, internationally recognized scientific and professional cooperation, openness, and a reputation for excellence. The international competitiveness of the Faculty guarantees the quality of its educational, research and developmental activities.

Company description: Innovation experience HUB (innexHUB), Digital Innovation Hub of East Lombardy, was established in July 2017 as a non-profit association by the Industrial Associations of Brescia, Cremona and Mantova and two craftmanship associations located in Brescia. The aim was to create a subject focused on spreading the digital culture among SMEs, making them aware of: what being digital means, what KETs are, how the digital is rapidly transforming business models and the current and future opportunities / threats linked to digital technologies.
innexHUB has two additional purposes: to help enterprises understand their digital maturity level and identify the subsequent actions to digitally evolve as well as to guide enterprises in their digital transformation paths, ensuring they can rely on trustworthy suppliers.
During 2017 and 2018 innexHUB strengthened its governance by engaging with 6 new shareholders (associations and confederations) representing 3 additional sectors: Agriculture, Construction and Commerce, Tourism and Hospitality Services. As of now innexHUB action field encompasses and addresses 4 sectors (Industry; Agriculture; Construction; Commerce, Tourism and Hospitality Services) as well as 1 horizontal cluster (Craftmanship) made of micro and small enterprises across different sectors.
It is worthy to mention that 2 Universities figure among innexHUB shareholders and their technical and scientific contribution is essential for the hubs’ governance and orientation (e.g., representatives from both Universities have a seat in the hub’s Technical and Scientific Committee).
Altogether innexHUB partners (shareholders) represent more than 50.000 SMEs located in the provinces of Brescia, Cremona and Mantova, equalling a third of the total population of active enterprises in the three provinces listed above.
In 2018 innexHUB has become fully operational by developing a catalogue of services that includes:
• Awareness creation: design and organization of seminars and workshops centred around the increasing role and opportunities of KETs and digitalization as well as the provision and dissemination of information / materials (e.g. videos and reports on best practices / success cases) by means of the hub’s website, e-learning platform and social channels;
• Digital Maturity assessment: development and administration of digital maturity / readiness assessments, both in self-assisted (freely accessible web-based application) and assisted modes (on premises interviews), to evaluate an enterprise current state of digital readiness (i.e., processes, products, tools, skills) and identify possible evolutionary trajectories;
• Ecosystem building, scouting, brokerage, networking: development of a catalogue of certified suppliers providing technical consulting in the design and implementation of digitalization projects as well as continuous training and education opportunities around digital topics to boost workforce upskilling;
• Access to funding: dissemination of digital innovation funding opportunities and support to SMEs in accessing to public and private funding instruments;
• Mentoring: support prior and during the implementation of digital transformation projects;
• Education and skills development: co-creation, in partnership with external organizations, of training and education courses providing intelligence on SMEs’ needs and how to better address them.

Company description: Confindustria Brescia was founded on the 14th of April 1897. It is the oldest Italian entrepreneurial organization, having been active for over 110 years. As part of the Confindustria system, the Association represents the industrial and services sectors in the province of Brescia in all the political, institutional, administrative and trade union bodies, both local and national, in order to safeguard their interests.
This Representation is coordinated with other trade associations operating in the province of Brescia to protect the general interests of industry and the competitiveness of the economy of Brescia.
Confindustria Brescia now brings together more than 1,300 large, small and medium-sized enterprises operating in different sectors and employing a labour force of over 67,000 people.

Mission and objectives
The main mission of the Confindustria Brescia is to support entrepreneurial culture, to promote the development of the area. Members of the Confindustria Brescia can be industrial firms and consortiums producing goods and offering services.
The main objectives of the Confindustria Brescia are:
· to encourage the spreading of entrepreneurial culture to develop the local economy through the promotion of innovation, the high quality of products and the improvement of production processes.
· to pursue sustainable growth of industrial activities by providing assistance, consulting, and training courses to companies.
· to develop competitiveness and the international aspect of industry in the area of Brescia.
· to promote a closer link between education and the production system.
· to assist the growth of employment and enhance the qualification of the workforce through training courses.
· to contribute to improving the local infrastructure facilities. 
· to strengthen interaction with local institutions and trade unions in order to develop the industrial framework of the province of Brescia along with the competitiveness of all firms.

entityDescription:
We at the Atlas Aero GmbH are certain that personal transport will undergo substantial transformation within the next decade. Therefore, we have developed and conceptually optimized Origin – an airplane which combines the advantages of fixed-wing aircraft with vertical take-off and landing capabilities. Its efficiency in forward flight is unrivalled by any of the existing concepts.
 
Avoid congestion, travel at 300 kph while using just as much fuel as a smart car (<5l/100km or, up to 1500km. Use established infrastructure like streets and garages – all due to Origin’s foldable wings which allow for on-ground driveability at 30 kph and space-efficient parking. Due to the use of a serial hybrid drive, we can easily switch to fuel cells powered by hydrogen or synthetic fuels as soon as they become available. Purely electric versions of our aircraft for shorter distances are also viable.
 
Our first airplane version is targeting pilots and VIP transports as a competition to small helicopters – being faster, greener, higher in range and easier-to-fly. These advantages also make it a great choice for first responders. Due to the outstanding aerodynamic efficiency, Origin’s concept can easily be optimized to obtain travel speeds of >400kph if efficiency is not the primary priority.
 
The second generation is intended to fly autonomously and may therefore reach a mainstream market, competing with cars and enabling ride-sharing models – ideal for the infrastructure of the future.

Use established infrastructure like streets and garages – all due to Origin’s foldable wings which allow for on-ground driveability at 30 kph and space-efficient parking. Due to the use of a serial hybrid drive, we can easily switch to fuel cells powered by hydrogen or synthetic fuels as soon as they become available. Purely electric versions of our aircraft for shorter distances are also viable.
 
Our first airplane version is targeting pilots and VIP transports as a competition to small helicopters – being faster, greener, higher in range and easier-to-fly. These advantages also make it a great choice for first responders. Due to the outstanding aerodynamic efficiency, Origin’s concept can easily be optimized to obtain travel speeds of >400kph if efficiency is not the primary priority.
 
The second generation is intended to fly autonomously and may therefore reach a mainstream market, competing with cars and enabling ride-sharing models – ideal for the infrastructure of the future.

entityDescription:
CGC has existed in one form or another for 30 years. Established in 1985 as a Materials Consultancy the company quickly developed an engineering/design competency concentrating on custom technical solutions for the aerospace, medical and industrial markets.
Demand for a “one-stop-shop” resulted in CGC developing and later expanding its manufacturing competency with the acquisition of a precision machine and fabrication shop in 2005. This acquisition is today organised under the Sheet Metal Precision Limited
Today, The CGC Group comprises two legal entities CGC Technology Limited & Sheet Metal Precision Limited. Both companies are ISO9001 accredited and CGC’s has a growing list of repeat business from blue-chip customers.
CGC’s technical competence and ability to innovate commercially attractive products was recognised by the UK Government in 2009 with the award of Queens Award for Enterprise: Innovation and our success in growing our business has been recognised this year by the UK Government with the 2016 Queens Award for Enterprise: Export.
In 2000 the company expanded into the manufacture of LEO satellite tracking antenna, delivering its first antenna in 2001. This system is still fully operational and in use by our client today.
In the intervening fifteen years CGC continued to innovate and develop its satellite ground station skills based adding competency in software writing, feed design, carbon reflector design (single and dual shaping), frequency selective subreflectors and low loss radome design.
Using the concept of product families and platform-based product development to increase variety, shorten lead-times, and reduce costs without compromising system performance CGC, today, is able to offer a product range, with generic ‘family’ features from 1.8M to 13M aperture to include auto-tracking systems as well as a range of deployable trailer mounted or fixed systems
CGC offers complete ground station solutions or will provide sections of the ground segment to global customer.

Albron is a foodservice company which is specialized in different areas. Namely: food concepts in business and industries, hospitality & leisure, health care and education. Our roots go back to 1900 in the harbour of Rotterdam. Together with the Rotterdam People’s Union and the Railway Temperance Association we started special halls where workers from the harbour could have their lunches warm and dry. HORIBA MIRA (hereafter referred to as MIRA) is a global provider of pioneering engineering, research and test services to the automotive, defence, aerospace and rail sectors. We work in close collaboration with vehicle manufacturers and suppliers around the world, providing comprehensive support ranging from individual product tests to turnkey engineering design, development and build programmes. 
With over 70 years’ experience in developing some of the world’s most iconic vehicles, our engineers utilise the latest test facilities and simulation tools to make vehicles and journeys safer, cleaner, more efficient and rewarding. Our suite of 37 major test facilities, 100km of specialised proving ground and wealth of engineering experience, combined with our expanding international presence, means we are confident that we can achieve our vision – that by 2020 every journey in the world will be positively influenced by us.
Progress towards achieving our vision has been significantly accelerated through the creation of MIRA Technology Park, Europe’s largest transport technology R&D cluster. By applying our advanced engineering, test and validation capabilities to our customers’ challenging programmes, we are already shaping journeys of the future.

OGS, Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e Geofisica Sperimentale (National Institute of Oceanography and Applied Geophysics) is an internationally oriented public research institution. This institution operates and develops its own mission in the European Research Area (ERA) and internationally, prioritizing the basic and applied research fields of:

Oceanography (under the Physical, Chemical and Biological aspects);
Geophysics and Marine Geology;
Experimental and Explorative Geophysics.
OGS applies its own expertise in Earth Sciences, and in Marine and Polar regions to contribute not only to the spreading and widening of the knowledge, but also to the practical solution of environmental, economical and social issues in line with the National Program of Research (PNR) and strategic objectives set by the EU, with particular referral to Horizon 2020.

entityDescription: The Studium Generalis Kalaritanum was founded in 1620 along the lines of the old Spanish Universities of Salamanca, Valladolid and Lérida. It originally offered Law, Latin, Greek and Hebrew Literature, the Liberal Arts, Medicine, Surgery, Philosophy and Science. When Sardinia passed under the House of Savoy government in the 18th century, the statute of the University was significantly modified, with the expansion of the science faculties and institutes. Designed by the Piedmontese engineer Saverio Belgrano di Famolasco, the new University building was completed at the end of the 18th century. Today it hosts the Rectorate and the administrative offices. The 19th and 20th centuries saw more and more emphasis placed on research activities, with the achievement of important, internationally acclaimed results, especially in the fields of Medicine, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Archaeology. In the 20th century, problems arising from severe damage to University buildings during the Second World War had to be addressed, and reconstruction is only now approaching its final phase. At the end of the 1960s ambitious plans were advanced for residential university structures in a campus style.

entityName: FONDAZIONE ISI - ISTITUTO PER L'INTERSCAMBIO SCIENTIFICO
entityDescription: The ISI foundation has been established in 1988 in Torino, where it still has its headquarter. In 2014 ISI established together with the Fondazione Sviluppo e Crescita CRT the related sister ISI Global Science Foundation in New York. The history of ISI is long and exciting, marked and characterized by a number of crucial steps and visionary men behind them: to begin with, intellectuals such as Carl Kaysen, Thomas Kuhn and Salva Luria, under the guide of the first President, Tullio Regge and later Mario Rasetti. Since its very beginning, ISI promoted a distinctive borderless attitude, which allowed it to draw an endless arc through time, space, disciplines and research domain to fulfill its continued commitment to its values. By proactively meeting these scientific challenges, ISI has nurtured the creation of a distributed network of top-notch researchers which enables a valuable knowledge exchange with targeted stakeholders, such as the broader scientific community, philanthropists, global foundations, governments and corporations in order to contribute to social, economic and cultural growth at global scale. Within the overarching domain of Complexity Science, the ISI Foundation leverages the competing contributions of Data and Theory to avoid the silos of science too prevalent elsewhere. The combination of data, theory and impact is the founding essence of all the ISI research domains, which feed each other through borderless collaborations among multidisciplinary scientists, providing a solid, growing and high-potential knowledge capital that can be leveraged in all possible endeavors. The exciting Scientific story of ISI was a long difficult but beautiful path whose horizon is as unpredictable and challenging, but stimulating and exciting as the exploration of the very frontiers of new science can be.

entityDescription:
Vianet is an Italian SME founded in 1993. It uses technologies to transform organizations and their processes, enabling them to be competitive, innovate their services, and improve performance while reducing costs.
Its competence includes international pilot projects with KPI definition, measurement, and verification involving citizens, stakeholders, and final users.
Its staff has participated in 500+ projects, sometimes as work package leaders and participating in project management.
Activities
- Definition and development of solutions using the most suitable technologies and methodologies (participatory design, Agile) to demonstrate, measure, and evaluate them in pilot cases and living labs
- Improvement of the customer experience and citizens, stakeholders, and tourists’ involvement in territories, communities, archaeological and cultural sites
- Communication, dissemination, and exploitation.
 
Vianet has been an ordinary member and center of excellence of DTC (District of Cultural Technologies) Lazio since 2021.
It is also a DTC-approved research and innovation infrastructure laboratory with expertise and references in exploiting and optimizing research, communication, and disseminating project results.
In addition, the company has over 100 European and international partners worldwide, with whom it participates in projects for Horizon Europe and internationally.
The list of major academic partners includes Sapienza, Tor Vergata, Roma3, Imperial College London, the University of Malaga, the Technical University of Kosice, the University of Haifa, Aalborg University, the Polytechnic University of Barcelona, Helwan University in Cairo, and Al-Balqa University in Jordan.
The primary research and innovation organizations include the CNR, the INFN, the ENEA, and the Institute of Communication and Information Systems of Athens.
The public administration includes the Ministry of Culture and Tourism in Ankara and the Ministry of Culture in Tunisia.
Private partners include L Global (USA), ClioMuse Tours, Khora, LiveViewStudio, SQLI Services, Holusion, and Setur.
Vianet has a collaboration agreement with Prof. Maurizio Forte, PhD, the William and Sue Gross Distinguished Professor of Classical Studies Art, Art History, and Visual Studies at Duke University (Durham, North Carolina), to develop generative AI for reconstructing ancient sites and environments. Prof. Forte was recently awarded the San Francesco Prize in Techno-Humanities 2024 for his work in Digital Humanities.
 
Recent Projects:
- Pluggy, EU grant no. 726765, https://Pluggy.eu
- 3D Tuning In, EU grant no. 644051, https://3d-tune-in.eu/
- Artemisia, DTC Lazio, https://www.dtclazio.it/artemisia-infn
- Ciabot, DTC Lazio, https://progettociabotdtc.it
- R.O.M.A., DTC Lazio, https://progettoromadtc.it
- STEP, DTC Lazio, demo https://bit.ly/4bkl6Rh
- Archeoverse, https://archeoverse.com
- ENGAGE, tba
 
Our policy includes supporting and respecting the protection of human rights.
Vianet upholds the elimination of discrimination in employment and occupation. We contribute to the enjoyment of rights, including those based on gender, race, religion, color, or disability.

The Project, in which the Universities of Campania, ENEA, CNR and a sufficient number of small and medium-sized enterprises participated, analyzes and provides solutions to the problem created by the introduction of an increasing number of distributed storage generation systems and rapidly variable loads that require electrical networks to meet the growing needs of flexibility, accessibility, reliability and quality of electrical service , economy and energy efficiency. The primary activities were the analysis and definition of requirements, functions, processes, design and testing of technologies with prototypes and demonstrators, technical-economic evaluations and interventions for energy saving and improvement of sustainability.

The core business of the ECU is the promotion of an efficient use of energy resources, moving from a linear and expensive economy to a clean and circular economy. To this end, we associate energy issues with cultural issues: the aim of the ECU is to carry out projects that will accompany businesses with a sustainable transition. Through the proposal of innovative technologies and, accompanied by energy diagnoses and specific energy saving solutions, ECU offers solutions for different sectors: Public Administration, Health, Industry, Private. Azienda Mobilità e Trasporti S.p.A. (AMT) is the mobility company owned by the City of Genova, the capital and biggest city in the Liguria Region (northern western Italy).
AMT is in charge of providing public transport to the Metropolitan City of Genoa, both in urban and extra-urban territory.
By a multi-modal transport system, counting over 130 million transfers per year covering 27 million kilometers, AMT suits the Genoese transport requirements best.
The multi-modal system is granted by different means of transport: 900 buses and trolley buses, a subway, 2 funicular railways, 13 public elevators, a cog railway, a narrow-gauge railway, an urban ferry-boat and on-call services.
AMT is interested in favoring the ecological transition, monitoring the environment in which it provides its transport service and, in general, improving the service offered by paying particular attention to customers.

entityDescription: The predecessor of Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) was founded in 1635 in the rural town of Nagyszombat by Cardinal Péter Pázmány, as a catholic university for teaching Theology and Philosophy. In 1770-1780, the University was transferred to Buda and later to Pest, and with the support of Maria-Theresa, the Empress of Austria and Queen of Hungary, became the Royal Hungarian University. Over the following decades, new faculties were established to meet the expectations of a learned society. In the second half of the 19th century, the University developed into a centre of modern higher education in today's sense, covering nearly every scholarly field. In 1950 the university was reorganized and adopted its present name. It was named after one of its professors, the world-famous physicist, Loránd Eötvös. Recently, a new campus has been built on the scenic banks of the Danube for the Faculties of Natural and Social Sciences and Informatics. Currently, the university has eight faculties: Science, Informatics, Law and Political Sciences, Humanities, Social Sciences, Education and Psychology, Elementary and Nursery School Teacher Training and the Bárczi Gusztáv Faculty of Special Education. Eötvös Loránd University is internationally recognized and its programs are accredited by the Hungarian Accreditation Board. The diplomas issued by Eötvös Loránd University are acknowledged worldwide, and its course credits are transferable in all countries in the European Union.Over the last hundred years, Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE) has had many world famous scientists and four Nobel Prize laureates among its teachers and alumni. The current number of students enrolled yearly has reached 32 000, and there is an academic staff of 1800 highly-qualified teachers and researchers.

entityDescription: PXL was founded in 2001. The mission of the company is to provide highly specialized competences in design and development of solutions for telecommunication and industrial embedded systems.PXL offers itself as a reliable technological partner to very demanding clients, thanks to the adoption of the most up-to-date techniques for software analysis and design, the skills on organization of complex development processes, the continuous investment in research.PXL has increased its abilities in fulfilling strategies aimed to communication and data security (COMSEC, TRANSEC) and in applying advanced software engineering methods (i.e. ¿software radio¿) for the development of radio equipments. Such abilities find successful application in complex telecommunication projects, where the company is involved as a partner or as a supplier of some between the main Italian companies in the sector, such as Selex Communications, Telespazio.PXL uses Voice over IP (VOIP) technology in industrial and military contexts, where the same technology has to be tailored around the specific needs of these fields. In this case VOIP is not strictly related to the implementation of an ordinary telephone service, but can represent a foundation block to achieve solutions that integrate voice communications into a wider range of applications; or it is adopted for its innovative aspects.PXL has a remarkable know-how and expertise in IP based multimedia communication systems, and in their integration with traditional communication networks. In particular, PXL use VOIP technology in applications for security and emergency management agencies. This expertise is the basis of the PXL¿s offer. In this context PXL propose innovative applications for ROIP (Radio Over IP) services. ROIP is the adaptation of VOIP technology for the transport, management and distribution of radio communication over IP networks. The system allows the interoperability of terrestrial radio communication networks, like those based on VHF, UHF, Tetra and Tetrapol standards, with VOIP applications and networks, including those using the satellite segment. Through VOIP, the IP network can support interoperability between the different radio networks and between them and telephone networks.PXL pays particular attention to the relationships with the research world: partnership agreements are held with Universities ¿La Sapienza¿ and ¿Tor Vergata¿ in Rome and research studies are done within ESA (European Space Agency) and ASI (Agenzia Spaziale Italiana) initiatives.PXL also offers consultancy mainly in software engineering to help in development of Mission Critical applications and firmware with real time constraints. The addressed customers are system integrators working in sectors like automotive, environmental monitoring, industrial automation. Besides consultancy, PXL offers a powerful product range, enlarged during time, aiming to empower customers with new tools in order to lessen time-to-market and to direct efforts and resources towards their own core business.PXL has formed partnerships that allow to complete its offer, to extend the market coverage, to improve services and products quality: to this aim, PXL exhibits a ¿Microsoft Embedded Partner¿ qualification and privileged relations with other Italian companies such as Kontron Italia, RaFi Elettronica, Sistemi Avanzati Elettronici.

entityDescription: The Geological Survey of Denmark and Greenland, GEUS, is a research and advisory institute in the Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities. The survey also operates in the private sector. Mission and functions GEUS' overall mission is to provide, to use, and to disseminate knowledge of geological materials, processes and relations that is important for the use and protection of geological resources in Denmark and Greenland. Part of this mission is to support administrative and legislative work in Danish Ministries and the Government of Greenland Authority, by providing state-of-the-art geoscientific knowledge of international standard. GEUS' main tasks are geological mapping, data collection and storage, to carry out research projects, to give advice, and to disseminate geoscientific knowledge. The activities are organised within five programme areas: 1. Data banks, information technology, and information to the general public 2. Water resources 3. Energy resources 4. Mineral resources and Greenland mapping 5. Nature and climate GEUS co-operates with numerous scientific institutions and networks, and other organisations around the world, such as Danish and Greenland research institutions and agencies, EuroGeoSurveys (EGS), the Forum of European Geological Surveys (FOREGS), the European Environmental Agency (EEA), and the Far East CCOP (Co-ordinating Committee for Coastal and Offshore Geoscience Programmes in South-East-Asia).

We perform sustained research, and develop and implement leading edge technologies such as triple frequency RTK and PPP with reliable integer ambiguity resolution. Our partners and customers benefit from our capabilities in simulation, rapid prototyping, testing and implementation.

entityDescription:
The University of Extremadura (UEx) is a public higher education and research institution located in southwest Spain. It combines teaching excellence with a strong commitment to research, innovation, and knowledge transfer, acting as a key driver for regional development and international cooperation. UEx covers a wide range of scientific areas, including life sciences, agricultural and food technologies, engineering, health sciences, social sciences, and humanities, fostering interdisciplinary approaches to address global challenges.
The university’s research activity is organized around several research institutes and centres, as well as over 200 consolidated research groups. Its strategic priorities include sustainability, digital transformation, health and well-being, and agri-food innovation, with a particular emphasis on collaboration with European and international partners. UEx researchers actively participate in Horizon Europe, Interreg, and other international programmes, reinforcing the institution’s global outlook.
Knowledge transfer and collaboration with industry, public administrations, and civil society are also core elements of the university’s mission, supported by its Office for European and International Projects and its Technology Transfer Office. The university hosts around 22,000 students and 2,500 teaching and research staff, fostering a dynamic environment for training young researchers, PhD candidates, and postdoctoral fellows.
UEx is widely recognized as a reference institution in areas such as agri-food research, renewable energies, ICT, health, and social innovation, and it actively promotes cooperation across disciplines and borders. Its role in the proposal aligns with its experience in conducting high-quality research, supporting innovation, and ensuring the dissemination and exploitation of results to maximize scientific, economic, and social impact.
